===Kansas City Chiefs===
====2008 season====
The Kansas City Chiefs selected Carr in the fifth round (140th overall) of the [[2008 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/draft.htm |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Carr was the 23rd cornerback drafted and the second cornerback drafted by the Chiefs in 2008.<ref>{{cite web| title=Wrapping Up the Kansas City Chiefs 2008 Draft Class| url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2008/4/27/462009/draft-post| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=arrowheadpride.com| author=Thorman, Chris| date=April 28, 2008}}</ref> He also became the highest drafted player in Grand Valley State's school history. Carr was only the eighth player drafted from Grand Valley State and was the first player drafted from Grand Valley State since [[Keyonta Marshall]] was selected 247th overall in the [[2005 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web| title= Football database: Grand Valley State Draft History| url=https://www.footballdb.com/draft/college.html?c=Grand+Valley+State| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=footballdb.com}}</ref> During the draft, general manager [[Carl Peterson]] decided to allow head coach Herman Edwards to select their 140th overall pick as a gift for his 54th birthday which fell on the day of the draft. Edwards immediately responded, "I want Brandon Carr! I promise you this; By opening day, he'll be starting!"<ref name="Edwards">{{cite web| title=Carl Peterson Let Herm Edwards Pick Brandon Carr As A Birthday Present| url=https://arrowheadaddict.com/2012/06/05/carl-peterson-let-herm-edwards-pick-brandon-carr-as-a-birthday-present/| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=arrowheadaddict.com| author=Allen, Patrick| date=June 5, 2012}}</ref>

On June 11, 2008, Carr signed a three-year, $1.36 million rookie [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $145,629.<ref name=Chiefs1>{{cite press release|url=http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/2008/06/11/chiefs_agree_to_terms_with_cb_brandon_carr/|title=Chiefs Agree to Terms with CB Brandon Carr|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080613231707/http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/2008/06/11/chiefs_agree_to_terms_with_cb_brandon_carr/|archive-date=June 13, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=OvertheCap: Brandon Carr| url=https://overthecap.com/player/brandon-carr/606| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=overthecap.com}}</ref> Throughout training camp, he competed against [[Brandon Flowers (American football)|Brandon Flowers]] and [[Dimitri Patterson]] for a job as a starting cornerback.<ref>{{cite web| title=River Falls Recap - Friday, 7/25 AM Walkthru| url=https://247sports.com/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/Article/River-Falls-Recap-Friday-725-AM-Walkthru-104531805| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=247sports.com| date=July 25, 2008}}</ref> Head coach [[Herman Edwards]] named Carr the third cornerback and first-team nickelback to start the regular season, behind [[Patrick Surtain]] and Brandon Flowers.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 08/29/2008| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/29/KC| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Chiefs trim roster to 53 players| url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2008/8/30/604336/chiefs-to-trim-roster-to-5| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=arrowheadpride.com| author=Thorman, Chris| date=August 30, 2008}}</ref>

Carr made his NFL debut and first career start in the season-opener at the [[2008 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]] and recorded three combined tackles in the 17–10 loss. On September 21, 2008, Carr earned his first start as an outside cornerback after Patrick Surtain injured his shoulder the previous week against the [[2008 Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Edward shakes it up| url=http://www.newspressnow.com/news/edwards-shakes-it-up/article_04c00d8d-1d66-5c6f-9e6e-259fc6b27d9b.html| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=newspressnow.com| date=September 17, 2008}}</ref> He finished the Chiefs' 38–14 loss at the [[2008 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] with a season-high nine solo tackles. The following week, he made two solo tackles, three pass deflections, and made his first career interception off a pass by quarterback [[Jay Cutler]] during a 33–19 victory against the [[2008 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in Week 4.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 4-2008: Denver Broncos @ Kansas City Chiefs| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2008092803/2008/REG4/broncos@chiefs#tab=recap| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Carr finished his rookie year with 73 combined tackles (70 solo), six pass deflections, two interceptions, and two fumble recoveries in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (career)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/careerstats| access-date=May 11, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He started the first two games at nickelback and last 14 games at left cornerback.

====2009 season====
[[File:Brandon Carr.JPG|200px|thumb|left|Carr stretching in January 2010]]
On January 23, 2009, the  Chiefs fired head coach Herman Edwards after they finished with a 2–14 record in 2008.<ref>{{cite web| title=Chiefs decide three seasons are enough, fire head coach Herm Edwards| url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d80e4f977/article/chiefs-decide-three-seasons-are-enough-fire-head-coach-edwards| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171206165026/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d80e4f977/article/chiefs-decide-three-seasons-are-enough-fire-head-coach-edwards| url-status=dead| archive-date=December 6, 2017| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=NFL.com| date=January 23, 2009}}</ref> Carr and Flowers entered training camp slated as the starting cornerbacks under new defensive coordinator [[Clancy Pendergast]]. Carr saw minor competition for his role from [[Maurice Leggett]] and [[Ricardo Colclough]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Chiefs Wrap Up Day Two of Mandatory Mini-Camp| url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/platform/2009/6/7/901522/chiefs-wrap-up-day-two-of| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=arrowheadpride.com| author=Thorman, Joel| date=June 7, 2009}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Head coach [[Todd Haley]] officially named Carr and Flowers the starting cornerback duo to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 09/06/2009| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/40/KC| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

During Week 4, Carr collected four solo tackles and a season-high three pass deflections in a 27–16 loss to the [[2009 New York Giants season|New York Giants]]. During Week 11, he recorded a season-high eight solo tackles in a 27–24 victory over the [[2009 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2009)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2009| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

Carr finished his second professional season with 62 combined tackles (56 solo), 19 passes defensed, two tackles for loss, an interception, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2010 season====
Carr and Flowers were retained as the starting cornerbacks entering camp under new defensive coordinator [[Romeo Crennel]]. Head coach Todd Haley officially named them the starters to begin 2010.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 09/05/2010| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/111/KC| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

During Week 5, Carr recorded a season-high eight combined tackles and a pass deflection during a 19–9 loss at the [[2010 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref name="stats10"/> On December 12, 2010, he tied his season-high of eight combined tackles in the Chiefs' 31–0 loss at the [[2010 San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]] in Week 14.<ref name="stats10">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2010)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2010| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2010}} season with 57 combined tackles (46 solo), 25 pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

The Chiefs finished first atop the [[AFC West]] with a 10–6 record. On January 9, 2011, Carr started in his first NFL playoff game and made three solo tackles in a 30–7 loss to the [[2010 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] in the AFC Wildcard Game.<ref name="stats10"/>

====2011 season====
Carr and Flowers entered the 2011 season as the starting cornerbacks ahead of [[Javier Arenas (American football)|Javier Arenas]] and [[Jalil Brown]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 09/04/2011| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/123/KC| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=ourlads.com}}</ref>

During Week 8, Carr recorded a season-high six solo tackles in the Chiefs' 23–20 win against the [[2011 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]]. On December 11, 2011, he made one tackle and a season-high three pass deflections during a 37–10 loss at the [[2011 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] in Week 14. In the regular-season finale, Carr recorded two combined tackles, deflected two passes, and an interception in the Chiefs' 7–3 win at the [[2011 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]] in Week 17. He intercepted [[Tim Tebow]]'s pass that was intended for [[Eddie Royal]] and sealed the Chiefs' victory on the last defensive play in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 17-2012: Kansas City Chiefs @ Denver Broncos| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2012010113/2011/REG17/chiefs@broncos| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Carr finished the season with 45 combined tackles (39 solo), 15 passes defensed, and four interceptions in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/> During the season, Carr's averaged a 46% completion rate among opposing quarterbacks and gave up only three touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Carr and Dallas Cowboys Working Out A Deal|url=http://www.dallascowboys101.com/2012/03/14/brandon-carr-and-the-dallas-cowboys-working-out-a-deal/|access-date=February 27, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131228145420/http://www.dallascowboys101.com/2012/03/14/brandon-carr-and-the-dallas-cowboys-working-out-a-deal/|archive-date=December 28, 2013|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

====2012 season====
Carr became an [[unrestricted free agent]] after the 2011 season and was regarded by analysts as the top cornerback available in [[free agency (sports)|free agency]].<ref>{{cite web| title=2012 NFL free agent cornerbacks: Carr, Rogers, Finnegan form a solid top trio| url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/1568176-2012-nfl-free-agent-cornerbacks-brandon-carr-carlos-rogers-cortland-finnegan| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=sportingnews.com| author=Iyer, Vinnie| date=March 9, 2012| archive-date=May 13, 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513081039/http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/1568176-2012-nfl-free-agent-cornerbacks-brandon-carr-carlos-rogers-cortland-finnegan| url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 11, 2012, Carr attended a private meeting with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on the first day of free agency.<ref>{{cite web| title=Cowboys get their man, sign Brandon Carr| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/55288/cowboys-get-their-man-sign-brandon-carr| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=ESPN.com| date=March 14, 2012}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On March 14, 2012, the [[Dallas Cowboys]] signed Carr to a five-year, $50.1 million contract with $26.5 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $10 million.<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/03/14/cowboys-sign-brandon-carr-for-five-years-50-1-million/|title=Cowboys sign Brandon Carr for five years, $50.1 million|first=Evan|last=Silva|date=March 14, 2012|access-date=December 9, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4690885/brandon-carr-to-get-26-5-million-guaranteed|title=Brandon Carr to get $26.5M guaranteed|date=March 15, 2012|first=Calvin |last=Watkin|access-date=December 9, 2015}}</ref>

====2012 season====
Carr entered training camp slated as the Cowboys' No. 1 cornerback, replacing [[Terence Newman]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Dallas Cowboys News: Brandon Carr, Morris Claiborne Could Lead a Top Defensive Unit in 2012| url=https://www.ibtimes.com/dallas-cowboys-news-brandon-carr-morris-claiborne-could-lead-top-defensive-unit-2012-751084| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=ibtimes.com| date=August 20, 2012}}</ref> Head coach [[Jason Garrett]] officially named him the starter to begin the regular season, alongside rookie [[Morris Claiborne]] and ahead of [[Orlando Scandrick]] and [[Mike Jenkins (American football)|Mike Jenkins]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Dallas Cowboys 2012 Official 53-Man Roster, Depth Chart Finalized| url=http://www.rantsports.com/nfl/2012/09/01/dallas-cowboys-2012-official-53-man-roster-depth-chart-finalized/| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=rantsports.com| author=Griffin, Jericho| date=September 1, 2012| archive-date=June 14, 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614051646/http://www.rantsports.com/nfl/2012/09/01/dallas-cowboys-2012-official-53-man-roster-depth-chart-finalized/| url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 11, 2012, Carr recorded four solo tackles, a pass deflection, and returned an interception for his first NFL touchdown during a 38–23 victory at the [[2012 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 10. He intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Nick Foles]] in the fourth quarter and returned it for a 47-yard touchdown.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 10-2012: Dallas Cowboys @ Philadelphia Eagles| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2012111109/2012/REG10/cowboys@eagles| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> During Week 15, he made four solo tackles, a season-high three pass deflections, and made a key interception in overtime to help the Cowboys' defeat the [[2012 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] 27–24. His interception occurred off a pass by [[Ben Roethlisberger]] that was intended for [[Mike Wallace (American football)|Mike Wallace]] with 41 seconds remaining in overtime.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Pittsburgh Steelers @ Dallas Cowboys| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2012121611/2012/REG15/steelers@cowboys| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> The following week, Carr collected a season-high six combined tackles in the Cowboys' 34–31 loss to the [[2012 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]] in Week 16.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2012)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2012| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2012}} season with 53 combined tackles (48 solo), 11 pass deflections, and three interceptions in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

Carr led the team in interceptions and pass deflections in his first season with the Cowboys and started his 100th career game.

====2013 season====
Defensive coordinator [[Monte Kiffin]] retained Carr and Claiborne as the starting cornerbacks after [[Rob Ryan]] was fired after the 2012 season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Dallas Cowboys Roster 2013: Latest Cuts, Depth Charts and Analysis| url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1750511-dallas-cowboys-roster-2013-latest-cuts-depth-charts-and-analysis| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130828155349/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1750511-dallas-cowboys-roster-2013-latest-cuts-depth-charts-and-analysis| url-status=dead| archive-date=August 28, 2013| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=bleacherreport.com| author=Gagnon, Brad| date=August 23, 2008}}</ref> He started in the [[2013 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys']] season-opener against the [[2013 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] and recorded four solo tackles, broke up a pass, and returned an interception for a touchdown in a 36–31 victory. The interception occurred off a pass attempt by [[Eli Manning]] that was intended for running back [[Da'Rel Scott]] and returned it for a 49-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 1-2013: New York Giants @ Dallas Cowboys| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013090812/2013/REG1/giants@cowboys| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 8, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles and deflected a pass in a 31–30 loss at the [[2013 Detroit Lions|Detroit Lions]]. The following week, he made a season-high eight solo tackles and broke up a pass during a 27–23 win against the [[2013 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings]] in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2013)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2013| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Carr finished the season with 71 combined tackles (60 solo), 12 pass deflections, three interceptions, and a touchdown in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2014 season====
The Cowboys promoted [[Rod Marinelli]] to defensive coordinator and moved Kiffin to a defensive assistant role. Head coach Jason Garrett opted to retain Carr and Claiborne as the starting cornerbacks duo with Orlando Scandrick as their nickelback to begin the season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 09/01/2014| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/162/DAL| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On October 5, 2014, Carr collected a season-high eight combined tackles and deflected a pass in the Cowboys' 20–17 loss to the [[2014 Washington Redskins|Washington Redskins]] in Week 8.<ref name="stats14"/> In Week 10, he recorded five solo tackles and made his first career sack on [[Chad Henne]] during a 31–17 victory at the [[2014 Jacksonville Jaguars|Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref name="stats14"/>

Carr finished the 2014 season with 54 combined tackles (45 solo), seven pass deflections, and a sack in 16 games and starts. He was held without an interception for the first time in his first seven seasons.<ref name="career"/>

The Cowboys finished atop the [[NFC East]] with a 12–4 record. On January 4, 2015, Carr started in the NFC Wildcard Game and recorded six solo tackles and a pass deflection during the Cowboys' 24–20 win against the [[2014 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]].<ref name="stats14"/> The following week, he made three solo tackles as the Cowboys were eliminated from the playoffs after losing 26–21 at the [[2014 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] in the NFC Divisional Round.<ref name="stats14">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2014)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2014| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2015 season====
During Week 3, Carr recorded a season-high eight combined tackles during a 39–28 loss to the [[2015 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]]. Four weeks later, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles in a 27–20 loss at the [[2015 New York Giants season|New York Giants]]. In Week 14, he tied his season-high of eight combined tackles and deflected a pass in a 28–7 loss at the [[2015 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2015)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2015| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Carr finished the 2015 season with 76 combined tackles (60 solo) and six pass deflections in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/> He started his 148th consecutive game but was held without an interception for the second consecutive season.

====2016 season====
On April 25, 2016, it was reported that Carr agreed to a pay cut from $9.1 million to $4.25 million plus incentives, in order to remain with the Cowboys for the 2016 season.<ref>{{cite web| title=CB Brandon Carr Agrees To Pay Cut; Lowers Salary By More Than $3 Million| url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/04/25/cb-brandon-carr-agrees-pay-cut-lowers-salary-more-3-million| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513152423/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/04/25/cb-brandon-carr-agrees-pay-cut-lowers-salary-more-3-million| url-status=dead| archive-date=May 13, 2018| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=DallasCowboys.com| author=Eatman, Nick| date=April 25, 2016}}</ref>

Carr started in the season-opener against the [[2016 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] and made two solo tackles, a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Eli Manning]] to end his 36-game interception drought in the narrow 20–19 loss.<ref name="stats16"/> During Week 8, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles and broke up a pass in a 29–23 overtime victory over the [[2016 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref name="stats16"/> In Week 13, Carr made eight combined tackles in the Cowboys' 17–15 victory at the [[2016 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]].<ref name="stats16">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2016)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2016| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Carr finished the season with 61 combined tackles (53 solo), nine pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/> He had a career resurgence in 2016 after defensive coordinator Rod Marinelli moved him to play the right outside cornerback position, where Carr experienced success with during his first four years in Kansas City.<ref>{{cite web| title=Why Brandon Carr Is The Most Important Free Agent The Cowboys Should Re-sign| url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/platform/2017/3/10/14879086/why-brandon-carr-is-the-most-important-free-agent-the-dallas-cowboys-should-re-sign-morris-claiborne| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=bloggingtheboys.com| date=March 10, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Carr an overall grade of 75.3, which ranked as the 52nd highest grade among the 116 qualifying cornerbacks in 2016.

The Cowboys finished atop the NFC East with a 13–3 record. On January 15, 2017, Carr made three solo tackles as the Cowboys lost 34–31 to the [[2016 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] in the NFC Divisional Round.<ref name="stats16"/>

====2017 season====
Carr became an unrestricted free agent in 2017 and was regarded as one of the top five cornerbacks available in free agency. He received interest from the [[New York Jets]] and Baltimore Ravens after not receiving an offer to return to the Dallas Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web| title=Report: Jets Have Interest in Free Agent Cornerback Brandon Carr| url=https://www.ganggreennation.com/platform/2017/3/12/14899126/report-jets-have-interest-in-free-agent-cornerback-brandon-carr| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=ganggreennation.com| date=March 12, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On March 16, 2017, the [[Baltimore Ravens]] signed Carr to a four-year, $23.50 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $4 million. The contract also includes an opt-out clause for the Ravens in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Reach Four-Year Agreement With Cornerback Brandon Carr|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Reach-Four-Year-Agreement-With-Cornerback-Brandon-Carr/caed16e2-eeb1-421b-b6ca-e1f94292e1d7|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228041216/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Reach-Four-Year-Agreement-With-Cornerback-Brandon-Carr/caed16e2-eeb1-421b-b6ca-e1f94292e1d7|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 28, 2018|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=March 16, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens bring in Brandon Carr on four-year deal|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-bring-in-brandon-carr-on-four-year-deal-0ap3000000793518|author=Sessler, Marc|website=NFL.com|date=March 16, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Brandon Carr contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/baltimore-ravens/brandon-carr-4372/| access-date=May 12, 2018| website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

====2017 season====
Head coach [[John Harbaugh]] officially named Carr a starting cornerback, along with [[Jimmy Smith (cornerback)|Jimmy Smith]], to start the regular season.

Carr started in the season-opener at the [[2017 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] and recorded two solo tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Andy Dalton]] during the first quarter of a 20–0 shutout victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100cin.htm|title=Baltimore Ravens at Cincinnati Bengals - September 10th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=October 6, 2017}}</ref> In the next game, Carr recorded a season-high four pass deflections, three solo tackles, and intercepted a pass by [[DeShone Kizer]] in the fourth quarter of the Ravens' 24–10 victory over the [[2017 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170rav.htm|title=Cleveland Browns at Baltimore Ravens - September 17th, 2017|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |access-date=October 28, 2017}}</ref> During Week 8, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles as the Ravens routed the [[2017 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] 40–0. In Week 15, he made four solo tackles, a pass deflection, and an interception during a 27–10 road victory over the Browns.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Brandon Carr (2017)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandoncarr/4365/gamelogs?season=2017| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Carr finished the 2017 season with 56 combined tackles (50 solo), 12 pass deflections, and tied his career-high with four interceptions in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career"/> He extended his consecutive start streak to 160 games. [[Pro Football Focus]] gave him an overall grade of 74.1, which ranked 69th among all qualifying cornerbacks in 2017.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Brandon Carr (2017)| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/brandon-carr/4454| access-date=May 13, 2018| website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2018 season====
On March 13, 2018, the Ravens exercised the second-year option on Carr's four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Ravens exercise CB Brandon Carr's option |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2018/03/ravens-exercise-cb-brandon-carrs-option |access-date=May 13, 2018 |website=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref> Carr once again started all 16 games in 2018, extending his consecutive start streak, recording 45 combined tackles, 11 passes defensed, and two interceptions. He finished tied for the team-lead in interceptions and second in passes defensed.

====2019 season====
Through the 2019 season, Carr was second among all NFL players in consecutive games started (192), behind only Chargers quarterback [[Philip Rivers]] (218 games) and ahead of Kansas City Chiefs offensive tackle [[Mitchell Schwartz]] (122).<ref name="autogenerated3">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/chiefs/gameday/mitchell-schwartz-snap-streak-ends |title=Mitch Schwartz's Consecutive-Snap Streak Comes to an End|author= Matt Derrick|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=January 12, 2020 |access-date=January 18, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/here-s-a-look-at-the-chiefs-records-and-milestones-from-the-2019-regular-season|author= Matt McMullen |title=Here's a Look at the Chiefs' Records and Milestones from the 2019 Regular Season |publisher=Chiefs.com |date= January 3, 2020|access-date=January 18, 2020}}</ref> He appeared in 16 with 16 starts at both right cornerback and free safety, while making 49 tackles, 2 sacks and 6 passes defensed.

On March 18, 2020, the Ravens declined the option on Carr's contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens decline DB Brandon Carr's contract option|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28922709/ravens-decline-db-brandon-carr-contract-option|author=Hensley, Jamison|website=ESPN.com|date=March 18, 2020}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys (second stint)===
On September 6, 2020, Carr was signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Carr Among 15 Practice Squad Additions|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/brandon-carr-among-15-practice-squad-additions|author=Phillips, Rob|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster six days later for the season opener against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], and was reverted to the practice squad on September 14.<ref>{{cite news |author=Drummond, K. D. |title=Cowboys promote DB Brandon Carr to active roster from PS |url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/12/dallas-cowboys-brandon-carr-activation-roster-practice-squad/ |website=USAToday.com |date=September 12, 2020 |access-date=September 29, 2020}}</ref> Carr was promoted to the active roster the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Carr, LB, OT Signed To Roster; 3 To IR|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/brandon-carr-lb-ot-signed-to-roster-3-to-ir|author=Phillips, Rob|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 15, 2020}}</ref> He appeared in three games as a reserve player and had one tackle. Carr was released on October 6.<ref>{{cite news |author=Gehlken, Michael |title=Cowboys release DB Brandon Carr to end brief, second stint in Dallas |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/cowboys/2020/10/06/cowboys-release-db-brandon-carr-to-end-brief-second-stint/ |website=DallasNews.com |date=October 6, 2020 |access-date=October 26, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In December 2012, Carr launched the Carr Cares Foundation. The foundation focuses on educational enrichment and physical fitness for youth. Influenced by Carr's passion for literacy and his love of sports, the foundation provides students in Dallas, Baltimore, and Flint, Michigan with opportunities to practice and perfect their literacy and athletic skills.<ref>{{cite news |author=Kramer, Claire |title=Brandon Carr: The Reason For It All |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/brandon-carr-the-reason-for-it-all |website=Baltimoreravens.com |date=February 1, 2019 |access-date=December 26, 2022}}</ref>

'''Brandon Lewis Gibson''' (born August 13, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington State Cougars]] and was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the sixth round of the [[2009 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[St. Louis Rams]] and [[Miami Dolphins]].

==Early life==
{{Unreferenced section|date=August 2025}}
Gibson grew up in [[Puyallup, Washington]] and went to Stahl Jr High School then graduated from [[Governor John R. Rogers High School]] in 2005.

==College career==
Gibson finished his college career at [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State]] as the school's all-time leading receiver with 2,756 yards and 182 receptions<ref name="Draft">{{cite web |author=Kent, Bob |title=WR Gibson Thankful For Opportunity |url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=17731 |publisher=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=April 26, 2009 |access-date=2009-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090701092434/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=17731 |archive-date=July 1, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> along with 17 touchdowns. He also played for the Washington State basketball team during the 2005-06 season, but decided to focus his attention on football.

In 2007, as a junior, Gibson started 11 games and was named to Phil Steele's Third-team All-America. Also, he was voted First-team All-Pac-10 honors. He set the WSU single-season record for receiving yards in a season with 1,180 on 67 receptions. He also led the team with nine touchdowns, a tie for third most touchdowns in a single season by a WSU Cougar. In 2006, he played in 12 games with no starts. He led the Cougars with 731 yards and was second on the squad in both receptions (49) and touchdowns (four). As a freshman, he earned a varsity letter after playing in 10 of the Cougars' 11 games during his debut season. Gibson ended the season with 9 catches for 172 yards (19.2 yard average) and 2 touchdowns.

Gibson seriously considered leaving Washington State to declare for the [[2008 NFL draft]] due to the team switching coaches, however, the new coaching staff convinced him to stay.<ref name="Draft"/>

As a senior in 2008, Gibson earned the fourth varsity letter of his career after starting in each of WSU's 13 games. He was named honorable mention All-Pacific-10 Conference and the team Offensive Most Valuable Player. In 2008, he caught 57 passes for 673 yards and two touchdowns. After the season, he received an invitation to play in the [[Senior Bowl]].

==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
Gibson pulled his hamstring during the [[2009 Senior Bowl]] in [[Mobile, Alabama]].<ref name="Draft"/>

===St. Louis Rams===
Gibson was traded from Philadelphia to the [[St. Louis Rams]] on October 20, 2009 along with a fifth round draft pick in 2010 in exchange for [[linebacker]] [[Will Witherspoon]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Wulf, Bo |title=Eagles Snag LB Witherspoon |url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=19132 |publisher=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=October 20, 2009 |access-date=2009-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091225014124/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=19132 |archive-date=December 25, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In his Ram debut, on November 15, 2009, he caught 7 passes for 93 yards, both Ram records for a rookie playing in his first game. The 93 yards was the most by any Ram receiver in 2009. His seven receptions in the game was also remarkable, as only teammate [[Danny Amendola]] had achieved that many receptions in a single game that season.

'''Brandon Scott Carter''' (born September 10, 1986)  is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]]. He was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2010. After football he signed to [[WWE]], where he worked in their [[Farm team|developmental territory]] [[NXT Wrestling]] under the name '''TAC'''.

==Early life==
Carter was born in [[Lakewood Township, New Jersey]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Brandon Carter New Orleans Saints | url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/roster/brandon-carter/8cc695e8-9d3a-4e09-81c4-006d1a382f18/ |work=New Orleans Saints |date=January 26, 2011 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405134925/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/roster/Brandon-Carter/8cc695e8-9d3a-4e09-81c4-006d1a382f18 |archivedate=April 5, 2017 |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He attended [[Spring Hill High School (Texas)|Spring Hill High School]] in [[Longview, Texas]], he played nose guard and [[defensive tackle]] until his senior season, when he broke his hand, causing him to play on the [[offensive line]].<ref name=122908DMN>{{cite news|publisher=The Dallas Morning News|title=Texas Tech guard's game face a real hit}}</ref>

As a junior, he received district defensive MVP and honorable-mention All-state honors. As a senior, he received Class 3A All-State first-team honors.

In [[track and field]] he competed in the [[shot put]], finishing third in the state as a senior.

==College career==
Carter accepted a football scholarship from [[Texas Tech University]]. As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman in 2006, he played in 12 games mainly on [[special teams]]. He had one start against [[Iowa State University]].

As a sophomore in 2007, he started all 13 games. As a junior in 2008, he was a starter at guard and allowed only one sack. He contributed to the team having an 11–2 record.<ref name=122908DMN/>

As a senior in 2009, Carter was listed at No. 15 on ''[[Rivals.com]]′s'' preseason offensive tackle power ranking.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Buchanan |first1=Olin |last2=Dienhart |first2=Tom |last3=Fox |first3=David |last4=Huguenin |first4=Mike |last5=Megargee |first5=Steve |date=August 22, 2009 |title=Preseason offensive tackle power rankings |work=Rivals.com |url=http://rivals100.rivals.com/content.asp?cid=978914 |access-date=September 1, 2009 |archive-date=March 24, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324093700/http://rivals100.rivals.com/content.asp?cid=978914 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also named to the 2009 [[Outland Trophy]] watch list.<ref name="FWAA Outland">{{Cite web |last=Richardson |first=Steve |date=August 11, 2009 |title=2009 Outland Trophy Watch List Announced |publisher=[[Football Writers Association of America]] |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2009/outland090811.html }}</ref> On September 27, 2009, Carter was suspended indefinitely for violating team rules.<ref>{{cite news|last=Griffin|first=Tim|title=Tech's Carter violates team rules|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=2009-09-27|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=4510370|access-date=2009-09-28}}</ref> He was reinstated on October 4, after missing only a single game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.redraiders.com/2009/10/04/carter-returns-to-tech-practice/|title=Carter reinstated, Potts doubtful for Saturday|last=Williams|first=Don|work=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|accessdate=2009-10-06|date=2009-10-04|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091008071414/http://www.redraiders.com/2009/10/04/carter-returns-to-tech-practice/|archivedate=2009-10-08}}</ref>

He is remembered for his intense personality, multi-colored [[Mohawk hairstyle|mohawk]], and wrestling style face paint while at Texas Tech.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/article.aspx?subjectid=216&articleid=20081209_216_B1_ALLYOU256510|title=College football season taught us many life lessons}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/sioncampus/12/10/the-college-football-oscars-campus-clicks/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622095449/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/sioncampus/12/10/the-college-football-oscars-campus-clicks/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 22, 2011|title=Campus Clicks | work=CNN | date=December 10, 2008 | accessdate=April 26, 2010}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Saints===
Carter was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[New Orleans Saints]] on April 26, 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/saints-announce-2010-rookie-free-agent-class-2248765 |title=Saints Announce 2010 Rookie Free Agent Class | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was waived from the team on September 4 and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/saints-reduce-roster-to-53-active-players-2749092 |title=Saints Reduce Roster To 53 Active Players | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was released by the Saints on September 15.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/saints-sign-cb-torrence-waive-lb-asiodu-make-pair-of-practice-squad-move-2784412 |title=Saints sign CB Torrence, waive LB Asiodu; make pair of practice squad moves | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On September 14, 2010, he was signed to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/talib-activated-2780125 |title=Talib Activated | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 30.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/moore-to-ir-piscitelli-released-in-flurry-of-moves-3097023 |title=Moore to IR, Piscitelli Released in Flurry of Moves | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He was waived/injured on August 29, 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-trim-roster-to-80-5624944 |title=Bucs Trim Roster to 80 | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On December 27, 2011, he was signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/offensive-tackle-joining-practice-squad-323281|title=Offensive Tackle Joining Practice Squad | accessdate=June 14, 2020}}</ref> He wasn't re-signed after the season.

==Professional wrestling==
Carter signed a developmental deal with the [[WWE]] in 2012 and would report to their developmental territory NXT Wrestling, where he was known as TAC.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2012/08/former-texas-tech-offensive-lineman-brandon-carter-signs-with-wwe.html/|title=SportsDayDFW}}</ref> On January 14, 2013, Carter was released from his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pwinsider.com/article/74720/another-wwe-release.html?p=1|title=Another WWE Release}}</ref>

Bryant was rated as a three-star recruit by ''247sports.com'',{{Cite web|url = https://247sports.com/Player/Brandon-Bryant-31127|title = Brandon Bryant|date = |accessdate = August 26, 2016|website = 247sports.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} ''Rivals.com'',{{Cite web|url = https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/13721|title = Brandon Bryant|date = |accessdate = August 26, 2016|website = Rivals.com|publisher = Yahoo|last = |first = }} ''Scout.com'',{{Cite web|url = http://www.scout.com/player/177323-brandon-bryant|title = Brandon Bryant|date = |accessdate = August 26, 2016|website = Scout.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} and [[ESPN]].{{Cite web|url = https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/179990/brandon-bryant|title = Brandon Bryant|date = |access-date = August 26, 2016|website = ESPN.com|publisher = ESPN|last = |first = }} He committed to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]] on November 4, 2013.{{Cite web|url = http://djournal.com/inside-msu-sports/2013/11/04/bryant-commits-bulldogs/|title = Bryant commits to the Bulldogs|date = June 28, 2013|accessdate = November 4, 2013|website = DJournal.com|publisher = |last = Lowery|first = Logan}} ==College career== ===Freshman season (2015)=== After sitting out the [[2014 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|2014 season]] as a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]], Bryant saw action in all 13 games in [[2015 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|2015]], starting in eight of them. Bryant was a backup safety for the first five games of the season before taking over starting duties in a 45–17 win over [[2015 Troy Trojans football team|Troy]], a game where he forced a fumble on Troy's first drive.{{Cite web|url = https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400603900|title = Mississippi State beats Troy 45-17|date = October 10, 2015|access-date = August 26, 2016|website = ESPN.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} The following week against [[2015 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|Louisiana Tech]], Bryant recorded his first collegiate [[interception]] and returned it for a touchdown{{Cite web|url = https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400603895|title = Prescott leads Mississippi State over Louisiana Tech 45-20|date = October 17, 2016|access-date = August 26, 2016|website = ESPN.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} and also recovered a blocked punt. Later that season, on an [[SEC Network]] broadcast, [[Tim Tebow]] named Bryant the "Freak of Week," citing Bryant's ability to run a [[40-yard dash]] in 4.24 seconds and to [[deadlift]] 600 pounds.{{Cite web|url = http://www.secsports.com/video/14126682/brandon-bryant|title = Tebow's Freak of the Week: Brandon Bryant|date = |accessdate = August 26, 2016|website = ESPN.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} Bryant caught another interception in a loss to Alabama.{{Cite web|url = http://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2015/11/19/msus-bryant-showing-nose-ball-starter/76050220/|title = MSU's Bryant showing a nose for the ball as a starter|date = November 19, 2015|accessdate = August 26, 2016|website = ClarionLedger.com|publisher = The Clarion-Ledger|last = Bonner|first = Michael}} ===Sophomore season (2016)=== Bryant was named by ''[[The Clarion-Ledger]]'' as the Bulldogs' second-most important player in 2016.{{Cite web|url = http://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2016/07/07/most-important-bulldogs-no-2-brandon-bryant/86798254/|title = No. 2: Brandon Bryant|date = July 7, 2016|accessdate = August 26, 2016|website = ClarionLedger.com|publisher = The Clarion-Ledger|last = Bonner|first = Michael}} He was called the "top playmaker" on the team and the backbone of the Bulldog defense. Bryant had an interception against [[2016 Samford Bulldogs football team|Samford]]. ===Junior season (2017)=== Bryant again played in all 13 games in the Bulldogs' [[2017 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|2017 season]], bringing down an interception against in a win over [[2017 BYU Cougars football team|BYU]]. ==Professional career== ===New York Jets=== After failing to be drafted in the 2018 supplemental NFL draft, Bryant signed with the [[New York Jets]] as an undrafted free agent on July 16, 2018.{{cite web|title=Jets Sign S Brandon Bryant, Waive WR Devin Smith|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-s-brandon-bryant-waive-wr-devin-smith|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=July 16, 2018}} He was waived on September 1, 2018, and was signed to the practice squad the next day.{{cite web|title=Final Cutdown: Jets Reach 53-Player Active Roster|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/final-cutdown-jets-reach-53-player-active-roster|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 1, 2018}}{{cite web|title=Jets Sign Four Players to Their Practice Squad|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-four-players-to-their-practice-squad|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 2, 2018}} He was promoted to the active roster on December 29, 2018.{{cite web|title=Jets Place CB Morris Claiborne, WR Quincy Enunwa and LB Kevin Pierre-Louis on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-cb-morris-claiborne-wr-quincy-enunwa-and-lb-kevin-pierre-louis-on-inj|first1=Eric|last1=Allen|first2=Ethan|last2=Greenberg|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 29, 2018}} He was waived/injured on August 29, 2019,{{cite news |title=Jets' Brandon Bryant: Waived/injured by Jets |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jets-brandon-bryant-waivedinjured-by-jets/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=August 29, 2019 |accessdate=August 30, 2019}} and placed on the team's [[injured reserve]] list the next day. He was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on September 10. ===Hamilton Tiger-Cats=== Bryant signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the CFL on April 16, 2020.{{cite news |title=Tiger-Cats sign linebacker Bryant |url=https://ticats.ca/article/tiger-cats-sign-linebacker-bryant |website=TiCats.ca |date=April 16, 2020 |accessdate=April 17, 2020}} He retired from football on June 28, 2021.{{cite news |title=Tiger-Cats add three players on defence |url=https://ticats.ca/article/tiger-cats-add-three-players-on-defence |website=TiCats.ca |date=June 28, 2021 |access-date=June 28, 2021}} ==References== {{Reflist|3}} ==External links== *[http://hailstate.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4120 Mississippi State Bulldogs football bio] {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bryant, Brandon}} [[Category:1995 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Players of American football from Mississippi]] [[Category:American football defensive backs]] [[Category:People from Tunica, Mississippi]] [[Category:Sportspeople from the Memphis metropolitan area]] [[Category:Mississippi State Bulldogs football players]] [[Category:New York Jets players]] [[Category:Hamilton Tiger-Cats players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]]

'''Brandon Ghee''' (born June 6, 1987) is a former professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the third round (96th overall) of the [[2010 NFL draft]], and also played for the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest]].

==Early life==
Ghee attended [[Jack Britt High School]] in [[Fayetteville, North Carolina]], where he was named all-state as a cornerback and all-region as a [[wide receiver]]. He also helped Jack Britt to the state championship game and scored two touchdowns in that contest.

Considered a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Ghee was listed as the No. 28 cornerback prospect in the nation in 2005.<ref>{{Citation |date=January 20, 2005 |title=Rivals.com Cornerbacks 2005 |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=882 }}</ref> He chose Wake Forest over offers from [[Clemson University|Clemson]], [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|North Carolina]], [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]] and [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University|Virginia Tech]].

==College career==
Ghee [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his initial season at Wake Forest, and did not participate in any team activities the following season because of academic reasons.

In 2007, he started each of the final 10 games and ranked fourth on the squad with 56 tackles. He also had 10 pass breakups, the second-most on the team.

As a redshirt junior in 2008, Ghee played in 11 games and finished second in the ACC in fumbles forced with four.

==Professional career==

===Cincinnati Bengals (first stint)===
Ghee was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the third round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] with the 96th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a wrist injury on August 24, 2012.<ref>[http://www.profootballweekly.com/2012/08/24/bengals-place-five-on-ir Bengals place five on I.R.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120827234313/http://www.profootballweekly.com/2012/08/24/bengals-place-five-on-ir |date=August 27, 2012 }}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
He signed a two-year deal with the [[San Diego Chargers]] on March 13, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.chargers.com/news/article-1/Chargers-Add-to-Secondary-with-CB-Brandon-Ghee/ab0aa66a-12b9-4ad4-a0b1-b0e2ab3a6834 |title=Chargers Add to Secondary with CB Brandon Ghee |access-date=2014-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140417191837/http://www.chargers.com/news/article-1/Chargers-Add-to-Secondary-with-CB-Brandon-Ghee/ab0aa66a-12b9-4ad4-a0b1-b0e2ab3a6834 |archive-date=2014-04-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
Ghee signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] on October 8, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Alper|first1=Josh|title=Titans place Bernard Pollard on IR, sign Brandon Ghee|date=8 October 2014 |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/10/08/titans-place-bernard-pollard-on-ir-sign-brandon-ghee/|publisher=Pro Football Talk|accessdate=10 October 2014}}</ref> He was waived on December 3, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign CB Jemea Thomas; Waive CB Brandon Ghee|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-1/Titans-Sign-CB-Jemea-Thomas-Waive-CB-Brandon-Ghee/163a2751-8b87-49f3-9921-d258a7de6037|publisher=Titans Online|accessdate=4 December 2014}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals (second stint)===
Ghee signed with the Bengals on March 19, 2015. He was released by the Bengals on September 5, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/afcnorth/post/_/id/85552/cincinnati-bengals-cut-21-players-put-vontaze-burfict-on-pup |title=Cincinnati Bengals cut 21 players, put Vontaze Burfict on PUP |last=Harvey |first=Coley |date=September 5, 2015 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=September 22, 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His brother, Patrick Ghee, played [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] at Wake Forest from 2002 to 2006.

'''Brandon Anderson''' (born December 10, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2009. He played [[college football]] for the [[Akron Zips football|Akron Zips]].

Anderson was also a member of the [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
Anderson attended [[Pulaski County High School (Virginia)|Pulaski County High School]] in [[Dublin, Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.southwesttimes.com/2009/05/archive-3475/ |title=Former Pulaski Cougars player signs with NFL's Colts |year=2009 |publisher=The Southwest Times |work=www.southwesttimes.com |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref> While at Pulaski, Anderson played football, [[basketball]] and ran [[track & field]]. As a member of the football team, Anderson played both [[running back]] and defensive back.

After Pulaski, Anderson attended [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in [[Chatham, Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hargravesports.com/sports/2011/5/11/PGFB_0511115311.aspx?path=pgfootball |title=NFL Alumni |publisher=Hargrave Military Academy |work=www.hargravesports.com |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://nyg.scout.com/a.z?s=64&p=8&c=2&nid=10639&yr=2004 |title=2004 Hargrave Military Academy Football Roster |publisher=Microsoft |work=www.scout.com |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref>

Anderson chose to attend the [[University of Akron]], accepting a football scholarship from the Zips on December 26, 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Brandon-Anderson-33690;_ylt=AmPhIbFO6TMPZGB3EDmEQpxDPZB4 |title=Brandon Anderson |publisher=Yahoo! |work=www.rivals.com |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref> Anderson also received scholarship offers from [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]] and [[UCF Knights football|Central Florida]].

==College career==
In 2005 as a freshman, Anderson recorded 22 tackles and one interception playing as a special teams player and reserve [[defensive back]]<ref name="espn college stats">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/12954/type/college/brandon-anderson |title=Brandon Anderson college stats |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref> In 2006, he returned 11 kickoffs for 157 yards with a long of 28 yards. Recorded 27 tackles and one interception. He also forced a fumble.<ref name="espn college stats" /> He recorded 17 tackles and one sack in 2007. His senior year, he returned one kickoff for 17 yards. Had a career high 42 tackles and had one interception.
During his college career, he recorded 108 tackles, 1 sack, 1 forced fumble, and 3 interceptions.<ref name="espn college stats" />

==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
Prior to the [[2009 NFL draft]], Anderson was projected to be undrafted by NFLDraftScout.com. He was rated as the 79th-best cornerback in the draft. Anderson averaged 4.42 on his 40-yard dash, but ran a 4.34 on his fastest attempt.<ref name="NFLDraftScout">{{cite web |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=56423&draftyear=2009&genpos=CB |title=Brandon Anderson, DS #79 CD, Akron |publisher=The Sports Xchange |work=www.nfldraftscout.com |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref> He was not invited to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]], he posted the following numbers during his Akron pro-day workouts:

===Indianapolis Colts===
Anderson signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] after going undrafted.

===Cleveland Browns===
Anderson was a practice squad member of the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 2009.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
Anderson signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in 2009. After a season on the practice squad, the Buccaneers dressed Anderson for 3 games in 2009, where he did not record any statistics.

===San Jose SaberCats===
In January 2012, Anderson signed with the [[San Jose SaberCats]] of the [[Arena Football League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4341723 |title=SaberCats Add Former Tampa Bay Buccaneers Defensive Back Brandon Anderson |date=January 12, 2012 |publisher=OurSports Central |work=www.oursportscentral.com |access-date=June 14, 2013}}</ref>

===Chicago Rush===
Anderson was assigned to the [[Chicago Rush]] for the 2013 season, but was placed on recallable reassignment by the Rush before the season began.

===Cleveland Gladiators===
Two days after the Rush placed Anderson on recallable reassignment, he was claimed by the [[Cleveland Gladiators]]. Anderson played the 2013 season with the Gladiators. He was reassigned on November 21, 2013.

Anderson now lives at home with his parents and works with youth of Pulaski County in Virginia.

'''Brandon DeSean Banks''' (born December 21, 1987) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]] and [[return specialist]]. He was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2010. He also played in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] and [[Toronto Argonauts]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Bakersfield College]] and for the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]]. Banks was the lightest active player in the NFL and CFL when he played at 150 pounds.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2010/10/about_brandon_bankss_size.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130220014721/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2010/10/about_brandon_bankss_size.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 20, 2013|title=About Brandon Banks's size| last=Steinberg|first=Dan|date=October 6, 2010|access-date=2012-08-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Banks |url=https://www.cfl.ca/players/brandon-banks/152593/ |publisher=CFL.ca |access-date=9 December 2014 }}</ref> He was inducted into the [[Canadian Football Hall of Fame]] in 2026.

==Early life==
Banks was a four-year starter and two-time all-conference selection at [[Garner Magnet High School]] in [[Garner, North Carolina]]. He led the Trojans to three consecutive conferences championships and a 33–5 record over his final three seasons. In 2017, he was inducted into the school Hall of Fame.

===Track and field===
Banks was named to the 2006 ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA high school track and field team after posting a 10.42 in the [[100-meter]] and a 21.44 in the [[200-meter]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=400&ATCLID=1523653 |title=Kansas State Official Athletic Site - Kansas State University |website=www.kstatesports.com |access-date=26 January 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120906235528/http://www.kstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=400&ATCLID=1523653 |archive-date=6 September 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==

===Junior college===
As a [[Bakersfield College]] Renegade, Banks earned first-team All-America honors from JC Gridwire as an all-purpose player/wide receiver. He was also named a ''PrepStar'' JUCO All-American. He helped lead Bakersfield to a No. 1 national ranking, a 12–1 record on the season and a berth in the Southern California championship game.  His 15 touchdowns set a school record.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Banks No. 83 |url=http://www.kstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=3062&SPID=212&DB_OEM_ID=400&ATCLID=1523653&Q_SEASON=2008 |publisher=Kansas State Athletics |access-date=2010-02-27 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213155455/http://www.kstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=3062&SPID=212&DB_OEM_ID=400&ATCLID=1523653&Q_SEASON=2008 |archive-date=February 13, 2009 }}</ref>

===Kansas State===
Banks transferred to [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]] to begin the [[2008 Kansas State Wildcats football team|2008 season]].

Banks became the second straight Wildcat to earn offensive newcomer of the year accolades after [[Deon Murphy]] took the honor in 2007. In all, Kansas State has had eight players earn conference newcomer of the year honors since 1996.

He had one of the best seasons in school history for a junior wide receiver after collecting 67 receptions for 1,049 yards and nine touchdowns. He became the sixth player in school history to reach 1,000 receiving yards in a season and his 67 catches and 1,049 receiving yards were the most by a Wildcat junior for a single season.

Banks also contributed on special teams in 2008 as he collected 498 yards on 18 kickoff returns and five punt returns for 58 yards. His 98-yard kickoff return against Nebraska tied for the fifth-longest in school history. Banks' 1,731 total all-purpose yardage in 2008 ranks fifth in single-season school history, while his 144.2 all-purpose yards per game mark checks in at No. 8 on the Kansas State single-season records chart. He was a first team Big 12 Conference selection on special teams and he was a second team All-American his senior year.

===Washington Redskins===
After the [[2010 NFL draft]], the [[Washington Redskins]] signed Banks as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 17, 2010.<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/2010/05/17/1951735/brandon-banks-signs-with-redskins.html Brandon Banks signs with Redskins], ''Kansas City Star'', May 17, 2010.</ref> He returned a punt 77 yards for a touchdown in the first preseason game against the [[2010 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] on August 13, and was shortly thereafter given the nickname, "Crazy Legs Banks".<ref name=excite>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121007100749/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/redskinsinsider/-the-washington-redskins-hoped.html Brandon Banks puts excitement back in the return game], ''The Washington Post'', September 2, 2010.</ref> Against the [[2010 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], however, he fumbled a return and had inconsistent play against the [[2010 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], which included a second lost fumble.<ref name=excite/> The Redskins released Banks on September 26, but re-signed him to the [[practice squad]] on September 29. In his first regular season NFL game, Banks returned his first punt 51 yards against the [[2010 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] which set up a Redskin touchdown. In Week 5 against the [[2010 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], his responsibilities expanded to include both punt and kick return duties. Banks recorded three punt returns for 47 yards and two kickoff returns for 33 yards, while a 62-yard kickoff return was negated by a holding penalty.<ref>[http://blog.redskins.com/2010/10/10/brandon-banks-is-growing-his-skillset/ Brandon Banks Is Growing His Skillset], Washington Redskins, October 10, 2010.</ref> In Week 6 against the [[2010 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Banks blocked a 48-yard [[Field goal (American and Canadian football)|field goal]] attempt by [[Adam Vinatieri]].<ref>[http://blog.redskins.com/2010/10/18/brandon-banks-blocks-a-kick-maybe/ Brandon Banks Blocks A Kick (Maybe)], Washington Redskins, October 17, 2010.</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nfl/playbyplay?gameId=301017028&period=0 Colts 27, Redskins 24: Play-By-Play], ESPN, October 17, 2010.</ref> On October 31 against the Lions, Banks totaled 271 return yards, setting a franchise record. His 96-yard kickoff return midway through the fourth quarter was the Redskins' first kick return for a touchdown in 70 games, and the first of Banks' career.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20101103231323/http://www.redskins.com/gen/articles/Banks_Breaks_Loose_In_a_Big_Way_168448.jsp Banks Breaks Loose In a Big Way], Washington Redskins, November 1, 2010.</ref> In Week 12, Banks ran a 77-yard punt return in a home game against the [[2010 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] for a touchdown to give the Redskins a lead late in the game, but a penalty called on [[Perry Riley]] negated the return and the Redskins lost.<ref>{{cite news| work=WashingtonPost.com | url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/redskinsinsider/brandon-banks/mike-shanahan-stands-behind-pe.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018065908/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/redskinsinsider/brandon-banks/mike-shanahan-stands-behind-pe.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=October 18, 2013 | title=Mike Shanahan stands behind Perry Riley | last=Reid | first=Jason | date=November 29, 2010 | access-date=2012-05-23}}</ref>

Starting the [[2011 NFL season|2011 season]] off slow, Banks would finally have an impressive 55-yard punt return before being pushed out of bounds in the second game against the [[2011 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{cite news | work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/post/brandon-banks-finally-breaks-one-loose/2011/11/20/gIQArS09fN_blog.html| last=Maese|first=Rick| title=Brandon Banks finally breaks one loose|date=November 20, 2011| access-date=2012-05-23}}</ref>
In Week 14 against the [[2011 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]], [[Rex Grossman]] gave the ball to [[Roy Helu]], who then gave it to Banks; Banks then threw a 49-yard touchdown pass to [[Santana Moss]].<ref>{{cite news| work=WashingtonTimes.com | url=http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2011/dec/11/redskins-vs-patriots-quarter-quarter-breakdown-gam/ | title=Redskins vs. Patriots: Quarter-by-quarter breakdown, game's key play | access-date=2011-12-11}}</ref> The pass was the first of Banks' career.
Later in Week 16 against the [[2011 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], Banks took a reverse handoff for a 59-yard touchdown run, but just like his punt return touchdown in the previous meeting between the two teams in the 2010 season, it was nullified by a penalty on [[Darrel Young]].<ref>{{cite news| work=WashingtonPost.com| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/dc-sports-bog/post/redskins-vikings-best-and-worst/2011/12/24/gIQAOqX2FP_blog.html | title=Redskins-Vikings best and worst| last=Steinberg|first=Dan|date=December 24, 2011| access-date=2012-05-23}}</ref> On the next play, [[Rex Grossman]] threw an interception and the [[2011 Washington Redskins season|Redskins]] went on to lose the game.<ref>{{cite news |work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/two-plays-seal-the-fate-of-the-redskins/2011/12/24/gIQAXfUGGP_story.html| title=Redskins loss to Vikings sealed by two key plays | last=Svrluga|first=Barry| date=December 24, 2011|access-date=2012-05-23}}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
Banks signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] on September 30, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/10/29/brandon-banks-making-his-presence-felt-with-cfls-tiger-cats/|title=Brandon Banks quickly makes impact for CFL's Tiger-Cats|first=Mike|last=Wilkening|date=October 29, 2013|access-date=2013-11-10}}</ref> He played in the final 4 regular season games of the [[2013 CFL season]] with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was named the Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 18 of the 2013 CFL season for returning a missed field goal for the game-winning touchdown to clinch home-field advantage in the Eastern Semi-finals. In  his second season in the league Banks returned two punts for touchdowns in the Tiger-Cats's 40-24 win over the [[Montreal Alouettes]] in the Eastern Final, advancing the Tiger-Cats to the [[102nd Grey Cup]]. An additional punt return was called back because of a penalty.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Allen |first=Scott |date=November 24, 2014 |title=Former Redskins return man Brandon Banks leads Hamilton to Grey Cup with two punt return TDs |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/dc-sports-bog/wp/2014/11/24/former-redskins-return-man-brandon-banks-leads-hamilton-to-grey-cup-with-two-punt-return-tds/ |access-date=November 24, 2014 |work=Washington Post}}</ref> In the [[102nd Grey Cup]], Banks recorded a 45-yard receiving touchdown, while an apparent punt return touchdown with under a minute left in the game was called back due to an illegal block.<ref>{{cite news |last=Mingo |first=Rita |url=https://calgaryherald.com/sports/football/cfl/grey-cup-2014/stamps-beat-ticats-20-16-to-claim-102nd-grey-cup |title=Stamps beat Ticats 20-16 to claim 102nd Grey Cup |work=Calgary Herald |date=2014-11-30 |access-date=2014-11-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cfl.ca/statistics/statsGame/id/12827 |title=Play by Play |publisher=cfl.ca |access-date=December 1, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141201183748/https://cfl.ca/statistics/statsGame/id/12827 |archive-date=December 1, 2014 }}</ref> He recorded 1,968 combined yards during the regular season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/cfl/cfl-east-final-ticats-banks-could-be-difference-vs-als-1.2841758 | title=CFL East Final: Ticats' Banks could be difference vs. Als | publisher=cbc.ca | date=November 20, 2014 | access-date=November 23, 2014}}</ref> His performance earned him his first CFL All-Star award.

[[File:16, Brandon Banks, June 22, 2019.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Banks before a Tiger-Cats game in 2019.]]
Banks saw a reduced workload in the receiving game in his third season in the CFL, despite playing in all 18 regular season games. He caught 22 passes for 220 yards, but carried the ball a career-high 20 times for 87 yards. He set personal bests across the board in both punt and kick return. In total he touched the ball 164 times (average of 9.1 times a game) for 2,070 yards with six touchdowns. He was named a CFL All-Star for the second consecutive season.

Banks played in the first 15 games of the [[2016 CFL season|2016 regular season]] before being suspended for two of the final three games of the year: He tested positive for a banned substance ([[Methylenedioxyamphetamine]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2016/10/19/ticats-brandon-banks-suspended-for-two-games-for-violating-drug-policy/|title=Ticats' Brandon Banks suspended for two games for violating drug policy|date=2016-10-19|website=CFL.ca|access-date=2016-10-19}}</ref> Banks finished the season having amassed 2,082 kickoff return yards and scoring three return touchdowns. He was the East division nomination for Special Teams Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thescore.com/cfl/news/1117202|title=Mitchell, Jackson announced as Most Outstanding Player nominees|newspaper=theScore.com|access-date=2016-11-10}}</ref>

Banks had a breakout season as a wide receiver in [[2017 CFL season|2017]], setting new career highs in receptions (67) yards (1,011) and touchdowns (8). For the first eight games of the season under head coach [[Kent Austin]] Banks only caught eight passes for 52 yards, however under new head coach [[June Jones]] Banks' involvement and productivity skyrocketed.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ralph |first=Dan |date=2017-10-24 |title=Brandon Banks excelling as receiver with Ticats under head coach Jones |url=https://nationalpost.com/pmn/sports-pmn/football-sports-pmn/cfl-football-sports-pmn/brandon-banks-excelling-as-receiver-with-ticats-under-head-coach-jones |access-date=2018-09-27 |work=National Post |language=en-US}}</ref> In the final 10 games of the season Banks caught 59 passes for 959 yards with eight touchdowns. Banks improved on his strong 2017 season, with an even more productive 2018 season; catching setting new career highs in receptions (94) yards (1,423) and touchdowns (11). He suffered a broken clavicle in the team's Week 19 loss to the [[Ottawa Redblacks]], causing him to miss the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/10/19/ticats-banks-sidelined-upper-body-injury/|title=Banks out for season with broken clavicle - CFL.ca|date=2018-10-19|work=CFL.ca|access-date=2018-10-22|language=en-US}}</ref> At the time of the injury Banks was second in the league in receptions and yards, and tied for first with teammate [[Luke Tasker]] for most receiving touchdowns. On January 28, 2019 Banks and the Tiger-Cats agreed to a two-year contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2019/01/26/report-ticats-sign-star-receiver-banks-two-year-deal/|title=Report: Ticats bring back Banks on two-year deal|date=2019-01-26|website=CFL.ca|language=en|access-date=2019-01-28}}</ref> Banks continued his excellent play into the [[2019 CFL season|2019 season]] where in the penultimate game of the season he set the franchise record for most receptions in a season with 112.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/dane-evans-brandon-banks-have-career-days-to-lead-hamilton-tiger-cats-past-montreal-alouettes-1.1387730|title=Dane Evans, Brandon Banks have career-days to lead Hamilton Tiger-Cats past Montreal Alouettes - TSN.ca|agency=The Canadian Press|date=2019-10-26|website=TSN|language=en|access-date=2019-10-26}}</ref> Banks was also named to his 6th consecutive Divisional All-Star list.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.cfl.ca/2019/11/06/2019-cfl-division-stars-announced/| title = 2019 CFL Division All-Stars Announced - CFL.ca| date = 6 November 2019}}</ref>  Banks was later named the [[CFL's Most Outstanding Player Award|CFL's Most Outstanding Player]] for his play in the 2019 season.<ref>{{cite web | title=Speedy MOP: Banks takes home Most Outstanding Player | website=CFL.ca | date=2019-11-22 | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2019/11/21/speedy-mop-banks-takes-home-outstanding-player/ | access-date=2025-07-06}}</ref> He re-signed with the Tiger-Cats on December 31, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=CFL's reigning Most Outstanding Player Banks re-signs with Tiger-Cats |url=https://ticats.ca/article/cfls-reigning-most-outstanding-player-banks-re-signs-with-tiger-cats |website=TiCats.ca |date=December 31, 2020 |access-date=December 31, 2020}}</ref> The [[2020 CFL season|2020 season]] was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada|COVID-19 pandemic]]. Banks played in the first four games of the [[2021 CFL season|2021 season]] catching 22 passes for 172 yards before suffering a rib injury.<ref>{{cite news|date=2021-09-10|title=Opinion {{!}} Brandon Banks' rib injury forces him out of Friday's Labour Day rematch in Toronto|language=en|work=The Hamilton Spectator|url=https://www.thespec.com/sports/ticats/opinion/2021/09/10/brandon-banks-rib-injury-forces-him-out-of-fridays-labour-day-rematch-in-toronto.html|access-date=2021-10-22|issn=1189-9417}}</ref> The injury caused him to miss the next three games, before briefly returning to action in Week 9, and then also missing Week 10 due to lingering pain.<ref>{{Cite web|agency=The Canadian Press|date=2021-10-20|title=Brandon Banks Hamilton Tiger-Cats first team practice - TSN.ca|url=https://www.tsn.ca/brandon-banks-hamilton-tiger-cats-first-team-practice-1.1709005|access-date=2021-10-22|website=TSN|language=en}}</ref> He became a free agent upon the expiry of his contract on February 8, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2022/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 13, 2022}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On February 13, 2022, it was announced that Banks had signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]]. He won his first ever Grey Cup with the Argonauts in Regina, Saskatchewan on November 20, the [[109th Grey Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2022/02/13/argos-add-2019-mop-brandon-banks/ |title=Argos add 2019 MOP Brandon Banks |publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] |date=February 13, 2022}}</ref> After one season with the club Banks was released by the Argos on January 3, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-03 |title=Argos Parting Ways With WR Brandon Banks |url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2023/01/03/argos-parting-ways-with-wr-brandon-banks/ |access-date=2023-01-03 |website=Toronto Argonauts |language=en}}</ref>

On June 4, 2026, before the Tiger-Cats' home opener, Banks signed a ceremonial one-day contract to retire as a member of the team.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2026/06/04/receiver-brandon-banks-signs-one-day-contract-to-retire-with-hamilton/ | title=Receiver Brandon Banks signs one-day contract | publisher=[[CFL.ca]] | date=June 4, 2026 | accessdate=5 June 2026}}</ref> During halftime of the game, he was announced as an inductee into the [[Canadian Football Hall of Fame]] as part of the class of 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2026/06/04/brandon-banks-to-be-inducted-into-cfhof-and-museums-class-of-2026/ | title=Brandon Banks to be inducted into CFHOF and Museum’s Class of 2026 | publisher=[[CFL.ca]] | date=June 4, 2026 | accessdate=5 June 2026}}</ref>
