'''Brandon Augustus Deaderick''' (born August 19, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the seventh round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]].

==Early life==
Deaderick attended [[Elizabethtown High School]] in [[Elizabethtown, Kentucky]]. As a junior, he had 95 tackles and 22 sacks, earning all-state honors. As a senior, he missed four games to injury but averaged ten tackles per game and recorded seven sacks on the season. He also led EHS to their first state championship game in 24 years.

==College career==
Following high school, Deaderick attended the [[University of Alabama]], where he [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed in his first season with the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Crimson Tide]] in 2005. As a freshman in 2006, Deaderick played in seven games, finishing with two tackles. In 2007, Deaderick appeared in all 13 games and made seven starts, recording 22 tackles and two sacks. As a junior in 2008, he started 14 games at defensive end and finished the season with 36 tackles and four sacks.

In 2009, Deaderick was shot in the forearm during a robbery attempt he witnessed the week before the [[Chick-fil-A Kickoff Game]].<ref name="September 1, 2009">{{Cite news |last=Kausler Jr. |first=Don |date=September 1, 2009 |title=Tide defensive end Brandon Deaderick not injured seriously in shooting |work=[[The Birmingham News]]}}</ref> He wasn't seriously injured in the incident, he would be medically cleared to play later in the week and subsequently play in the 2009 opener.<ref name="September 4, 2009">{{Cite news |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=September 4, 2009 |title=Alabama's Brandon Deaderick gets medical OK to play again |work=[[The Birmingham News]]}}</ref> Alabama finished the [[2009 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|2009 season]] 14–0 beating Texas 37–21 in the [[2010 BCS National Championship]] game. He finished his senior season with 23 tackles and one sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 Alabama Crimson Tide - Brandon Deaderick #95 - Tackles Game Log - through 01/07/2010 |url=http://www.cfbstats.com/2009/player/8/1000078/tackle/gamelog.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220602172702/http://www.cfbstats.com/2009/player/8/1000078/tackle/gamelog.html |archive-date=June 2, 2022 |website=cfbstats.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===New England Patriots===
Deaderick was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the seventh round (247th overall) of the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed a four-year contract on July 9, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Christopher |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Patriots sign Deaderick |url=http://itiswhatitis.weei.com/sports/newengland/football/patriots/2010/07/09/report-patriots-sign-deaderick/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100713151652/http://itiswhatitis.weei.com/sports/newengland/football/patriots/2010/07/09/report-patriots-sign-deaderick/ |archive-date=July 13, 2010 |access-date=July 14, 2010 |website=[[WEEI (AM)|WEEI]]}}</ref> As a rookie, Deaderick received his first career start in Week 6 against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], recording his first career sack. He went on to start three of the next four games for the Patriots, but was a healthy inactive for the team's [[NFL on Thanksgiving Day|Thanksgiving game]] in Week 12 against the [[Detroit Lions]]. After playing in the next three games as a reserve, Deaderick missed the team's Week 16 game with an injury but was a healthy scratch for the regular season finale. He finished the regular season with 10 tackles and 2.0 sacks in 10 games played (four starts). On January 3, 2011, during the Patriots' [[2010–11 NFL playoffs|playoffs]] bye week, Deaderick was suspended by the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=January 3, 2011 |title=Source: Brandon Deaderick suspended |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/news/story?id=5985992 |access-date=January 4, 2011 |website=ESPNBoston.com}}</ref> His suspension was lifted on January 7, 2011.

Deaderick played 10 games in the 2011 regular season with 17 tackles and 2 sacks. He also started in [[Super Bowl XLVI]], where the Patriots eventually lost to the [[New York Giants]] 21–17.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLVI - New York Giants vs. New England Patriots - February 5th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201202050nwe.htm |access-date=December 6, 2017 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Deaderick played 14 games in the 2012 regular season with 18 tackles, 1 sack, and 2 forced fumbles. He was released by the Patriots on May 13, 2013.<ref name="NERel">{{Cite news |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=May 13, 2013 |title=New England Patriots release former Alabama DT Brandon Deaderick |url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2013/05/new_england_patriots_release_f.html |access-date=May 14, 2013 |publisher=AL.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Deaderick was claimed off waivers by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on May 14, 2013.<ref name="JAXclaim">{{Cite news |last=Champlin |first=Drew |date=May 14, 2013 |title=Former Alabama DL Brandon Deaderick claimed off waivers by Jacksonville Jaguars |url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2013/05/former_alabama_dl_brandon_dead.html |access-date=May 15, 2013 |publisher=AL.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on December 23, 2013.<ref name="u372">{{cite web | last=Gantt | first=Darin | title=Jaguars bring Kyle Love in again, Brandon Deaderick on IR | website=NBC Sports | date=2013-12-23 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/jaguars-bring-kyle-love-in-again-brandon-deaderick-on-ir | access-date=2025-01-13}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On June 3, 2014, he signed a one-year contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 3, 2014 |title=New Orleans Saints sign C Jonathan Goodwin, DL Brandon Deaderick to one-year contracts |url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-sign-C-Jonathan-Goodwin-DL-Brandon-Deaderick-to-one-year-contracts/86048fd3-c010-4cef-a4a8-2afc69efbd6e |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606071819/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-sign-C-Jonathan-Goodwin-DL-Brandon-Deaderick-to-one-year-contracts/86048fd3-c010-4cef-a4a8-2afc69efbd6e |archive-date=June 6, 2014 |access-date=June 3, 2014 |website=New Orleans Saints}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
Deadrick signed with the [[Houston Texans]] in June 2015 but was cut from training camp on September 4, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodbery  |first=Evan |date=2015-06-03 |title=Former New Orleans Saints DT Brandon Deaderick signs with Houston Texans |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/former-new-orleans-saints-dt-brandon-deaderick-signs-with-houston-texans/article_98805dc6-fcd2-5407-989c-df7c9ff9289a.html |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
On August 15, 2016, Deaderick was signed by the Bills.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Zac |date=August 16, 2016 |title=Bills cut Hankerson, add two defensive linemen |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bills-cut-hankerson-add-two-defensive-linemen |access-date=October 2, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> On September 2, 2016, he was released by the Bills as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=September 2, 2016 |title=Vets Felton and Lawson headline Bills cut to 53 |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/vets-felton-and-lawson-headline-bills-cut-to-53-17612870 |access-date=October 2, 2023 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

'''Brandon Bolden''' (born January 26, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]]. He was signed as an undrafted free agent in 2012 by the [[New England Patriots]], where he played nine non-consecutive seasons.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{Cite web |title=#34 Brandon Bolden Biography |url=http://www.olemisssports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bolden_brandon00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229023508/http://www.olemisssports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bolden_brandon00.html |archive-date=December 29, 2010 |access-date=October 21, 2010 |website=Ole Miss Rebels Athletics}}</ref> Primarily utilized as a [[American football positions#Special teams|special teams]] player, Bolden was a member of two [[Super Bowl]]-winning teams with New England. In between his two Patriots stints, he played for the [[Miami Dolphins]] in 2018. Bolden left the Patriots a second time to join the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] in 2022.

==Early life==
Bolden attended [[Scotlandville Magnet High School]] in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Underhill |first=Nick |date=February 9, 2015 |title=Patriots' Brandon Bolden following in footsteps of grandfather, former Chiefs player Frank Pitts |url=http://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/saints/article_7fd53f11-0957-56ed-a73e-261920d9dc97.html |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=The Advocate |language=en}}</ref> As a senior, Bolden rushed for 886 yards and 12 touchdowns en route to being named First-team All-District 5-5A. He also caught 12 passes for 256 yards. SuperPrep named him SuperPrep All-Region and ranked him the No. 34 best player in [[Louisiana]]. Bolden was named the No. 93 best running back in the nation by Scout.com. He was heavily recruited by [[Les Miles]] and [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]], but ultimately decided to play for [[Houston Nutt]] at [[Ole Miss]].<ref name="autogenerated1" />

==College career==
Although fellow running back Enrique Davis was more regarded as a recruit,{{Citation needed|date=February 2017}} by his sophomore year, Bolden had gained the starting role for the Rebels. In the 2009 season, he finished with 129 carries for 614 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandon-bolden-1/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2010 season, Bolden averaged nearly six yards a carry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandon-bolden-1/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Against [[2011 BYU Cougars football team|BYU]] in the first game of the 2011 season, Bolden suffered a broken ankle. Although the fracture was a minor one and he only missed a few games, he never returned to his previous form. He finished the 2011 season with 96 carries for 472 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandon-bolden-1/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was not selected in the [[2012 NFL draft]], although some sites predicted he might be drafted in one of the later rounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 21, 2006 |title=Brandon Bolden {{pipe}} Mississippi, RB : 2012 NFL Draft Scout Player Profile |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=81978&draftyear=2012&genpos=RB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425083610/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=81978&draftyear=2012&genpos=RB |archive-date=April 25, 2016 |access-date=September 18, 2016 |website=NfldraftScout.com}}</ref> Although [[Bleacher Report]] reported on April 30, 2012, that he had agreed to a free agent contract with the [[Washington Redskins]], Bolden later tweeted that the report was false. On May 2, 2012, a ''[[The New York Times|New York Times]]'' blog reported that he had signed a free agent deal with the [[New England Patriots]].

During the 2012 preseason, Bolden had 36 carries for 128 yards and caught four passes, but [[fumbled]] the ball twice, losing one. Nevertheless, at the end of training camp, the Patriots elected to keep Bolden on their 53-man roster, rather than try to place him on their [[practice squad]]. He scored his first touchdown in the Patriots' Week 3 loss to the [[Baltimore Ravens]];<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Baltimore Ravens – September 23rd, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209230rav.htm |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> in Week 4, against the [[Buffalo Bills]], he led the Patriots with 137 yards on 16 carries—an average of 8.6 yards per carry. He scored one touchdown and added an 11-yard reception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills – September 30th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209300buf.htm |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He and [[Stevan Ridley]], who had 106 yards on 22 carries with two touchdowns, became the first Patriots running backs to accrue 100 rushing yards in the same game since 1982. Moreover, [[Wes Welker]] and [[Rob Gronkowski]] had 100-yard games that day as well, making the four only the second such quartet of two 100-yard rushers and two 100-yard receivers in a single game for the same team. For his efforts, Bolden was named the NFL's FedEx Ground Player of the Week for Week 4.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2015 |title=FedEx Players Air and Ground |url=http://www.nfl.com/voting/players-air-and-ground/2012/reg/4 |access-date=September 18, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On November 9, 2012, Bolden was suspended four games for violating the NFL's policy on performance-enhancing substances.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 9, 2012 |title=Patriots rookie RB Bolden suspended four games |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/patriots-rookie-running-back-brandon-bolden-suspended-four-223306230--nfl.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110003428/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/patriots-rookie-running-back-brandon-bolden-suspended-four-223306230--nfl.html |archive-date=November 10, 2012 |access-date=November 9, 2012 |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2012 season with 56 carries for 274 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Bolden was active for 12 of the Patriots' games during the 2013 season and finished the year with 271 rushing yards, three rushing touchdowns and 4.9 yards per carry; he also had 152 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=April 2, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the game, he played only on special teams as the Patriots defeated the [[Atlanta Falcons]] by a score of 34–28 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LI – New England Patriots vs. Atlanta Falcons – February 5th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201702050atl.htm |access-date=September 2, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> The Patriots trailed 28–3 in the third quarter, but rallied to win the game, 34–28, in the first overtime game in Super Bowl history and the largest comeback in Super Bowl history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Rich |date=January 1, 2017 |title=Which Pats could be playing their last regular season game for New England? |url=https://www.patspulpit.com/2017/1/1/14139480/which-patriots-could-be-playing-their-last-regular-season-game-for-new-england |access-date=February 11, 2017 |website=Pats Pulpit|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=February 5, 2017 |title=New England Patriots win Super Bowl LI |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-erase-deficit-defeat-falcons-in-super-bowl-li-0ap3000000783692 |access-date=February 5, 2017 |website=NFL.com |publisher=NFL}}</ref>

On April 5, 2017, Bolden re-signed with the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2017 |title=Patriots re-sign RB Brandon Bolden |url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/04/05/patriots-re-sign-rb-brandon-bolden |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406081752/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/04/05/patriots-re-sign-rb-brandon-bolden |archive-date=April 6, 2017 |access-date=April 5, 2017 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> On September 2, 2017, he was released by the Patriots, but was re-signed two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Patriots reach 53-man limit |url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/09/02/patriots-reach-53-man-limit |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171128033226/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/09/02/patriots-reach-53-man-limit |archive-date=November 28, 2017 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2017 |title=Patriots Re-Sign RB Brandon Bolden; Place LB Shea McClellin on Injured Reserve; Make Changes to the Practice Squad |url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/09/04/patriots-re-sign-rb-brandon-bolden-place-lb-shea-mcclellin-injured-reserve-make |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905022936/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/09/04/patriots-re-sign-rb-brandon-bolden-place-lb-shea-mcclellin-injured-reserve-make |archive-date=September 5, 2017 |access-date=September 5, 2017 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> As in 2016, he saw little action as a running back. In the first half of 2017, he saw no carries from the backfield, but served extensively on [[special teams]], serving as a [[Gunner (American football)|gunner]] opposite [[Matthew Slater]]. Bolden recorded six special teams tackles through Week 9 of 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=March 6, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On February 24, 2018, Bolden signed a one-year contract extension with the Patriots through the 2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=February 24, 2018 |title=Patriots bring back RB Brandon Bolden for 2018 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/patriots-bring-back-rb-brandon-bolden-for-2018-0ap3000000917442 |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=February 24, 2018 |title=Patriots retain core special teamer Brandon Bolden on one-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4811742/patriots-retain-core-special-teamer-brandon-bolden-on-1-year-deal |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On September 1, Bolden was released by the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Patriots Announce Roster Cutdown |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-cutdown-to-53-man-roster |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

=== Miami Dolphins ===
On September 4, 2018, Bolden signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2018 |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-3 |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> He mainly played on special teams and recorded 91 rushing yards (54 of which came on one play, which was a career long, against the Patriots in the [[Miracle in Miami]] game), two rushing touchdowns, and a receiving touchdown on the 2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=March 6, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New England Patriots (second stint)===
[[File:Brandon Bolden 2019.jpg|thumb|Bolden in a game against the [[Washington Redskins]] in 2019]]
On March 13, 2019, Bolden signed a two-year contract with the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |date=March 13, 2019 |title=Patriots Rumors: Brandon Bolden Agrees to 2-Year Contract to Return to NE |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2825414-patriots-rumors-brandon-bolden-agrees-to-2-year-contract-to-return-to-ne |access-date=March 13, 2019 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> Overall, in the 2019 season, Bolden recorded 15 carries for 68 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns to go along with nine receptions for 111 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On July 28, 2020, Bolden announced his decision to opt out of the [[2020 NFL season|2020 season]], due to concerns over the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 28, 2020 |title=Patriots re-sign wide receiver Will Hastings |work=Patriots.com |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-re-sign-wide-receiver-will-hastings |access-date=July 29, 2020}}</ref>

In 2021, Bolden had a career-high 405 receiving yards on 41 receptions as the Patriots primary third-down back, along with 44 carries for 226 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

=== Las Vegas Raiders ===
On March 16, 2022, Bolden signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2022 |title=Raiders sign RB Brandon Bolden |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-rb-brandon-bolden-nfl-free-agency-2022-offseason |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref> He appeared in 16 of the 17 regular season games in 2022 and mainly contributed on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

In Week 15, against the Los Angeles Chargers, Bolden scored a 26-yard rushing touchdown on just his second carry of the 2023 season.<ref name="f360">{{cite web | last=Trezevant | first=Ezekiel | title=Raiders Leaning on Running Back Depth | website=SI.com | date=2023-12-20 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/raiders/news/las-vegas-raiders-josh-jacobs-brandon-bolden-zamir-white-ameer-abdullah | access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he appeared in 17 games in mainly a special teams role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Bolden 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoldBr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brandon and his wife Arianna have three children together. Their son Brycen was born in May 2011, their daughter Axelle-Masai was born in March 2017, and their youngest daughter Aviana was born in February 2019. The couple was married in June 2014, having been together since 2008 when they both attended [[Scotlandville Magnet High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Getting to know Brandon Bolden ... again |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/getting-to-know-brandon-bolden-again |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

Bolden's grandfather, [[Frank Pitts]], was a [[wide receiver]] who played for the Oakland Raiders in 1974.  Pitts played for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in [[Super Bowl I]] and [[Super Bowl IV]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=September 22, 2012 |title=Football journey: Brandon Bolden |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4730511/football-journey-brandon-bolden |access-date=September 22, 2012 |website=Patriots Blog |publisher=ESPN Boston}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2009 |title=Around The Web: Replacing TG, Krumrie Runs, Chiefs Bloodlines In SEC |url=http://www.kcchiefsblog.com/tony-gonzalez/around-the-web-replacing-tg-krumrie-runs-chiefs-bloodlines-in-sec |url-status=dead |access-date=September 22, 2012 |website=KC Chiefs Blog}}</ref> In 2021, Bolden changed his jersey number from 38 to 25 so Pitts could see his grandson playing in his number.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fiske |first=Angelique |date=June 10, 2021 |title=Brandon Bolden shares the sentimental reason for changing his jersey number |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/brandon-bolden-shares-the-sentimental-reason-for-changing-his-jersey-number |access-date=June 10, 2021 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

On December 31, 2021, Bolden revealed that he had suffered from cancer in 2018. He was diagnosed with [[epidermoid carcinoma]], a form of skin cancer, following the Patriots' loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in [[Super Bowl LII]] and temporarily lost function of the right side of his face. He since underwent surgery and is cancer-free.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Tyler |date=December 31, 2021 |title=Patriots' Brandon Bolden reveals he battled cancer in 2018, didn't think he'd play in NFL again |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/patriots-brandon-bolden-reveals-he-battled-cancer-in-2018-didnt-think-hed-play-in-nfl-again/ |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

Offensive line analyst | statlabel1 = Games played | statvalue1 = 90 | statlabel2 = Games started | statvalue2 = 87 | pfr = FuscBr00 }} '''Brandon Fusco''' (born July 26, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the sixth round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania]].{{cite web |url=http://www.dailynorseman.com/2011/4/30/2145651/minnesota-vikings-select-slippery-rock-center-brandon-fusco|title=Minnesota Vikings Select Slippery Rock Center Brandon Fusco|date=April 30, 2011 |publisher=Daily Norseman|accessdate=April 30, 2011}} He currently serves as an offensive line analyst at [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]]. ==Early life== Fusco attended [[Seneca Valley School District#Seneca Valley Senior High School|Seneca Valley Senior High School]] in [[Harmony, Pennsylvania]], where he played [[offensive tackle]]. He did not play football until his junior year at Seneca Valley, stating "Sophomore year, didn't really do nothing and football just kind of came to my attention. I always watched it on TV and I sometimes got into a ticked off mood so I wanted to get out on the field and take my frustrations out on people." Despite performing for a team that won just one of eighteen contests during his two varsity seasons, Fusco earned All-WPIAL Class AAA-1 and honorable mention Quad North All-Star honors. Fusco was also an honor roll student. Fusco was not heavily recruited out of high school, mainly due to his lack of prep school experience and his 6–4, 240 lbs frame. He was only offered a chance to play football at small college schools, [[Youngstown State University|Youngstown State]] and [[Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania|Slippery Rock]] being the leading candidates. He eventually chose to enroll at Slippery Rock, stating that he felt very connected with the coaching staff. ==College career== After enrolling at Slippery Rock in 2006, Fusco spent his freshman season as a [[Redshirt (college sports)|red shirt]] on the scout team, where he played [[offensive tackle]]. In 2007 spring drills, Fusco shifted to [[Center (American football)|center]]. As a sophomore, Fusco received All-American honorable mention, All Super Region I and All [[Pennsylvania State Athletic Conference]] first-team honors. He started all eleven games at center, delivering ten [[touchdown]]-resulting blocks for a unit that rushed for 29 scores. His efforts help Slippery Rock rank second in the conference with an average of 484.14 yards per game. Fusco received All-American, All-Region and All-[[Pennsylvania State Athletic Conference|PSAC]] first-team accolades as a junior. Named the team captain, he also received squad MVP honors. He led the PSAC Western Division with 98 knockdowns and eleven touchdown-resulting blocks, despite the team's lack of a strong aerial game that ranked 59th in the nation. It was his drive blocking skills that helped the team finish fifth nationally in rushing (239.54 ypg) and seventh in total offense (456.69 ypg). He became the 19th player in school history to garner All-American first-team honors more than once in a career, as the 2010 [[Gene Upshaw Award]] winner and team captain captured All-PSAC honors for the third consecutive year. '''Brandon Jake Bair'''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://goducks.com/sports/football/roster/brandon-bair/3513 |title=Brandon Bair - Football - University of Oregon Athletics |website=goducks.com |access-date=May 9, 2021}}</ref> (born November 24, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). ==College career==
Bair played for the [[Oregon Ducks football|Ducks]] at the [[University of Oregon]] from 2007 to 2010. He was a backup his first two seasons and a starter for the final two. He finished his college career with totals of 106 tackles, five sacks, 12 pass breakups, one forced  fumble, and one fumble recovery.

'''Brandon Boykin''' (born July 13, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] and was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the fourth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Baltimore Ravens]].

==Early life==
Boykin attended [[Fayette County High School (Georgia)]] and played for the varsity football team. In his senior year, he, along with fellow NFL Player [[Matt Daniels]], led the football team into its first undefeated season in over 20 years but lost in the second round of the GHSA playoff. Boykin also played for the school's basketball team where he averaged 18 points and five assists per game while helping lead his team to the State Championship game where he and his team came up short.

==College career==
Boykin attended the [[University of Georgia]] from 2008 to 2011. He finished his career with 159 tackles, nine [[interceptions]] and a [[Quarterback sack|sack]]. As a senior, he was named the MVP of the [[2012 Outback Bowl]] after tackling [[Keshawn Martin]] for a safety, and returning a punt 92 yards for a touchdown in a 33–30 triple overtime loss to the [[Michigan State Spartans]].  Boykin also won the [[Paul Hornung Award]].<ref name="a462">{{cite web | last=Ching | first=David | title=Brandon Boykin grabs Outback Bowl MVP honors | website=ESPN.com | date=2012-01-03 | url=https://insider.espn.com/colleges/georgia/football/story/_/id/7416479/georgia-bulldogs-cornerback-brandon-boykin-outback-bowl-mvp | access-date=2024-10-27}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/colleges/georgia/football/story/_/id/7442603/georgia-bulldogs-brandon-boykin-wins-paul-hornung-award-most-versatile Brandon Boykin claims Hornung Award]</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
[[File:Brandon Boykin 111812-F-FF749-509 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Boykin in 2012 with the Eagles.]]
Boykin was selected in the fourth round (123rd overall) of the [[2012 NFL draft]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed a four-year contract with the team on May 11, 2012. His first season he recorded 31 total tackles, 7 passes defended, and 1 forced fumble. He saw little playing action on defense, but his 1,037 kick return yards were second in the NFC and seventh in the NFL.

Boykin started the 2013 season with his first interception, off [[Washington Redskins|Redskins]] [[quarterback]] [[Robert Griffin III]], helping the Eagles to win 33–27. He recorded his next interception in a week 5 win over the [[New York Giants|Giants]] where he picked off [[Eli Manning]]. In a week 10 game against the [[Green Bay Packers]] who were without quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]], Boykin intercepted quarterback [[Scott Tolzien]]'s pass in the [[endzone]] and ran it back for 76 yards. He followed up again the next week, intercepting Redskins quarterback Robert Griffin III. In a week 16 game against the [[Chicago Bears]], Boykin intercepted [[Jay Cutler]] and ran it back 54 yards for the score. The week 17 showdown against division rival [[Dallas Cowboys]] was for the [[NFC East]] division title. Late in the fourth quarter the Cowboys marched down the field when back-up quarterback [[Kyle Orton]] threw behind his [[wide receiver]], [[Miles Austin]]. Boykin intercepted the pass and kneed it after a short return.<ref name="cbssports interception">{{cite web | url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20131229_PHI@DAL/eagles-beat-cowboys-to-take-nfc-east-title | title=Eagles beat Cowboys to take NFC East title | publisher=CBSSports.com | date=December 29, 2013 | access-date=December 30, 2013}}</ref><ref name="thelandryhat interception">{{cite web | url=http://thelandryhat.com/2013/12/29/postgame-recap-eagles-24-cowboys-22/ | title=Postgame Recap: Eagles 24, Cowboys 22 | publisher=TheLandryHat.com | date=December 29, 2013 | access-date=December 30, 2013 | author=Lane, Mark}}</ref> The interception led to the Eagles rushing the ball twice for a first down, then two kneel downs to run out the clock and seal the Eagles' divisional win at a final score of 24–22.<ref name="cbssports interception" /><ref name="thelandryhat interception" /> Boykin enjoyed a breakout year in 2013 with 42 solo tackles, 5 assists, 2 forced fumbles, 16 passes defended, and 6 interceptions (second in the NFL). For the 2014 season, Boykin had 36 solo tackles, 5 assists, 9 passes defended, and an interception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Boykin 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoykBr00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On August 1, 2015, Boykin was traded to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in exchange for a conditional 2016 5th-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Eagles trade CB Brandon Boykin to Steelers|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/eagles-trade-cb-brandon-boykin-to-steelers-0ap3000000505792|work=NFL.com|access-date=August 2, 2015}}</ref>

=== Carolina Panthers ===
On March 28, 2016, Boykin signed a one-year contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000648373/article/panthers-sign-brandon-boykin-to-oneyear-deal?campaign=tw-nf-sf23267233-sf23267233 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328202450/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000648373/article/panthers-sign-brandon-boykin-to-oneyear-deal?campaign=tw-nf-sf23267233-sf23267233 | url-status=dead | archive-date=March 28, 2016 | title=Panthers sign Brandon Boykin to one-year deal | work=[[NFL.com]] | date=March 28, 2016 | access-date=March 28, 2016 | author=Sessler, Marc}}</ref> The Panthers released Boykin and two others to create roster space for six new rookie tryouts two months later.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/panthers-release-cornerback-brandon-boykin-0ap3000000662782|title=Panthers release cornerback Brandon Boykin|first=Kevin|last=Patra|date=May 16, 2016|access-date=May 17, 2016}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On July 27, 2016, Boykin signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chicago Bears sign CB Brandon Boykin and WR BJ Daniels|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/chicago-bears/article/chicago-bears-sign-cb-brandon-boykin-and-wr-bj-daniels-46461865/|last=Bell|first=Allan}}</ref> He was placed on the team's [[injured reserve list]] on August 3,  due to a [[pectoralis major muscle|pectoral]] injury suffered during training camp.<ref>{{cite web|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/08/03/bears-put-brandon-boykin-on-injured-reserve/|title=Bears put Brandon Boykin on injured reserve|first=Michael|last=Smith|date=August 3, 2016|access-date=August 3, 2016}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On June 5, 2017, Boykin signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign Two Cornerbacks, Cut Kyle Arrington|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Cornerbacks-Cut-Kyle-Arrington/3cc14bf0-1ecf-48b8-b0cd-9038a69fc23f|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=June 5, 2017}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Make 15 Moves To Set 53-Man Roster Ahead Of 2017 Season|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Make-15-Moves-To-Set-53-Man-Roster-Ahead-of-2017-Season/bdeb00bc-4c08-4b47-a63d-d0e432ee878a|author=Downing, Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119035032/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Make-15-Moves-To-Set-53-Man-Roster-Ahead-of-2017-Season/bdeb00bc-4c08-4b47-a63d-d0e432ee878a|archive-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref>

'''Brandon Brooks''' (born August 19, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Houston Texans]] and [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami RedHawks]] and was selected in the third round by the Texans in the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Brooks played four seasons with the Texans, including three as a starter. In 2016, he joined the Eagles in free agency. He played for six seasons with the team, winning [[Super Bowl LII]] and making three consecutive [[Pro Bowls]] from 2017 to 2019 in the process. He retired after missing 31 combined regular season games over the next two seasons due to injuries.

==Early life==
Brooks helped captain the [[Riverside University High School]] Tigers to an 11–2 record, a city championship and an appearance in the 2006 state semifinals and he was named all-state in 2006. He also played baseball and basketball.<ref name="Brandon Brooks - Football">{{cite web | url=https://miamiredhawks.com/sports/football/roster/brandon-brooks/922 | title=Brandon Brooks - Football }}</ref>

==College career==
A four-year starter at Miami, Brooks was named second-team All-MAC ([[Mid-American Conference]]) for each of the 2009, 2010 and 2011 seasons, the last of which the RedHawks went 10–4 overall, winning the MAC championship and a postseason bowl game. He earned a bachelor's degree in psychology.<ref name="Brandon Brooks - Football"/><ref name="Speaker">{{Cite web |date=2018-03-06 |title=NFL's Brandon Brooks '11 is Miami 2018 spring commencement speaker |url=https://miamioh.edu/news/top-stories/2018/03/brandon-brooks.html |access-date=2025-01-03 |website=Miami University}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
In his rookie season, Brooks was inactive for the first 10 games before being used as a reserve for the final six games as well as two playoff games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Scout Player Profile |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=89836&draftyear=2013&genpos=OG |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226050624/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=89836&draftyear=2013&genpos=OG |archive-date=February 26, 2014 |access-date=April 1, 2012 |website=NFLDraftScout.com}}</ref> In the 2013 season, he became a starter and remained there throughout his time with the Texans.

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On March 9, 2016, Brooks signed a five-year, $40 million contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 9, 2016 |title=Brandon Brooks Added To Offensive Line |url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Brandon-Brooks-Added-To-Offensive-Line/c6c7941f-3349-46be-91ed-8594b5e6c7e5 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825150057/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Brandon-Brooks-Added-To-Offensive-Line/c6c7941f-3349-46be-91ed-8594b5e6c7e5 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |access-date=March 10, 2016 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He started 14 games at right guard in his first year in Philadelphia.

[[File:Brandon Brooks and Jason Peters.jpg|thumb|right|Brooks (left) during the Eagles' Super Bowl LII victory parade]]
On December 19, 2017, Brooks was named to his first Pro Bowl along with right tackle [[Lane Johnson]] after starting all 16 games at right guard.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2017 |title=NFL announces 2018 Pro Bowl rosters |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/updated-player-rosters-for-2018-pro-bowl-in-orlando-0ap3000000895772 |access-date=December 26, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He could not play in the Pro Bowl because of his team advancing to the Super Bowl. Brooks would win his first Super Bowl when the Eagles defeated the [[New England Patriots]] in [[Super Bowl LII]] by a score of 41–33.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Lindsay H. |date=February 4, 2018 |title=Eagles dethrone Tom Brady, Patriots for first Super Bowl title in stunner |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/super/2018/02/04/super-bowl-2018-score-philadelphia-eagles-new-england-patriots/305840002/ |access-date=February 25, 2019 |website=USA TODAY |language=en}}</ref>
 
On December 17, 2018, Brooks was named to his second Pro Bowl. That season the Philadelphia Eagles went 9–7 and earned a wildcard spot. They defeated the Chicago Bears 16–15 in the wildcard round, then lost 20–14 to the New Orleans Saints in the divisional round. The loss was costly for Brooks, as he suffered a torn Achilles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt, Darin |date=January 13, 2019 |title=Eagles guard Brandon Brooks suffers torn Achilles |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/01/13/eagles-guard-brandon-brooks-suffers-torn-achilles/ |access-date=September 5, 2021 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sport}}</ref> He was able to return for the 2019 season, as he also incorporated [[Chinese martial arts|Kung fu]] in his off-field training.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Brandon Brooks Uses Brains to Beat Brawn {{!}} NFL Films Presents |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hu-XlTd6V80 |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=YouTube.com | date=October 31, 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

Brooks signed a four-year, $54.2 million contract extension through the 2024 season with the Eagles on November 11, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Spadaro, Dave |date=November 11, 2019 |title=Brandon Brooks' remarkable comeback leads to four-year contract extension |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/brandon-brooks-remarkable-comeback-leads-to-four-year-contract-extension |access-date=November 11, 2019}}</ref> He was named to his third straight Pro Bowl on December 17, 2019.

On December 29, 2019, Brooks suffered a dislocated shoulder in the last regular season game against the New York Giants, forcing him to miss the postseason.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2019 |title=Eagles Pro Bowl guard Brooks out rest of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28396459/eagles-pro-bowl-guard-brandon-brooks-rest-season-dislocated-shoulder |access-date=December 30, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 98th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2020]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2020-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 6, 2021 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On June 15, 2020, it was announced that Brooks tore his Achilles and would miss the upcoming 2020 season. He was placed on the active/[[physically unable to perform list]] at the start of training camp on August 4, 2020,<ref>{{Cite news |last=McPherson, Chris |date=August 4, 2020 |title=Eagles claim TE Caleb Wilson; place Brandon Brooks on Active/PUP list |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-claim-te-caleb-wilson-place-brandon-brooks-on-active-pup-list |access-date=August 4, 2020}}</ref> and placed on reserve/PUP at the start of the regular season on September 5.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McPherson, Chris |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster |access-date=September 12, 2020}}</ref> He began practicing with the team again on December 30, but the team did not activate him before the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gallen, Daniel |date=December 30, 2020 |title=Philadelphia Eagles begin practice windows for RG Brandon Brooks, LB Davion Taylor |work=PennLive.com |url=https://www.pennlive.com/philadelphiaeagles/2020/12/philadelphia-eagles-begin-practice-windows-for-rg-brandon-brooks-lb-davion-taylor.html |access-date=February 18, 2021}}</ref>

In Week 2 of the 2021 season, Brooks suffered a pectoral strain and was placed on injured reserve on September 21, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Eagles agree to sign G Jack Anderson off the Bills' practice squad|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/roster-moves-eagles-agree-to-sign-jack-anderson-off-the-bills-practice-squad|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=September 21, 2021}}</ref>

On January 26, 2022, Brooks announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Kevin|last=Patra|title=Eagles guard Brandon Brooks announces retirement after 10 seasons|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/eagles-guard-brandon-brooks-announces-retirement-after-10-seasons|website=NFL.com|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Brooks was diagnosed with a stress-related [[anxiety disorder]] in 2016, which explained his vomit bouts only on game days, even after a stomach ulcer was treated.<ref name=":0" /> He is also a [[Jiu-Jitsu]] practitioner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=#98 Brandon Brooks (G, Eagles) {{!}} Top 100 Players of 2020 {{!}} NFL - YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0G9j7r47SaQ |access-date=July 27, 2020 |website=www.youtube.com| date=July 26, 2020 }}</ref>

He was the spring 2018 commencement speaker at his alma mater, Miami University.<ref name="Speaker" />

Brooks currently resides in [[Medford, New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flynn |first=Kelly |date=April 10, 2019 |title=An Eagle makes his nest in Medford |url=https://thesunpapers.com/2019/04/10/an-eagle-makes-his-nest-in-medford/ |access-date=December 13, 2020 |website=thesunpapers.com}}</ref> After retiring, he enrolled at the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania|Wharton School]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and graduated with an MBA.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Dave |date=May 10, 2022 |title=Brandon Brooks, ex-Philadelphia Eagle from Miami, accepted to Penn's Wharton MBA program |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/miami-university/2022/05/10/brandon-brooks-accepted-wharton-school-mba-program-penn-miami-redhawks-philadelphia-eagles-guard/9723420002/ |access-date=August 15, 2022 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}}</ref>  He is an investment banker with [[Goldman Sachs]].

'''Brandon Collins''' (born April 21, 1989) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]].

==Early life==
Collins was born in Austin and his family quickly moved to San Angelo, TX before moving to Bryan and then finally Brenham. His parents were coaches and he was an honor roll student in high school. He played high school football at Brenham High School where he was a three-year letterman and  a 4A all-state wide receiver and an all-Greater Houston safety. He was also an all-district point guard in basketball and a regional qualifier in the 110 hurdles, the 300 hurdles and the long jump.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Collins |url=https://lionsports.net/sports/football/roster/brandon-collins/1254 |access-date=30 August 2025}}</ref>

His cousin [[Shaud Williams]] played for the Buffalo Bills.

==College career==
Collins started his college career at the [[University of Texas]]. In 2007, he played in 7 games as a freshman and had 2 special teams tackles and the next year he played in 12 games with 3 starts and caught 35 passes for 430 yards and 3 touchdowns, including a 103-yard receiving game against Texas A&M.<ref name="Records">{{cite web |title=Texas Football Record Book |url=https://texaslonghorns.com/documents/2024/8/8/Football_Record_Book.pdf |access-date=21 February 2025}}</ref>   He played in the 2009 Fiesta Bowl where he 7 receptions for 60 yards and Texas won.<ref>{{cite web |title=Texas 24-21 Ohio State |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/boxscore/_/gameId/290050251 |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref> He missed the 2009 season because he was academically ineligible. Then, in early 2010 he was dismissed from the Texas team when he was arrested for aggravated robbery.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Griffin |first1=Tim |title=Texas WR Collins dismissed |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/bowls09/news/story?id=4793373 |access-date=29 August 2025 |date=3 January 2010}}</ref>

He transferred to [[Southeastern Louisiana University]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite news |title=Former Texas Receiver Clear to Play at SLU |url=https://victoriaadvocate.com/2010/09/01/former-texas-receiver-clear-to-play-at-slu/ |access-date=29 August 2025 |work=Victoria Advocate |date=1 September 2010}}</ref> In his first season at Southeastern Louisiana he played in all 11 games with 8 starts and was second on the team with 56 catches for a team-high 875 yards (15.6-yard avg.) and 4 touchdowns. He also returned 13 punts for 88 yards. In 2011, he led the team in receptions (61) and receiving TDs (5) and was 2nd in receiving yards (746) while also recording 37 yards on 4 carries and leading the team with 21 kick off returns for 232 yards.<ref>{{cite web |title=2011 Football Cumulative Statistics - Southeastern Louisiana University Athletics |url=https://lionsports.net/sports/football/stats/2011?&clean=true |access-date=30 August 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===New York Giants===
Collins was signed on May 14, 2012, by the [[New York Giants]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Former Lion Brandon Collins Signs Free Agent Deal With New York Giants|url=http://www.sportsnola.com/sports/local-sports-news/slu-news/584900-former-lion-brandon-collins-signs-free-agent-deal-with-new-york-giants.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130202220140/http://www.sportsnola.com/sports/local-sports-news/slu-news/584900-former-lion-brandon-collins-signs-free-agent-deal-with-new-york-giants.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=2 February 2013|publisher=Sports NOLA|access-date=24 June 2013}}</ref> On September 4 he was signed to the Giants’ practice squad, but his contract was terminated on Sept. 10 and was not re-signed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Giants Wide Receiver Brandon Collins Suspended For First 4 Games Of Season |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/giants-wide-receiver-brandon-collins-suspended-for-first-4-games-of-season/ |access-date=29 August 2025 |date=24 June 2013}}</ref>

On January 4, 2013, he was re-signed to a reserve/futures contract, but on June 24, 2013, he was suspended without pay for the first four games of the 2013 regular season for violating the NFL policy and program regarding substances of abuse.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Valentine |first1=Ed |title=Giants Roster Breakdown: Brandon Collins |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/2013/6/25/4457708/new-york-giants-roster-breakdown-brandon-collins |access-date=30 August 2025 |date=25 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Giants Wide Receiver Brandon Collins Suspended For First 4 Games Of Season|url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2013/06/24/giants-wide-receiver-brandon-collins-suspended-for-first-4-games-of-season/|work=CBS News New York|access-date=24 June 2013}}</ref> On August 25, 2013, he was cut by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/LB-Aaron-Curry-among-players-released/4c5623fc-f421-491a-a843-0e3cb78cf38c |title=LB Aaron Curry among players released |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 26, 2013 |website=Giants.com |access-date=September 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130829084616/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/LB-Aaron-Curry-among-players-released/4c5623fc-f421-491a-a843-0e3cb78cf38c |archive-date=2013-08-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
In February 2014 he was signed by the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] but was released before the season started.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tiger Cats Add 5 to Roster |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2014/02/27/tiger-cats-add-five-to-roster/ |access-date=30 August 2025 |date=27 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tiger-Cats Add Five to Roster |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2014/02/27/tiger-cats-add-five-to-roster/ |access-date=21 November 2024 |date=27 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ticat Transactions |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2014/06/16/ticats-transactions-june-16-2014/ |access-date=21 November 2024 |date=16 June 2014}}</ref>

===San Jose Sabercats===
In October 2014, Collins was assigned the [[San Jose SaberCats]] of the [[Arena Football League]].<ref name="SJSCxations">{{cite web |title=San Jose SaberCats Transactions |url=https://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=25 |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref> Before the season started he was placed on inactive reserve and then a few weeks later moved to league suspension. He returned to the SaberCats in late April, after the season had started, and played in his first game on May 9. He had two receptions for 47 yards and a touchdown in that game and played in another game before he was placed on the injured reserve. On June 1, 2015, he was put onto reassignment.<ref>{{cite news |title=Area roundup: Spokane Shock add two defensive linemen |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2015/jun/04/area-roundup-spokane-shock-add-two-defensive/ |access-date=21 November 2024 |date=4 June 2015}}</ref><ref name="SJSCxations"/>

On June 2, 2015, Collins was claimed by the [[Spokane Shock]]. Two days later, he was traded back to the SaberCats. He played in a game on June 13 and then was put back on injured reserve on June 19, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=SaberCats Transactions |url=https://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=25 |access-date=28 August 2025}}</ref><ref name="SJSCxations"/> He was  reactivated from injured reserve on August 12, before the first playoff game, and then returned to it on August 21.<ref name="SJSCxations"/> The SaberCats went on to win [[ArenaBowl XXVIII]].

In the offseason the SaberCats exercised the league rookie option and signed him to a one-year contract.<ref name="SJSCxations"/>

===Los Angeles Kiss===
A few weeks after being signed by the SaberCats, the league announced that the team would cease operations and in December 2015, Collins was assigned to the [[Los Angeles KISS]]. He was "in the middle of a breakout season" in 2016, including making the "AFL highlight of the game" in week 1,<ref>{{cite web |title=LA Kiss Postseason Media Guide |url=https://funwhileitlasted.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/2016-LA-Kiss-Postseason-Media-Guide.pdf |access-date=30 August 2025}}</ref> with the KISS when an ACL tear sidelined him for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bledsoe |first1=Neal |title=KISS the Team Goodbye |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/kiss-the-team-goodbye |access-date=13 July 2025 |work=FOX Sports |date=30 June 2017}}</ref>

===Baltimore Brigade===
From 2017 to 2019 he played for the [[Baltimore Brigade]]. In 2017, he joined the team late but started two of the last six game and scored two touchdowns in their one playoff game that year.<ref>{{cite web |title=2017 Baltimore Brigade Postseason Media Guide |url=https://funwhileitlasted.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/2017-Baltimore-Brigade-Postseason-Media-Guide.pdf |access-date=30 August 2025}}</ref>

In 2018, he helped them reach [[ArenaBowl XXXI]] which they lost to the [[Washington Valor]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Collins |url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/?page=players&player=13252&pageview=career |website=Arena Fan |access-date=21 November 2024}}</ref> In that game he scored 3 TDs but was forced out of the game after an injury.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fominykh |first1=Katherine |title=Brigade suffer home invasion |url=https://digitaledition.baltimoresun.com/tribune/article_popover.aspx?guid=31dfa3c8-a448-4975-8117-9ce61a124c50 |access-date=21 November 2024}}</ref>

He had a standout season in 2019, finishing in the top 10 in receptions, receiving yards and receiving TDs,<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 Arena Football League Leaders |url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/leaders/l-Arena/y-2019 |access-date=13 July 2025}}</ref> but missed the last game and the playoffs with another injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Collins |url=https://www.rotowire.com/arena/player.php?id=154 |access-date=13 July 2025}}</ref> The [[Arena Football League]] shut down following the 2019 season at which point Collins was the Brigade's career leader in receiving yards, points and touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |title=BRIGADE DROP GAME 47-40 TO VALOR IN FINAL SECONDS |url=http://www.baltimorebrigade.com/wk12-story |access-date=13 July 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191129194054/http://www.baltimorebrigade.com/wk12-story |archive-date=2019-11-29}}</ref>

'''Brandon Michael Barden''' (born March 15, 1989) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[tight end]]. He was originally signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2012. He played [[college football]] at [[Vanderbilt University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Brandon-Barden/823449e5-8b19-4d03-a4cb-f48910e1bfde|title=The Tennessee Titans: Brandon Barden|accessdate=January 20, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304060540/http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Brandon-Barden/823449e5-8b19-4d03-a4cb-f48910e1bfde|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/barden_brandon00.html|title=Vanderbilt Commodores: Brandon Barden|accessdate=January 20, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171101135510/http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/barden_brandon00.html|archive-date=November 1, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Tennessee Titans===
After going undrafted, Barden was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Tennessee Titans]].

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Barden was signed to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] practice squad on November 19, 2013. He was signed to the active roster at the conclusion of the 2013 regular season. The Jaguars released Barden on August 29, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Cut-day-C-Mike-Brewster-QBs-Ricky-Stanzi-and-Stephen-Morris-waived/d4666d8f-fb6d-4c2a-96ff-2d847c0e3297# |title=Cut day: C Mike Brewster, QBs Ricky Stanzi and Stephen Morris waived |access-date=August 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181357/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Cut-day-C-Mike-Brewster-QBs-Ricky-Stanzi-and-Stephen-Morris-waived/d4666d8f-fb6d-4c2a-96ff-2d847c0e3297# |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Barden was signed to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] practice squad on October 14, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/TE-Brandon-Barden-signed-to-Practice-Squad/67120a17-8c02-4fc4-95a9-486bfb07eac8 |title=TE Brandon Barden signed to Practice Squad |access-date=August 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018022822/http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/TE-Brandon-Barden-signed-to-Practice-Squad/67120a17-8c02-4fc4-95a9-486bfb07eac8 |archive-date=October 18, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 31, he signed a future deal with the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Sign-19-To-ReserveFutures-Contracts/3270d295-cf1e-4ac8-8eb1-6913d08d481a# |title=Chiefs Sign 19 To Reserve/Futures Contracts |access-date=February 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119090658/http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Sign-19-To-ReserveFutures-Contracts/3270d295-cf1e-4ac8-8eb1-6913d08d481a# |archive-date=November 19, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 4, 2015, the [[Dallas Cowboys]] signed Barden.<ref>[http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/08/04/tues-practice-recap-cowboys-make-te-changes-mincey-solid-return Tues. Practice Recap: Cowboys Make TE Changes; Mincey Solid in Return]</ref> On September 1, 2015, he was released by the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/09/01/cowboys-release-four-make-six-roster-moves-meet-75-man-limit |title=Cowboys Release Four, Make Six Roster Moves To Meet 75-Man Limit |last=Helman |first=David |date=September 1, 2015 |website=DallasCowboys.com |accessdate=September 29, 2015}}</ref>

'''Brandon Matthew Copeland''' (born July 2, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2013 and also played for the [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Detroit Lions]], [[New York Jets]], [[New England Patriots]], and [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn Quakers football|Penn Quakers]].

==Early life==
Copeland is from [[Sykesville, Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |title=Long shots vie for roster spots |url=http://www.csnbaltimore.com/blog/ravens-talk/long-shots-vie-roster-spots |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130628232000/http://www.csnbaltimore.com/blog/ravens-talk/long-shots-vie-roster-spots |archive-date=June 28, 2013 |access-date=May 31, 2013 |publisher=csnbaltimore.com}}</ref> He is the grandson of former [[History of the Baltimore Colts|Baltimore Colts]] [[defensive end]] [[Roy Hilton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home-Grown Brandon Copeland Trying To Make It |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Home-Grown-Brandon-Copeland-Trying-To-Make-It/fd71e1a7-1b94-4476-9bfe-91e4c2434732 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607062114/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Home-Grown-Brandon-Copeland-Trying-To-Make-It/fd71e1a7-1b94-4476-9bfe-91e4c2434732 |archive-date=June 7, 2013 |access-date=May 31, 2013 |publisher=baltimoreravens.com}}</ref> Copeland graduated from the [[Gilman School]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=May 16, 2013 |title=Taking stock at Ravens' inside linebacker position minus Rolando McClain |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-taking-stock-at-inside-linebacker-minus-rolando-mcclain-20130515,0,7205536,full.story |url-status=dead |access-date=May 31, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140404154557/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-taking-stock-at-inside-linebacker-minus-rolando-mcclain-20130515,0,7205536,full.story |archive-date=April 4, 2014}}</ref> where he played 3 sports: football, basketball and track. During his senior year of high school, Copeland was awarded the position of team captain.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Biography |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/team/roster/brandon-copeland/ad4a057b-53e8-400d-bba6-bdb22bf27942/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130613023414/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/team/roster/brandon-copeland/ad4a057b-53e8-400d-bba6-bdb22bf27942/ |archive-date=June 13, 2013 |access-date=May 31, 2013 |publisher=baltimoreravens.com}}</ref>

He was on the championship squad at the 2006 [[Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association]].<ref name="auto"/> He received the National Football Foundation Scholar Athlete of the Year Award in 2008 and was an Academic All-State team honoree the same year.<ref name="auto"/>

==College career==
Copeland attended the [[University of Pennsylvania]] where he was the captain of the 2012 Ivy League championship winning team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IVY CHAMPS! Football Wins Thriller to Claim Outright Title, 35-28 |url=http://www.pennathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205746145 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304031544/http://www.pennathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205746145 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=May 31, 2013 |publisher=pennathletics.com}}</ref> He graduated from the [[Wharton School]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in economics.

===Baltimore Ravens===
[[File:Brandon Copeland Stadium Practice 2013.jpg|thumb|Copeland with the Baltimore Ravens in 2013]]
On April 27, 2013, Copeland signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ravens Sign 14 Undrafted Free Agents |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-14-Undrafted-Free-Agents/590e9c6d-3c55-40cd-98b8-32b2a06e1e8b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130506043657/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-14-Undrafted-Free-Agents/590e9c6d-3c55-40cd-98b8-32b2a06e1e8b |archive-date=May 6, 2013 |access-date=May 3, 2013 |website=baltimoreravens.com}}</ref> He was waived on August 31.

===Tennessee Titans===
Copeland was signed to the [[Tennessee Titans]] practice squad on October 8, 2013. He was released from the Titans practice squad on November 5, and re-signed to the practice squad on November 12. Copeland signed with Tennessee to a future contract on December 31.

===Orlando Predators===
On February 13, 2015, Copeland was assigned to the [[Orlando Predators]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). On March 6, 2015, Copeland was placed on the refused to report list by the Predators. On April 7, 2015, Copeland was placed on other league exempt list by the Predators.

===Detroit Lions===
On March 22, 2015, Copeland participated in the [[NFL Scouting Combine#Veteran combine|NFL Veterans Combine]]. On April 7, Copeland signed a one-year contract with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twentyman |first=Tim |date=April 7, 2015 |title=Lions sign linebacker Brandon Copeland |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-insider/article-1/Lions-sign-linebacker-Brandon-Copeland/fa1b1467-d70b-45bf-aa97-5492b9b41398 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410183511/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-insider/article-1/Lions-sign-linebacker-Brandon-Copeland/fa1b1467-d70b-45bf-aa97-5492b9b41398 |archive-date=April 10, 2015 |access-date=April 7, 2015 |website=Detroit Lions}}</ref> After participating in the combine, he and [[Ifeanyi Momah]] were the only participants to be offered contracts.

In 2017, Copeland suffered a torn pectoral in the Lions' first preseason game and was ruled out for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams, Charean |date=August 14, 2017 |title=Brandon Copeland reportedly out for year with torn pec |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/14/brandon-copeland-reportedly-out-for-year-with-torn-pec/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 16, 2017 |title=Lions sign three free agents |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-three-free-agents/e0cc4e07-398b-488d-bb21-ca47db712732 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816204831/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-three-free-agents/e0cc4e07-398b-488d-bb21-ca47db712732 |archive-date=August 16, 2017 |access-date=August 16, 2017 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On March 19, 2018, Copeland signed with the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda, Nate |date=March 19, 2018 |title=Jets Sign LB Brandon Copeland |url=http://nfltraderumors.co/jets-sign-lb-brandon-copeland/}}</ref> He played in 16 games with 10 starts, recording 35 combined tackles, and five sacks.

On March 25, 2019, Copeland re-signed with the Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg, Ethan |date=March 25, 2019 |title=Jets Re-Sign LB Brandon Copeland |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-re-sign-lb-brandon-copeland |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was suspended for the first four games of the 2019 season by violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman, Jeremy |date=August 21, 2019 |title=Jets OLB Brandon Copeland suspended four games |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jets-olb-brandon-copeland-suspended-four-games-0ap3000001043173 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was reinstated from the suspension on October 7 and activated prior to Week 6.
In Week 9 against the [[Miami Dolphins]], Copeland recorded a team-high 9 tackles and sacked [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] once in the 18–26 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2019 |title=Dolphins get first win of 2019, top Jets 26-18 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128080 |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On March 25, 2020, Copeland signed a $1.1 million contract with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper, Josh |date=March 22, 2020 |title=Patriots add Brandon Copeland |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/22/patriots-add-brandon-copeland/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> On October 28, he was placed on injured reserve after suffering a torn pectoral in Week 7.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2020 |title=Patriots place LB Brandon Copeland on injured reserve and TE Jake Burt on practice squad injured reserve |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-place-lb-brandon-copeland-on-injured-reserve-and-te-jake-burt-on-practi |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On March 19, 2021, Copeland signed a one-year contract with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 19, 2021 |title=Falcons Sign LB Brandon Copeland and S Erik Harris |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-lb-brandon-copeland-and-s-erik-harris |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> On September 11, he was waived by the Falcons,<ref>{{Cite web |first=Dave |last=Choate |date=September 11, 2021 |title=Falcons reportedly cut OLB Brandon Copeland. Wait, what? |url=https://www.thefalcoholic.com/2021/9/11/22668952/falcons-reportedly-cut-olb-brandon-copeland-wait-what |website=TheFalcoholic.com}}</ref> but was re-signed two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Myles |last=Simmons |date=September 13, 2021 |title=Falcons re-sign Brandon Copeland |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/09/13/falcons-re-sign-brandon-copeland/ |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens (second stint)===
On September 21, 2022, Copeland signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Clifton |title=Ravens Sign Linebacker Brandon Copeland to Practice Squad |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-brandon-copeland-practice-squad |access-date=21 September 2022 |work=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He was released from the Ravens on October 18.<ref>{{cite web | last=Brown | first=Clifton | title=Ravens Sign Two Veteran Linebackers to Practice Squad | website=Baltimore Ravens | date=2022-10-18 | url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-devon-kennard-practice-squad | access-date=2026-04-05}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On August 21, 2023, Copeland announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=2023-08-21 |title=Veteran LB Copeland retires after 10 NFL seasons |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38232518/free-agent-linebacker-brandon-copeland-32-retires-nfl |access-date=2023-08-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Copeland interned at the investment bank [[UBS]] over two summers during college and has since returned to Penn to teach a financial literacy seminar with Dr. Brian Peterson, the director of Penn's Makuu Black Cultural Center.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elkins, Kathleen |date=March 2, 2019 |title=NFL player who saves nearly 90% of his income teaches a money class at Penn called 'Life 101' |website=[[CNBC]] |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/01/nfls-brandon-copeland-is-teaching-life-101-a-money-class-at-penn.html}}</ref>
He has also appeared on the Netflix series ''Buy My House'' in 2022.

'''Brandon Duc Allen''' (born September 5, 1992) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] for the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]] and was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the sixth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]]. Allen has also been a member of the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Denver Broncos]], [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], and [[Tennessee Titans]].

==Early life==
Allen attended [[Fayetteville High School (Arkansas)|Fayetteville High School]] in [[Fayetteville, Arkansas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrews |first=C. Steve |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Former Arkansas QB Brandon Allen set for historic eighth NFL season |url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2023/08/29/former-arkansas-qb-brandon-allen-set-for-historic-eighth-season-in-the-nfl/ |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Razorbacks Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> As a senior, he threw for 3,408 yards and 38 [[touchdowns]]. He was ranked by [[Rivals.com]] as the fifth-best pro-style [[quarterback]] recruit.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Allen, 2011 Pro Style Quarterback, Arkansas |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/brandon-allen-14348?view=pv |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Allen was [[redshirted]] as a freshman in 2011. In 2012, he was the backup to [[Tyler Wilson (American football)|Tyler Wilson]]. He appeared in five games and started one game after Wilson missed a game because of injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Matt |date=September 15, 2012 |title=Tyler Wilson does not start for Arkansas against Alabama |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2012-09-15/tyler-wilson-arkansas-does-not-start-alabama-brandon-allen-john-l-smith |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=Sporting News |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924132547/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2012-09-15/tyler-wilson-arkansas-does-not-start-alabama-brandon-allen-john-l-smith |url-status=dead }}</ref> He finished the season completing 21 of 49 passes for 186 yards with one touchdown and three [[interceptions]].

In 2013, Allen took over as the starting quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2013 |title=Allen taking control at Arkansas as quarterback|agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=ncf&id=9559126 |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwartz |first=Nick |date=November 25, 2013 |title=Arkansas QB's truck egged after losing game to Mississippi State |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2013/11/arkansas-allen-truck-egged |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=For The Win }}</ref> He passed for 1,552 yards, completing 49.6 percent of his throws, and threw for 13 touchdowns and 10 interceptions for a team that finished 3–9 under first year head coach [[Bret Bielema]].

As a junior in 2014, Allen had 2,285 passing yards, 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. He was the offensive MVP of the [[2014 Texas Bowl]], a 31–7 victory against the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]]. Allen threw two touchdowns in the game, and Arkansas finished with a 7–6 record.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Autullo |first=Ryan |date=December 29, 2014 |title=Texas Bowl notebook: Arkansas’ Allen a surprise MVP |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/news/2014/12/30/texas-bowl-notebook-arkansas-allen/6715464007/ |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Austin American-Statesman |language=en-US}}</ref>

During his senior year in 2015, Allen threw a then-school record six touchdown passes, and ran in the game winning 2 point conversion in a 53–52 overtime win over [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arkansas vs. Ole Miss – Game Summary – November 7, 2015 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400603908 |access-date=August 28, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He broke the record two weeks later with seven touchdowns in a 51–50 loss to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Razorbacks Football: Allen's Big Day Bittersweet |url=https://www.swtimes.com/article/20151123/SPORTS/311239949 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=Times Record |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mississippi State vs. Arkansas – Game Summary – November 21, 2015 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400603922 |access-date=August 28, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He also broke Arkansas' record for career passing touchdowns against Mississippi State.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holt |first=Bob |date=November 22, 2015 |title=Records don't matter now |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2015/nov/22/records-don-t-matter-now-20151122-1/ |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=Arkansas Online}}</ref> He finished the year with 3,440 passing yards, 30 touchdowns, and eight interceptions for a team that finished 8–5, and beat [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]] in the [[2016 Liberty Bowl (January)|2016 Liberty Bowl]], 45–23.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas State vs. Arkansas – Game Summary – January 2, 2016 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400852740 |access-date=August 28, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Allen finished his career with 7,463 passing yards, 64 passing touchdowns, and 26 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 8, 2015 |title=Brandon Allen |language=en-US |work=Arkansas Razorbacks |url=https://www.arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/brandon-allen-2/ |access-date=August 28, 2017}}</ref>  Allen majored in recreation and sport management.
