===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Allen was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the sixth round with the 201st overall pick in the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=April 30, 2016 |title=Jaguars snap defensive draft by taking Arkansas QB Brandon Allen |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/jacksonville-jaguars/post/_/id/17620/jaguars-snap-defensive-draft-by-taking-arkansas-qb-brandon-allen |access-date=September 4, 2017}}</ref> On May 5, 2016, Allen signed a four-year $2.48 million contract, which included a $147,687 signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2016 |title=Brandon Allen contract |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/jacksonville-jaguars/post/_/id/17688/sixth-round-picks-tyrone-holmes-brandon-allen-sign-with-jaguars |access-date=June 10, 2016 |website=ESPN.Go.com}}</ref> Allen was the Jaguars' third-string quarterback his rookie season behind [[Blake Bortles]] and [[Chad Henne]].

Allen was waived by the Jaguars on September 3, 2017, following final roster cuts for the 2017 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Jaguars release second-year QB Brandon Allen |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-release-second-year-qb-brandon-allen-0ap3000000838839 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On September 4, 2017, Allen was claimed off waivers by the [[Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=September 4, 2017 |title=Rams Claim QB Brandon Allen |url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Claim-QB-Brandon-Allen/d135de48-d5bf-43fc-b65c-56a73cf902d1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021021749/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Claim-QB-Brandon-Allen/d135de48-d5bf-43fc-b65c-56a73cf902d1 |archive-date=October 21, 2017 |access-date=September 5, 2017 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> He was inactive for every game of the season as the Rams' third-string quarterback behind [[Jared Goff]] and [[Sean Mannion (American football)|Sean Mannion]]. Allen was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 20.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=December 20, 2017 |title=Rams Place Allen on IR, Sign Edebali |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-place-allen-on-ir-sign-edebali-20027115 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref>

On September 18, 2018, Allen was waived by the Rams and was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=September 18, 2018 |title=Rams Waive QB Brandon Allen, Cut Two from Practice Squad |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-waive-qb-brandon-allen-cut-two-from-practice-squad |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref>

Allen signed a reserve/future contract with the Rams on February 7, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=February 7, 2019 |title=Rams sign two players to free agent contracts |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-sign-two-players-to-free-agent-contracts |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> On August 30, Allen was released as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Han |first=Jamie |date=August 30, 2019 |title=Rams make initial roster cuts, 18 players released |work=TheRams.com |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-make-initial-roster-cuts-18-players-released |access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref>

=== Denver Broncos ===
On September 1, 2019, Allen was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Broncos claim four players off waivers, sign seven players to practice squad |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-claim-four-players-off-waivers-sign-seven-players-to-practice-squad |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> After an injury to starting quarterback [[Joe Flacco]] in Week 8 of the 2019 season, Allen stepped in as the starting quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=October 28, 2019 |title=Joe Flacco to miss Week 9 game vs. Browns, Brandon Allen to start at quarterback |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/joe-flacco-to-miss-week-9-game-vs-browns-brandon-allen-to-start-at-quarterback?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |access-date=October 31, 2019 |website=DenverBroncos.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Allen made his first start in Week 9 against the [[Cleveland Browns]]. In the game, Allen threw for 193 yards and two touchdowns in the 24–19 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2019 |title=Allen leads Broncos past Browns 24–19 in first NFL start |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128088 |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

=== Cincinnati Bengals ===
[[File:Brandon Allen (51394704964) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Allen in 2021]]
On August 1, 2020, Allen was signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 1, 2020 |title=Bengals Sign Two Free Agents |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-sign-two-free-agents |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=Bengals.com}}</ref> He was released on September 5,<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Bengals Reduce 2020 Roster To 53 Players |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reduce-2020-roster-to-53-players |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=Bengals.com}}</ref> but was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2020 |title=Bengals Establish Practice Squad |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-establish-practice-squad-x0373 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=Bengals.com |archive-date=September 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929052540/https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-establish-practice-squad-x0373 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Allen was promoted to the active roster on November 23 after starting quarterback [[Joe Burrow]] suffered a season-ending injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2020 |title=Joe Burrow Placed On Reserve/Injured List; Quinton Spain & Brandon Allen Signed Off The Practice Squad |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/joe-burrow-placed-on-reserve-injured-list-quinton-spain-brandon-allen-signed-off |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=Bengals.com |archive-date=November 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129214049/https://www.bengals.com/news/joe-burrow-placed-on-reserve-injured-list-quinton-spain-brandon-allen-signed-off |url-status=dead }}</ref> Two days later, the team announced that Allen would start for the Bengals during their Week 12 game against the [[New York Giants]] in place of the injured Joe Burrow.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=November 25, 2020 |title=Bengals planning to start QB Brandon Allen over Ryan Finley vs. Giants |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-planning-to-start-qb-brandon-allen-over-ryan-finley-vs-giants |access-date=November 25, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> During Week 16 against the [[Houston Texans]], he had 371 passing yards and two touchdowns in the 37–31 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans – December 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012270htx.htm |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Allen started the final game for the season against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], where he completed six of 21 passes for 48 yards, two interceptions, and a [[List of NFL quarterbacks who have posted a passer rating of zero|passer rating of 0.0]] as the Bengals lost 38–3.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 3, 2021 |title=Bengals' Brandon Allen: Dreadful against Ravens |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bengals-brandon-allen-dreadful-against-ravens/ |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 10, 2021, Allen signed a one-year contract extension with the Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 10, 2021 |title=Bengals Re-Sign Quarterback Brandon Allen |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-re-sign-quarterback-brandon-allen |url-status=live |access-date=March 10, 2021 |website=Bengals.com |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210318145150/https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-re-sign-quarterback-brandon-allen |archive-date=March 18, 2021 }}</ref>

Allen played his first game of the 2021 season against the [[Detroit Lions]] in Week 6. Allen threw a touchdown pass to [[Auden Tate]] on his only pass attempt of the game, while taking 3 kneel downs at the end of the game. Allen would appear in the Bengals' next game against the Ravens, recording no stats in the 41–17 victory. In Week 9, with the game out of reach for the Bengals, Allen would go 1 for 2 for 6 yards passing, while rushing once in the 41–16 loss to the Browns. In Week 12, Allen would once again see playing time, this time against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. Allen threw an incomplete pass on his only passing attempt, and lost a yard on his only rush attempt of the game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2021 |title=Brandon Allen 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AlleBr00/gamelog/2021/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211219080902/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AlleBr00/gamelog/2021/ |archive-date=December 19, 2021 |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Allen started the season finale against the Browns where he threw for 136 yards and a touchdown in the 21–16 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Cleveland Browns – January 9th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201090cle.htm |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Allen re-signed with the Bengals on a one-year contract on March 18, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|work=Bengals.com|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-roster-moves-x4967|title=Bengals Roster Moves|date=March 18, 2022|accessdate=March 20, 2022}}</ref> On August 31, the Bengals cut Allen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marcum |first=Jason |date=August 31, 2022 |title=Bengals cut Brandon Allen and sign 13 to practice squad |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2022/8/31/23331503/bengals-roster-news-brandon-allen-practice-squad-2022 |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Cincy Jungle|publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref> He re-signed with the Bengals the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=September 2, 2022 |title=Bengals re-sign Brandon Allen |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bengals-re-sign-brandon-allen |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> Allen was subbed in at the end of the Week 9 game against the [[Carolina Panthers]] due to the Bengals resting their starters for the majority of the fourth quarter. Allen completed all three of his pass attempts for a total of 22 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Cincinnati Bengals – November 6th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202211060cin.htm |access-date=October 12, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On May 8, 2023, Allen was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign Quarterback, Defensive Lineman and Tight End to One-Year Deals|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-quarterback-defensive-lineman-and-tight-end-to-one-year-deals|website=49ers.com|date=May 8, 2023|access-date=May 8, 2023}}</ref> He served as the team's third-string quarterback behind [[Brock Purdy]] and [[Sam Darnold]] in 2023.[[File:49ers offense vs Bears 2024.jpg|thumb|Allen leading the 49ers' offense against the [[2024 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] in 2024]]On March 13, 2024, Allen re-signed with the 49ers.<ref>{{cite web |title=49ers Release Arik Armstead, Re-Sign Quarterback and Other Moves |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/free-agency-arik-armstead-colton-mckivitz-george-odum-brandon-allen-quarterback-dl |website=49ers.com |date=March 13, 2024 |access-date=March 13, 2024}}</ref> He began the season as the second-string quarterback behind Brock Purdy after beating out [[Joshua Dobbs]] during training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Branch |first=Eric |date=September 4, 2024 |title=What other ailment has kept 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey sidelined? |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/49ers/article/ailment-kept-49ers-christian-mccaffrey-19745268.php |access-date=September 10, 2024 |website=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref> After Purdy was ruled out with an injury, Allen was named the starter for the 49ers' Week 12 matchup against the [[Green Bay Packers]], marking Allen's first start since the 2021 season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gordon |first1=Grant |title=Niners QB Brock Purdy (shoulder) ruled out Sunday vs. Packers; Brandon Allen to start |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/niners-qb-brock-purdy-shoulder-ruled-out-sunday-vs-packers |access-date=November 22, 2024 |work=NFL.com |date=November 22, 2024}}</ref> Against the Packers, Allen threw for 199 yards, a touchdown, an interception, and lost a fumble in a 38–10 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Megargee |first=Steve |date=November 24, 2024 |title=Josh Jacobs runs for 3 TDs as Packers roll past short-handed 49ers 38-10 |url=https://apnews.com/article/49ers-packers-score-3217d53c809e76e22bea11b7fbba0e80 |access-date=November 24, 2024 |publisher=Associated Press}}</ref> Allen also entered the Week 14 game against the [[Chicago Bears]] on two occasions, initially after Purdy exited the game with a suspected injury and again when [[garbage time|victory for the 49ers was assured]]; he threw an interception during the latter stint.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Chamberlain|first=Gene|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bears/onsi/chicago-bears-and-san-francisco-49ers-in-game-blog|title=Bears and 49ers In-Game Blog: 49ers 38, Bears 13 FINAL|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=December 8, 2024|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 14, 2025, Allen signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] on a one-year, $1.42 million contract, reuniting with head coach [[Brian Callahan]] from his tenure as offensive coordinator for the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |website=TennesseeTitans.com |title=Titans Sign Veteran QB Brandon Allen |date=Mar 14, 2025 |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-veteran-qb-brandon-allen |access-date=Mar 14, 2025}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On April 13, 2026, Allen signed a one-year contract with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salamone |first1=Dan |title=Giants sign quarterback Brandon Allen |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-quarterback-brandon-allen-stats-free-agency-nfl-2026 |website=Giants.com |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Brandon Jamal Bostick''' (born May 3, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Newberry Wolves football|Newberry Wolves]]. Bostick was signed by the [[Green Bay Packers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2012. He was also a member of the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Arizona Cardinals]] and [[New York Jets]]. He is known for his [[Muffed punt|muff]] of an [[onside kick]] in the [[2014 NFC Championship Game|2014 NFC Championship game]] that allowed the [[Seattle Seahawks]] to make a late fourth-quarter comeback, defeat the Packers and advance to Super Bowl XLIX.

==Early life and college==
Bostick was born in [[Florence, South Carolina]] and graduated from [[West Florence High School]] in 2007. He then attended [[Newberry College]], a [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] school. After redshirting his freshman year, Bostick played at Newberry as [[wide receiver]] from the 2008 to 2011 seasons. In 39 games, he started 24 and made 136 receptions for 1,935 yards and 19 touchdowns. Bostick also played basketball at Newberry for the second half of his junior season.<ref name="Packers">{{cite web|url=http://www.packers.com/team/roster/Brandon-Bostick/855d5326-2230-4a0b-9f22-20b58a40a56b|title=Brandon Bostick|publisher=Green Bay Packers|access-date=January 19, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902190739/http://www.packers.com/team/roster/brandon-bostick/855d5326-2230-4a0b-9f22-20b58a40a56b/|archive-date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Newberry">{{cite web|title=Brandon Bostick|url=http://newberryathleticsite.com/profile.asp?playerID=1228|publisher=Newberry College|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111118202415/http://newberryathleticsite.com/profile.asp?playerID=1228|archive-date=November 18, 2011}}</ref> He was a [[sports management]] major at Newberry.<ref name="Newberry"/>

===Green Bay Packers===
[[File:Brandon Bostick in 2014.jpg|thumb|Bostick at Packers training camp in 2014]]
He was signed by the Packers as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 30, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Bostick signs contract with Green Bay Packers|url=http://www.newberrywolves.com/fb/news/2011-12/5278/brandon-bostick-signs-contract-with-green-bay-packers/|publisher=Newberry College|access-date=January 20, 2015|date=May 30, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617222309/http://www.newberrywolves.com/fb/news/2011-12/5278/brandon-bostick-signs-contract-with-green-bay-packers/|archive-date=June 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bostick spent his entire rookie season in 2012 on the practice squad.<ref name="Packers"/>

Playing primarily on special teams, Bostick made his NFL debut on September 15, 2013, against [[2013 Washington Redskins season|Washington]].<ref name="Packers detailed">{{citation|title=Brandon Bostick|url=http://prod.static.packers.clubs.nfl.com/assets/docs/2014/2014-packers-83-268.pdf|website=Packers 2014 Media Guide|publisher=Green Bay Packers|pages=92–93|date=2014|access-date=January 20, 2015|archive-date=October 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141026101507/http://prod.static.packers.clubs.nfl.com/assets/docs/2014/2014-packers-83-268.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He recorded his first NFL touchdown catch on November 10, 2013, against the [[2013 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], on a 22-yard pass from [[Scott Tolzien]], in a play that was also Tolzien's first career touchdown pass.<ref name="Packers"/><ref>{{cite web|last1=Reischel|first1=Rob|title=Scott Tolzien shifts from practice squad to starter|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/packers/scott-tolzien-shifts-from-practice-squad-to-starter-b99139504z1-231682991.html|website=Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel|access-date=January 20, 2015|date=November 12, 2013}}</ref> Bostick finished the 2013 season with 7 receptions for 120 yards and a touchdown in 11 games.<ref name="Packers"/> He missed the [[NFL on Thanksgiving Day|Thanksgiving Classic]] due to a concussion suffered during the November 24 game.  On December 15 against [[2013 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas]], Bostick suffered a foot injury late in the second half; he was placed on season-ending injured reserve six days later.<ref name="Packers detailed"/>

Bostick played 13 games in the 2014 season and made 2 receptions for 3 yards and a touchdown.<ref name="Packers"/> On November 9, in a [[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday night]] 55–14 win over the [[2014 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], Bostick made the Packers' first touchdown score, on a pass from [[Aaron Rodgers]] on fourth down from the Bears' 1-yard line.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gamecenter: Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers|url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014110910/2014/REG10/bears@packers#menu=gameinfo|contentId%3A0ap3000000425849&tab=analyze|publisher=NFL|access-date=January 20, 2015|date=November 9, 2014}}</ref>

In the [[2014–15 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship Game: Seattle Seahawks 28.2C Green Bay Packers 22 .28OT.29|NFC Championship Game]] against the [[2014 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] on January 18, 2015, with slightly over 2 minutes remaining and the Packers leading 19–14, Bostick, the Packers' third-string tight end, misplayed a Seahawks [[onside kick]] by ignoring his blocking assignment and stepping in front of [[All-Pro]] receiver [[Jordy Nelson]] who was assigned to catch and was waiting for the ball. The ball bounced off Bostick's helmet and was recovered by Seahawks wide receiver [[Chris Matthews (American football)|Chris Matthews]]. In the ensuing drive, the Seahawks scored a touchdown and a two-point conversion to go ahead 22–19. [[Mason Crosby]] made a game-tying field goal with 14 seconds left, but Seattle won 28–22 in overtime. Bostick was widely credited in both Wisconsin and National sports media as having made a [[Bill Buckner]]-type mistake costing his team a chance for a championship.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wilner|first1=Barry|title=Seahawks rally stuns Packers 28–22 in OT for NFC title|url=http://pro32.ap.org/article/seahawks-rally-stuns-packers-28-22-ot-nfc-title|publisher=Associated Press|access-date=January 18, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Farmer | first=Sam | title=Seahawks pull miracles out of their pocket, earn return to Super Bowl | website=Los Angeles Times | date=2015-01-18 | url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/nfl/la-sp-seahawks-packers-20150119-story.html | access-date=2025-09-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Seahawks rally to stun Packers in OT, clinch return trip to Super Bowl | website=ABC7 New York | date=2015-01-19 | url=https://abc7ny.com/post/seahawks-rally-to-stun-packers-in-ot-clinch-return-trip-to-super-bowl/480762/ | access-date=2025-09-27}}</ref> In his postgame interview, Bostick acknowledged that he was supposed to block so that [[Jordy Nelson]] could recover the onside kick.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wood |first1=Ryan |title=Bostick admits play for onside kick 'not my job' |url=http://www.greenbaypressgazette.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2015/01/18/bostick-admits-play-for-onside-kick-not-my-job/21976159/ |website=Green Bay Press-Gazette |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150120081700/http://www.greenbaypressgazette.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2015/01/18/bostick-admits-play-for-onside-kick-not-my-job/21976159/ |archive-date=January 20, 2015 |date=January 19, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Bostick was released on February 16, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasyfootball/update/25070773/packers-release-nfc-title-game-goat-brandon-bostick|title=Packers release NFC title game goat Brandon Bostick|last=Krest|first=Shawn|work=fantasynews.cbssports.com|date=February 16, 2015|access-date=February 16, 2015}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Bostick was claimed off waivers by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on February 18, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/vikings-claim-tight-end-brandon-bostick-off-waivers-0ap3000000471264|title=Vikings claim tight end Brandon Bostick off waivers|first=Nick|last=Shook|work=NFL.com|date=February 18, 2015|access-date=February 18, 2015}}</ref> He was released as part of the first wave of roster cuts on August 30, 2015.

===Arizona Cardinals===
On September 7, 2015, the [[Arizona Cardinals]] signed Bostick to their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Practice-Squad-Set-For-Cardinals/0e6435c2-45b2-4b05-aea5-e7234141db91 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301044621/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Practice-Squad-Set-For-Cardinals/0e6435c2-45b2-4b05-aea5-e7234141db91 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 1, 2018 |title=Practice Squad Set For Cardinals |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=September 7, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com |access-date=September 11, 2015}}</ref> On September 22, 2015, he was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.azcardinals.com/2015/09/22/kerwynn-williams-cut-as-massie-returns/ |title=Kerwynn Williams cut as Massie returns |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=September 22, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com |access-date=October 5, 2015 |archive-date=October 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006020111/http://blog.azcardinals.com/2015/09/22/kerwynn-williams-cut-as-massie-returns/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On October 2, 2015, Bostick was re-signed to the Cardinals' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Looking-To-Break-Out-Michael-Floyd/f12622a4-3959-425b-b9b4-c9d2eb3cade3 |title=Looking To Break Out Michael Floyd |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=October 2, 2015 |website=AZCardinals.com |access-date=October 5, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005004343/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Looking-To-Break-Out-Michael-Floyd/f12622a4-3959-425b-b9b4-c9d2eb3cade3 |archive-date=October 5, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 1, 2015, he was released from practice squad.

===New York Jets===
On December 8, 2015, the [[New York Jets]] signed Bostick to their practice squad. '''Brandon Coleman''' (born June 22, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. He signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] as an undrafted free agent after the [[2014 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Coleman attended [[Bishop McNamara High School]] in [[Forestville, Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunleavy |first=Ryan |date=November 16, 2013 |title=Brandon Coleman took lessons learned from tap to field |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/aac/2013/11/16/brandon-coleman-tap-dance-nfl-draft-rutgers-scarlet-knights/3612869/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211082023/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/aac/2013/11/16/brandon-coleman-tap-dance-nfl-draft-rutgers-scarlet-knights/3612869/ |archive-date=February 11, 2017 |access-date=August 12, 2023 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> As a senior, he had 41 receptions for 838 yards and 10 [[touchdowns]].{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}

==College career==
As a sophomore at Rutgers in 2012, Coleman had 43 receptions for 718 yards and 10 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Caldwell |first=Dave |date=August 29, 2013 |title=As Brandon Coleman Goes, So Goes Rutgers |url=http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324906304579039180912286534.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230812183826/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887324906304579039180912286534 |archive-date=August 12, 2023 |access-date=August 12, 2023 |website=[[Wall Street Journal]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He was named Second-team All-Big East for the 20212 season.<ref name="d062">{{cite web |last=Bellano |first=Anthony |date=December 17, 2013 |title=Rutgers Receiver Brandon Coleman Headed to the NFL; Players Honored at Banquet |url=https://patch.com/new-jersey/eastbrunswick/rutgers-receiver-brandon-coleman-headed-to-the-nfl-players-honored-at-banquet-eastbrunswick |access-date=January 13, 2025 |website=East Brunswick, NJ Patch}}</ref> The following season, Coleman recorded 34 receptions, 538 yards, and four touchdowns his junior year with the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Scarlet Knights]].<ref name="Junior Stats">{{Cite web |title=Brandon Coleman College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandon-coleman-2.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915082040/http://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandon-coleman-2.html |archive-date=September 15, 2015 |access-date=April 30, 2015 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Coleman entered the [[2014 NFL draft]] after his junior season, however went undrafted.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 14, 2013 |title=Rutgers WR Brandon Coleman to enter 2014 NFL Draft |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rutgers-wr-brandon-coleman-to-enter-2014-nfl-draft-0ap2000000297808 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004155109/https://www.nfl.com/news/rutgers-wr-brandon-coleman-to-enter-2014-nfl-draft-0ap2000000297808 |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=August 12, 2023 |website=[[NFL.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Brandon Carswell''' (born May 22, 1989) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]]. Carswell signed as an undrafted free agent after the [[2012 NFL draft]].

==High school==
Carswell attended [[Milpitas High School]] in [[Milpitas, CA]]. Carswell chose to attend USC after being recruited by many other top schools.

==College career==
Carswell played the most during his redshirt senior year, after considering transferring due to sanctions.

==Professional career==

===Oakland Raiders===
Carswell was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent after the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He was released on September 12, 2012.

===San Francisco 49ers===
In 2013, he signed with the 49ers but was placed on injured reserve. He was waived on April 11, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Waive WR Brandon Carswell|url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Waive-WR-Brandon-Carswell/fe1ee4cc-5793-4c41-ab8b-aada44144888|publisher=49ers.com|accessdate=April 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000220/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Waive-WR-Brandon-Carswell/fe1ee4cc-5793-4c41-ab8b-aada44144888|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Brandon Dixon''' (born April 26, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the sixth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats football|Northwest Missouri State Bearcats]].

Dixon was also a member of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[New England Patriots]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[New York Giants]] and [[Orlando Apollos]].

'''Brandon Dunn''' (born September 5, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Houston Texans]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]].

==Early life==
Dunn played [[high school football]] at [[Pleasure Ridge Park High School]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], where he was a three-year starter and team captain. He was the team's Most Valuable Player and best offensive lineman in 2009. Dunn was also the team's top defensive lineman in 2008. He recorded 65 tackles and 16 sacks as a senior, including 30 solo tackles. He also recorded 50 tackles and 16 sacks his junior year.<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandon_dunn_709591.html |title=Brandon Dunn |publisher=gocards.com |access-date=December 16, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218175050/http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandon_dunn_709591.html |archive-date=December 18, 2014 }}</ref>

==College career==
Dunn played at the [[University of Louisville]] from 2010 to 2013.<ref name="A"/> He played in 49 games for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Cardinals]], starting 30. He recorded career totals  of 101 tackles, 3 sacks, 2 fumble recoveries and 2 pass deflections.

'''Brandon Doughty''' (born October 6, 1991) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] and was their starting quarterback from 2013 to 2015. He was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the seventh round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Doughty attended [[North Broward Preparatory School]] in [[Coconut Creek, Florida]].  During his career as the starting [[quarterback]] he passed for 2,885 yards with 23 [[touchdowns]] and 12 [[interceptions]].  Rated as a three-star recruit by both [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com]], Doughty was named an FACA North-South All-Star, a Dade-Broward All-Star and was named to the First-team All-Broward County by the ''[[Miami Herald]]'' and the ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]''.

Originally, Doughty had committed to [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic]] before signing with WKU for the 2010 recruiting class.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225013/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-01-15/sports/flspbrowagt16-20100115_1_cooper-city-boyd-anderson-james-pagano Broward high school results and schedules]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Coming in the air |url=http://www.fauowlaccess.com/articles/289/wku-coming-in-the-air-at-fau.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304035248/http://www.fauowlaccess.com/articles/289/wku-coming-in-the-air-at-fau.aspx |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=December 26, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
===2010===
Doughty [[redshirted]] the 2010 season.<ref name="profile">{{Cite web |title=#12 Brandon Doughty |url=http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandon_doughty_845138.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141203011251/http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandon_doughty_845138.html |archive-date=December 3, 2014 |access-date=December 26, 2014 |website=WKUSports.com |publisher=Western Kentucky Hilltoppers}}</ref>

===2011===
{{see also|2011 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football team}}
Doughty made his [[college football]] debut for the Hilltoppers in a 40–14 loss to [[2011 Navy Midshipmen football team|Navy]].  Making a relief appearance, Doughty completed 12 of 21 passes for 102 yards, no touchdowns and an interception.  Still, his performance was enough to earn him the starting job the next week at home against [[2011 Indiana State Sycamores football team|Indiana State]]. However, after only three plays (and one completion for four yards), Doughty suffered a knee injury which ended his freshman season.<ref name="wkuherald">{{Cite web |last=Stephens, Brad |date=September 21, 2011 |title=WKU routed; Doughty, Vasquez likely out for season |url=http://wkuherald.com/sports/article_95d5307e-e316-11e0-8a25-001a4bcf6878.html |access-date=December 26, 2014 |publisher=WKUHerald.com}}</ref><ref name="profile" />

===2012===
{{see also|2012 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football team}}
As a redshirt sophomore, Doughty saw limited action as a relief quarterback, appearing in two games against [[2012 Austin Peay Governors football team|Austin Peay]] and [[2012 Southern Miss Golden Eagles football team|Southern Miss]].  In these games, Doughty completed one of three pass attempts for seven yards.<ref name="profile" />

===2013===
{{see also|2013 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football team}}
Regaining his starting job as a redshirt junior, Doughty set many records during the 2013 season.  Among the new records were single-season passing yards (2,857), single-season completion percentage (65.8), and single-game completions and passing yards (29 and 386, respectively, both in a 32–26 defeat on October 26 against [[2013 Troy Trojans football team|Troy]]).  Overall, Doughty finished the 2013 season completing 246 of 374 attempts with 14 touchdowns and 14 interceptions.

===2014===
{{see also|2014 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football team}}
2014 was the Hilltoppers' first season as a member of [[Conference USA]] (C-USA). Doughty broke his previous records for single-game completions and passing yards (46 and 569, respectively, in the season-opening 59–31 victory over [[2014 Bowling Green Falcons football team|Bowling Green]]).  Playing only one game with a completion percentage below 58.3 or a passer rating lower than 119.9 (that game being a 59–10 defeat on November 10 to [[2014 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|Louisiana Tech]]), Doughty and WKU finished the regular season with a 7–5 overall record (4–4 in C-USA).

On December 10, Doughty was named C-USA's Most Valuable Player,<ref name="cusamvp">{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2014 |title=Conference USA Announces Football Players of the Year |url=http://www.conferenceusa.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121014aad.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217054739/http://www.conferenceusa.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121014aad.html |archive-date=December 17, 2014 |access-date=December 26, 2014 |publisher=Conference USA}}</ref> the same day it was announced that the [[NCAA]] had granted him a sixth year of eligibility.<ref name="yearsix">{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2014 |title=Doughty Granted Sixth Year of Eligibility by NCAA |url=http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121014aaa.html |access-date=December 26, 2014 |website=WKUSports.com |publisher=Western Kentucky Hilltoppers}}</ref>

The next day, on December 11, Doughty was announced as the winner of the 2014 [[Sammy Baugh Trophy]], becoming the first Hilltopper and only the third quarterback from C-USA to do so.<ref name="baughaward">{{Cite web |date=December 11, 2014 |title=Brandon Doughty Wins 2014 Sammy Baugh Award |url=http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121114aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215042455/http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121114aaa.html |archive-date=December 15, 2014 |access-date=December 26, 2014 |website=WKUSports.com |publisher=Western Kentucky Hilltoppers}}</ref>

On December 24, Doughty led the Hilltoppers to a 49–48 victory over [[2014 Central Michigan Chippewas football team|Central Michigan]] in the [[2014 Bahamas Bowl]], completing 31 of 42 pass attempts for 486 yards, five touchdown passes and no interceptions en route to being named the Offensive MVP for the game.<ref name="bahamasbowl">{{Cite web |date=December 24, 2014 |title=Popeye's Bahamas Bowl Postgame Notes |url=http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-footbl/recaps/122414aab.html |access-date=December 26, 2014 |publisher=Western Kentucky Hilltoppers}}</ref>

Overall, for the season Doughty completed 375 of 552 passing attempts for an [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS)-leading 4,830 yards (16th all-time in the FBS) and 49 touchdowns (a C-USA football single-season record and tied for sixth all-time in the FBS) and only ten interceptions, picking up a quarterback rating of 167.1.

===2015===
Doughty completed 388 of 540 passes for 5,055 yards with 48 touchdowns. His 5,055 yards in the 2015 season broke his previous record for most yards in a single season. From the beginning of the 2014 season to the end of the 2015 season he threw for 97 touchdowns, more than any other quarterback in a two-year span in NCAA history. Doughty finished his career in the top 25 in NCAA history for career passing yards, passing touchdowns, and completion percentage. Doughty played in the [[2016 East–West Shrine Game]] prior to the [[2016 NFL draft]].

===Toronto Argonauts===
In April 2018, Burks participated in [[The Spring League]], a developmental league to highlight players in front of NFL and CFL scouts. Burks was the first player signed to a professional team when he agreed to terms with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the CFL on April 16.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thespringleague.com/2018/04/17/congrats-rb-brandon-burks-1st-cfl-signing-spring-leagues-2018-season/|title=Home|access-date=2018-04-18|archive-date=2018-04-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418230825/https://www.thespringleague.com/2018/04/17/congrats-rb-brandon-burks-1st-cfl-signing-spring-leagues-2018-season/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.argonauts.ca/2018/04/16/argos-add-running-back-brandon-burks/| title = Argos add running back Brandon Burks - Toronto Argonauts| date = 16 April 2018}}</ref> Burks made a splash during the preseason, recreating a Spring League play against the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] where he reversed direction numerous times to avoid tackles for a loss before streaking for a large gain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thespringleague.com/2018/04/09/brandon-burks-electrifying-reverse/|title=Home}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.cfl.ca/2018/06/01/burks-jukes-and-runs-in-for-the-td/| title = Must Watch: Burks dazzles with first TD run - CFL.ca}}</ref> In the two preseason games, Burks had 13 carries for 69 yards, as well as two catches for 42 yards and a score. As a result, Burks was assigned to the practice roster after the preseason, but was promoted to the active roster for the team's week 4 game against Edmonton.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/ |title=Transactions - CFL.ca |access-date=2018-07-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831185325/https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/ |archive-date=2017-08-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also called up in weeks 6 and 15, handling reserve running back and returner duties in all three games, before being demoted back to the practice roster. Following a season ending injury to starting running back [[James Wilder Jr.]], and the trade of backup [[Martese Jackson]], Burks assumed the starting role as the Argos limped to a last place finish to the season. In eight games played, Burks produced 283 yards on 45 carries, 125 yards and a touchdown on 18 receptions, and 72 yards on four kick returns. He was released by the Argonauts on February 3, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Toronto born OL Jamal Campbell is staying home|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2020/02/03/toronto-born-ol-jamal-campbell-stays-home-argos-bring-back-knox/|publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]]|date=February 3, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==

===Freshman year===
During his first year at [[Penn State]], Bell played in seven games with twenty-three total tackles, fourteen solo tackles. In his first game as a [[Penn State Nittany Lions|Nittany Lion]] he recorded  two tackles one of them a solo tackle in a 45–7 win over [[Eastern Michigan]]. His best game statistically was vs [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]] on November 11 he recorded six tackles four of them solo in a win during the season finale.<ref name="ESPN">{{cite news |title = PSU's Brandon Bell Freshman highlights |work = ESPN.com |date = November 29, 2013 |url = http://www.espn.com/college-football/player/gamelog/_/id/552315/year/2013/brandon-bell |access-date = October 23, 2016 }}</ref>

===Sophomore year===
During the [[2014 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|2014 season]], Bell began getting a substantial increase of playing time. He started ten games for Penn State. Bell recorded his first college [[interception]] in a game against [[Rutgers]] and the next week vs [[UMass]] he had his first sack in a 48–7 win. Bell's best game of his career and the year was a thirteen tackle effort and also a sack in a 31-24 Double Over-Time loss to the [[Ohio State Buckeyes]]. Bell finished the year with a total of 43 tackles, two sacks and one interception in ten games.<ref name="ESPN"/>
<ref name="GOPSUSPORTS">{{cite news |title = Brandon Bell PSU bio |work = GoPSUsports.com |date = December 29, 2014 |url =http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandon_bell_857060.html |access-date = October 23, 2016 }}</ref>

===Junior year===
Bell set career highs with sacks and tackling during the 2015 campaign. Totaling 56 tackles and three and a half sacks Bell was one of Penn State's best defenders.  In the first game of the year Bell had one sack and seven tacks vs the [[Temple Owls]]. His best game of the year was a nine tackle performance in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] opener vs [[Rutgers]]. In his last game during his junior year, in the [[Taxslayer Bowl]] against [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]] he had eleven tackles in a compact fallen short when Penn State lost 24-17 after scoring fourteen unanswered points to pull within a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web |title = Brandon Bell - Collegian - PSU |date = August 29, 2016 |access-date = October 23, 2016 |url = http://www.collegian.psu.edu/football/article_f0e018c6-6e58-11e6-8f88-03ca36191b1c.html |publisher = COLLEGIAN }}</ref>

===Senior year===
Bell's first appearance as a senior was in the [[2016 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|season opener]] vs [[Kent State]] he recorded a tackle and an interception in a 33–13 win. The next week, he had nine tackles in a [[Sports Rivalry|rivalry]] game vs [[Pitt Panthers|Pitt]] in a 42–39 loss. During the final seconds of the game on a tackle on Pitt’s James Connor, Bell suffered a knee injury sidelining him for the next three weeks. Bell's best performance was a 19 tackle, one sack game vs the [[Ohio State Buckeyes]]. The Nittany Lions upset No. 2 Ohio State on a blocked FG attempt and ran it back 64 yards for the [[touchdown]]. The win put PSU in the [[AP Poll]] for the first time since 2011. There ranking in their Top 25 was No. 24.

On November 26, Bell recorded a tying-season high 18 tackles with 2 tackles for loss in a 45–12 Big Ten East clinching win over [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]]. And on December 3, [[2016 Big Ten Football Championship Game|2016 Big Ten Championship]] 13 tackles, one sack and a forced fumble.

'''Brandon Scott Aubrey''' (born March 14, 1995) is an American [[multi-sport athlete]] who plays as a [[placekicker]] for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He has also played professional [[association football]] as a [[center back]].

In 2017, Aubrey was drafted by [[Toronto FC]] of [[Major League Soccer]] and played for the club's [[Toronto FC II|reserve team]] before moving to [[Bethlehem Steel FC]]. He then switched to [[American football]] and played for the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL) in 2022 and 2023 before being signed by the Cowboys in 2023.

Since entering the NFL, Aubrey has emerged as one of the league's top placekickers. With a {{Percentage|112|127|1}} career field goal percentage, Aubrey ranks as the fifth-most accurate field goal kicker in NFL history,{{efn|Minimum 100 attempts. The only players with a higher career field goal percentage are [[Cameron Dicker]] ({{Percentage|128|137|1}}), [[Eddy Piñeiro]] ({{Percentage|139|155|1}}), [[Justin Tucker]] ({{Percentage|417|468|1}}), and [[Harrison Butker]] ({{Percentage|251|284|1}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Field Goal % Career Leaders (since 1938) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/fg_perc_career.htm |access-date=December 16, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>}} and he has been named an [[All-Pro]] in all three of his seasons thus far. Aubrey also holds the NFL record for the most career field goals made from 60 yards or longer, with six.

==Soccer career==
===Youth career===
Aubrey played youth soccer with Dallas Texans SC. He captained the '95 team from 2008 to 2010 and during his time with the team, they won five State Cup titles, were regional finalist in 2009, were Classic League grand champions in 2009 and 2010, were 2009 Premiere League West champions, and also won the 2008 Gothia Cup (Sweden), the 2009 Dallas Cup, the 2009 Disney Showcase, and the 2009 Tivoli Cup (Denmark).<ref name="Youth">{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2018 |title=Brandon Aubrey Notre Dame profile |url=https://fightingirish.com/roster/brandon-aubrey/ |access-date=October 15, 2023 |website=Notre Dame Athletics}}</ref> He was named to USSDA All-Select Team in 2011–12 and helped them win the U17 Disney Showcase twice.<ref name="Youth" />

Aubrey played his high school freshman and sophomore seasons at [[Dallas Jesuit]] in [[Dallas, Texas]] in 2010 and 2011, where he was named Honorable Mention All-District as a freshman and First Team All-District as a sophomore.<ref name="Youth" />

===College career===
Aubrey played four years of [[College soccer in the United States|college soccer]] at the [[University of Notre Dame]] between 2013 and 2016, wherein 2016 Aubrey was named NSCAA Third Team All-American, NSCAA First Team All-South Region, First Team All-ACC, and NSCAA Academic All-American. The 2013 team won a National Championship. <ref name="Youth" />

===Professional career===
====Toronto FC====
Aubrey was selected in the first round (21st overall) of the [[2017 MLS SuperDraft]] by [[Toronto FC]].<ref name="mlssoccer">{{cite web|url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2017/01/14/toronto-fc-surprised-see-highly-touted-brandon-aubrey-fall-no-21|title=Toronto FC "surprised" to see highly touted Brandon Aubrey fall to No. 21|work=[[Major League Soccer]]|first=James|last=Grossi|date=January 14, 2017}}</ref> He was loaned to the second team, [[Toronto FC II]], in the [[USL Championship|USL]] for the 2017 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Villella |first=Evan |date=January 10, 2018 |title=Steel add Brandon Aubrey to squad |url=https://www.brotherlygame.com/2018/1/10/16873942/bethlehem-steel-sign-brandon-aubrey |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=Brotherly Game}}</ref> Aubrey made his professional debut on March 25, 2017, starting for Toronto FC II against the [[Phoenix Rising FC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aubrey profile |url=https://www.osdbsports.com/nfl/players/brandon-aubrey/110e6fe0-1c34-11ee-8294-af17faac15de |url-status=dead |website=OSBD Sports |access-date=December 24, 2023 |archive-date=December 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231224125838/https://www.osdbsports.com/nfl/players/brandon-aubrey/110e6fe0-1c34-11ee-8294-af17faac15de }}</ref>

====Bethlehem Steel FC====
[[File:CINvBST 2018-06-13 - Brandon Aubrey (43565763110) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Aubrey in 2018|left]]
In January 2018, Aubrey signed with USL club [[Bethlehem Steel FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.philadelphiaunion.com/post/2018/01/10/bethlehem-steel-fc-sign-defender-brandon-aubrey|title=Bethlehem Steel FC Sign Defender Brandon Aubrey|website=[[Philadelphia Union]]|date=January 10, 2018|access-date=January 27, 2018}}</ref> He was released by the club at the end of the 2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bethlehemsteelfc.com/news_article/show/968765 |title=Bethlehem Steel FC Announces Roster Moves with 2019 in Mind |access-date=November 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181121204200/https://www.bethlehemsteelfc.com/news_article/show/968765 |archive-date=November 21, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==American football career==
After being released from [[Bethlehem Steel FC]] in 2018, Aubrey decided to use his degree from [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]] to become a software engineer. While watching an NFL game on TV in 2019, a [[placekicker]] missed a field goal and Aubrey's wife told him: "You could do that."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunau |first=Casey |date=September 8, 2023 |title=MLS to NFL: Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey completes 6-year journey |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/mls-to-nfl-dallas-cowboys-kicker-brandon-aubrey-completes-6-year-journey |access-date=September 15, 2023 |website=MLSSoccer.com}}</ref> From 2019 to 2022, Aubrey worked with former [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]] kicker and kicking coach Brian Egan three times a week.<ref name="x328">{{cite web | last=Eisenberg | first=Jeff | title=From 9-to-5 to the NFL: Brandon Aubrey's incredible journey to the Dallas Cowboys | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=December 20, 2023 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/from-9-to-5-to-the-nfl-brandon-aubreys-incredible-journey-to-the-dallas-cowboys-152808391.html | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref>

===Birmingham Stallions===
====2022 season====
{{See also|2022 Birmingham Stallions season}}

Aubrey was drafted as a placekicker by the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] in the [[2022 USFL draft]] and made his debut as a professional [[American football]] player on April 16, 2022.<ref name="m653">{{cite web | last=Shepkowski | first=Nick | title=Notre Dame futboler drafted by USFL team | website=Fighting Irish Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=February 24, 2022 | url=https://fightingirishwire.usatoday.com/2022/02/24/notre-dame-soccer-football-usfl-draft-aubrey-coney/ | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> Aubrey played in all 10 games making 18 of his 22 field goal attempts (81.8%) and 22 of his 24 extra-point attempts (91.7%), which both led the league. He also had a league-leading 55 kickoffs with a 66.5-yard average. On June 16, Aubrey was named to the inaugural All-[[United States Football League (2022)|USFL]] Team.<ref>{{cite web |title=2022 ALL-USFL TEAM SPECIAL TEAMS UNVEILED |url=https://www.theusfl.com/the-usfl/2022-all-usfl-team-special-teams-unveiled |website=The USFL.com |access-date=September 17, 2023}}</ref> After winning the Divisional Finals 31–17, the Stallions beat the [[Philadelphia Stars (2022)|Philadelphia Stars]] in the [[2022 USFL championship game]] 33–30. In the game, Aubrey was successful on two of his three attempts with a 42-yard long and made three of his four extra-point tries.<ref>{{cite web |title=Birmingham Stallions Vs Philadelphia Stars – July 3, 2022 |url=https://www.theusfl.com/championship-birmingham-stallions-vs-philadelphia-stars-jul-03-2022-game-boxscore-43 |website=The USFL.com |access-date=September 17, 2023}}</ref>

====2023 season====
{{See also|2023 Birmingham Stallions season}}

Aubrey re-signed with the Stallions for the 2023 season. He finished the season 14-for-15 (93.3%) on field goals with a 49-yard long while also finishing 35-for-35 (100.0%) on extra points, which led the league. Aubrey also added a league-leading 57 kickoffs and six touchbacks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former MLS draft pick, USFL player battling to become Cowboys' kicker for 2023 season |url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/sports/nfl/cowboys/former-mls-draft-pick-usfl-player-brandon-aubrey-battling-become-dallas-cowboys-kicker/287-178d0403-2f70-4c4e-9659-e11cfccee56f |website=WFAA.com |date=August 6, 2023 |access-date=September 17, 2023}}</ref> The Stallions finished the regular season with an 8–2 record, making them the champions of the South Division.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 USFL DIVISION STANDINGS |url=https://www.foxsports.com/usfl/standings |website=FoxSports.com |access-date=September 17, 2023}}</ref> After winning the Divisional Finals against [[New Orleans Breakers (2022)|New Orleans Breakers]] 47–22, the Stallions made it to their second-straight [[2023 USFL championship game|USFL championship game]]. During the game, Aubrey made all four of his extra-point attempts to help the Stallions win 28–12.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Orleans Breaks Vs Birmingham Stallions – June 25, 2023 |url=https://www.theusfl.com/playoffs-new-orleans-breakers-vs-birmingham-stallions-jun-25-2023-game-boxscore-88 |website=TheUSFL.com |access-date=September 17, 2023}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===

====2023 season====
[[File:Brandon Aubrey 10 1 2023.jpg|thumb|right|Aubrey with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in 2023]]
The Stallions terminated Aubrey's contract on July 3, 2023,<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStallions |title=Contract Terminated / Signing with NFL Team |number=1676022105899409408 |date=July 3, 2023 |access-date=July 5, 2023}}</ref> allowing him to sign with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] three days later.<ref>{{cite news |last=Harris |first=Nick |title=Cowboys Sign Kicker Brandon Aubrey From USFL |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-sign-kicker-brandon-aubrey-from-usfl |website=DallasCowboys.com |date=July 6, 2023 |access-date=July 6, 2023}}</ref>

In his NFL debut, Aubrey connected on both of his field goal attempts with a long of 38, and made four of his five extra-point attempts in the 40–0 shutout road victory over the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants - September 10th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309100nyg.htm |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 8 43–20 victory over the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Aubrey accounted for 11 points, including a 58-yard field goal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Dallas Cowboys - October 29th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310290dal.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=November 1, 2023 |title=Bengals QB Joe Burrow, Eagles QB Jalen Hurts highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-qb-joe-burrow-eagles-qb-jalen-hurts-highlight-players-of-the-week |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> as well as NFC Special Teams Player of the Month for October.<ref name="s368">{{cite web | last=Gordon | first=Grant | title=Dolphins WR Tyreek Hill, Eagles WR A.J. Brown highlight October Players of the Month | website=NFL.com | date=November 2, 2023 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/dolphins-wr-tyreek-hill-eagles-wr-a-j-brown-highlight-october-players-of-the-mon | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Aubrey set an NFL record for most consecutive field goals made to start a career with his 19th made attempt during the 28–23 road loss,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles - November 5th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311050phi.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> beating the previous holder [[Travis Coons]].<ref name="g515">{{cite web | last=Podell | first=Garrett | title=Cowboys rookie kicker Brandon Aubrey breaks NFL record for most consecutive made field goals to start a career | website=CBSSports.com | date=November 5, 2023 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-rookie-kicker-brandon-aubrey-breaks-nfl-record-for-most-consecutive-made-field-goals-to-start-a-career/ | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> During a Week 14 33–13 victory over the Eagles, Aubrey became the first kicker in NFL history to make two field goals from 59+ yards in the same game (59, 60).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys - December 10th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202312100dal.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He would then be named [[NBC Sunday Night Football|''Sunday Night Football'']] Player of the Game, along with [[Dak Prescott]] and [[Stephon Gilmore]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys' Aubrey hits from 60 and 59 yards while extending record to 30 straight FGs to start career |url=https://apnews.com/article/cowboys-brandon-aubrey-field-goal-streak-c1ee6b8c0b677e8662281ad1dc468592 |website=AP News |date=December 11, 2023 |access-date=December 12, 2023}}</ref> For his performance, Aubrey earned his second NFC Special Teams Player of the Week award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=December 13, 2023 |title=New York QBs Zach Wilson, Tommy DeVito highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-york-qbs-zach-wilson-tommy-devito-highlight-players-of-the-week |access-date=December 13, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

In the 2023 season, Aubrey converted 49 of 52 extra point attempts and 36 of 38 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aubrey 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AubrBr00.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2024 season====
On August 17, 2024, Aubrey kicked a 66-yard field goal in a preseason game against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], unofficially [[Field Goal#Longest field goal records|tying the NFL record]].<ref name="r042">{{cite web | last=Archer | first=Todd | title=Aubrey fires up Cowboys with 66-yard field goal | website=ESPN.com | date=August 18, 2024 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/40902179/brandon-aubrey-fires-cowboys-66-yard-fg-preseason-win | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> During the season-opening 33–17 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]], Aubrey nearly kicked another 66-yard field goal, which would have officially tied the NFL record, but the Cowboys were penalized for a delay of game penalty, negating the field goal.<ref name="q741">{{cite web | last=Podell | first=Garrett | title=What kept Cowboys' Brandon Aubrey's 66-yard FG from being snapped on time? Why not from 71 yards? This is why | website=CBSSports.com | date=September 8, 2024 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-brandon-aubrey-nearly-ties-nfl-record-for-longest-field-goal-almost-tried-from-71/amp/ | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Cleveland Browns - September 8th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202409080cle.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Aubrey kicked a 65-yard field goal, officially breaking [[Brett Maher (gridiron football)|Brett Maher]]'s record for the longest made field goal in Cowboys franchise history, along with being the second-longest field goal in NFL history.<ref name="o711">{{cite web | last=Leslie | first=Mike | title=Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey drills a monster 65-yard field goal to get Dallas on the board | website=WFAA | date=September 22, 2024 | url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/sports/nfl/cowboys/cowboys-kicker-brandon-aubrey-drills-65-yard-field-goal-dallas-baltimore-ravens/287-77633698-6955-49f0-a1e4-976db4f0c971 | access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> The Cowboys went on to lose 28–25.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Dallas Cowboys - September 22nd, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202409220dal.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During Week 16 against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on [[NBC Sunday Night Football|''Sunday Night Football'']], Aubrey went 4/4 on field goals and 3/3 on 50+ yard kicks in the narrow 26–24 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys - December 22nd, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202412220dal.htm |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baca |first=Michael |date=December 24, 2024 |title=Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, Panthers RB Chuba Hubbard highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2024-week-16-jonathan-taylor |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

In the 2024 season, Aubrey converted all 30 extra point attempts and 40 of 47 field goals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aubrey 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AubrBr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2025 season====
During Week 2, Aubrey scored 16 points as the Cowboys defeated the [[2025 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] 40–37 in overtime. He made all four of his field goals and all four of his extra points. Aubrey's four field goals included a 64-yard field goal at the end of regulation and the 46-yard game winner in overtime. This made him the only NFL player with multiple successful 64+ yard field goals.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-15 |title=Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey is coming for GOAT status -- and an NFL record may be weeks away |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-kicker-brandon-aubrey-is-coming-for-goat-status-and-an-nfl-record-may-be-weeks-away/ |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> Aubrey also became the first player in NFL history to convert a game-tying field goal with no time remaining in the fourth quarter and a game-winning field goal with no time remaining in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Patra|first=Kevin|title=Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer: We would have tried Brandon Aubrey's game-tying FG from '70-ish'|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cowboys-brian-schottenheimer-we-would-have-tried-brandon-aubrey-s-game-tying-fg-from-70-ish|work=NFL|date=September 15, 2025|access-date=September 15, 2025}}</ref> He was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=2025-09-17 |title=Brandon Aubrey's big day nets him NFC special teams player of the week |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/brandon-aubreys-big-day-nets-him-nfc-special-teams-player-of-the-week |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> During Week 7, Aubrey became the first NFL kicker in NFL history with five made field goals of 60-plus yards.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Podell |first1=Garrett |title=Cowboys' Brandon Aubrey becomes first kicker in NFL history with five made field goals of 60-plus yards |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-brandon-aubrey-becomes-first-kicker-in-nfl-history-with-five-made-field-goals-of-60-plus-yards/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=22 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251022142017/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-brandon-aubrey-becomes-first-kicker-in-nfl-history-with-five-made-field-goals-of-60-plus-yards/ |archive-date=October 22, 2025 |date=October 19, 2025}}</ref>

During Week 12 against the Eagles, Aubrey made a 42-yard field goal as time expired, helping the Cowboys cap off a 24–21 comeback victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2025 |title=Dak Prescott rallies Cowboys from 21 down to beat Eagles 24-21 after breaking Tony Romo's record |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401772890 |access-date=November 26, 2025 |work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Detroit Lions]], Aubrey had five field goals in the 44–30 road loss, including three that were from a distance of 55 yards or more, with the longest being from 63 yards. He broke an NFL record for most field goals in a game from a distance of 55 yards or further while also breaking the record for most field goals of 60 yards or more in an NFL season, with three. Not only that, but Aubrey set a new personal record for most career 60 yards or longer field goals, with his 63-yard field goal in this game being the sixth of his career.<ref>{{Citeweb|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-kicker-brandon-aubrey-nfl-records-field-goal/?utm_source=firefox-newtab-en-us|title=Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey breaks two NFL records in one game after smashing 63-yard field goal vs. Lions|last=Breech|first=John|date=December 5, 2025|accessdate=December 5, 2025}}</ref>

====2026 season====
Designated as a [[restricted free agent]] in the 2026 offseason, the Cowboys placed a second-round tender on Aubrey on March 7, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cowboys-place-second-round-tender-on-kicker-brandon-aubrey|work=NFL.com|title=Cowboys place second-round, $5.76 million tender on kicker Brandon Aubrey |date=March 7, 2026|first=Grant|last=Gordon}}</ref> 

On April 20, 2026, Aubrey and the Cowboys agreed to a record-breaking four-year deal worth $28 million ($7 million per year) with $20 million guarantee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-20 |title=Brandon Aubrey, Cowboys Agree To Record-Setting Contract Extension |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/onsi/brandon-aubrey-dallas-cowboys-agree-nfl-record-setting-contract-extension |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=Dallas Cowboys On SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Machota |first=Jon |date=2026-04-20 |title=Cowboys, Brandon Aubrey reach 4-year, $28 million deal: Source |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7212576/2026/04/20/cowboys-brandon-aubrey-contract-extension-kicker/ |access-date=2026-04-20 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
Facyson signed with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] as an undrafted free agent in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/virginia-tech/virginia-tech-senior-brandon-facyson-plays-with-guts-in-every-sense/article_3b730bf6-3553-5f39-a4ac-c3a2a453bfcf.html|title=Virginia Tech senior Brandon Facyson plays with guts, in every sense|first=MIKE BARBER Richmond|last=Times-Dispatch|website=Richmond Times-Dispatch}}</ref> Facyson finished his rookie season with 3 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]], playing in 15 games as well as both playoff games for the Chargers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandonfacyson/2560719/gamelogs?season=2018|title=NFL Players | Past & Current NFL Players}}</ref> In Facyson's second season he made his first professional start in a Week 2 loss to the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandonfacyson/2560719/gamelogs?season=2019|title=NFL Players | Past & Current NFL Players}}</ref> Facyson finished his second season starting 4 games, playing in all 16, and recording 41 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FacyBr00.htm|title=Brandon Facyson Stats|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

Facyson was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on November 7, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Los Angeles Chargers place CB Brandon Facyson on COVID-19 list |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30274296/los-angeles-chargers-place-cb-brandon-facyson-covid-19-list |website=ESPN.com |date=November 7, 2020 |accessdate=December 9, 2020}}</ref> and activated on November 25.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chargers' Brandon Facyson: Back from COVID list |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chargers-brandon-facyson-back-from-covid-list/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=November 25, 2020 |accessdate=December 9, 2020}}</ref>

Facyson re-signed with the Chargers on March 19, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Welcome Back, Brandon Facyson and Michael Badgley! |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/michael-badgley-brandon-facyson-resign-with-bolts |website=Chargers.com |date=March 19, 2021 |access-date=March 21, 2021 |archive-date=March 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210321190928/https://www.chargers.com/news/michael-badgley-brandon-facyson-resign-with-bolts |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2021, and re-signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Announce Practice Squad and Claim Two Players Off Waivers|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/practice-squad-2021|website=Chargers.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

On August 28, 2024, Facyson was placed on injured reserve, and released a few days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders claim DT Jonah Laulu and S Thomas Harper|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-claim-dt-jonah-laulu-and-s-thomas-harper-waive-byron-young-mj-devonshire|website=Raiders.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

'''Brandon Dillon''' (born April 30, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Marian Knights football|Marian Knights]] and has been a member of the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[New York Jets]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Vegas Vipers]], and [[Washington Commanders]].

==Early life==
Dillon grew up in [[Bringhurst, Indiana]] and attended [[Carroll High School (Flora, Indiana)|Carroll High School]] in nearby [[Flora, Indiana]], where he played baseball, basketball, and football. In football, Dillon was a four-year starter on both offense and defense and was named All-Area by the ''[[Kokomo Tribune]]'' twice and was a two-time Class A All-State selection, as well as all-area by the ''[[Lafayette Journal & Courier]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/high-school/2014/12/24/rensselaer-duo-named-jc-small-school-players-year/20872541/|title=Rensselaer duo named J&C Small School Players of the Year }}</ref> He was also a two-time All-Area selection in basketball.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kokomotribune.com/sports/football-marian-s-dillon-signs-with-minnesota/article_7b09cf9a-6967-11e9-8314-1ffdc29ad4c6.html|title=FOOTBALL: Marian's Dillon signs with Minnesota|work=[[Kokomo Tribune]]|date=April 27, 2019|access-date=September 9, 2019}}</ref> Despite being recruited by [[Bowling Green Falcons football|Bowling Green]], [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo]] and [[Ohio Bobcats football|Ohio University]] to join their programs as a preferred walk-on, Dillon opted to enroll at nearby [[Marian University (Indiana)|Marian University]], an [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thedickinsonpress.com/sports/football/4039206-More-than-5000-will-be-a-crowd-for-Vikings-rookie-tight-end|title=More than 5,000 will be a crowd for Vikings rookie tight end|first=Chris|last=Thomasson|work=[[The Dickinson Press]]|publisher=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=September 9, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
Dillon was a member [[Marian University (Indiana)#Football|Marian Knights]] for four seasons and was a freshman when the team won the 2015 [[NAIA Football National Championship|NAIA National Championship]]. As a senior, Dillon caught 35 passes for 603 yards and five touchdowns and was named a first-team NAIA All-American. After the season he was the only NAIA player to be invited to participate in the 2017 [[NFLPA Collegiate Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fox59.com/2019/04/13/colts-local-pro-day-major-audition-for-marians-brandon-dillon-purdues-jake-thieneman-others/|title=Colts' local Pro Day major audition for Marian's Brandon Dillon, Purdue's Jake Thieneman, others|first=Mike|last=Chappell|website=Fox59.com|date=April 13, 2019|access-date=September 8, 2019}}</ref> Dillon finished his collegiate career with 105 receptions for 1,661 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns in 42 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/north/gallery/minnesota-vikings-2019-undrafted-free-agents-043019|title=Vikings 2019 undrafted free agent capsules|website=[[Fox Sports North]]|date=April 30, 2019|access-date=September 8, 2019}}</ref>
