'''Brandon Aiyuk''' ({{respell|EYE|yook}}; born March 17, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Sierra College|Sierra College Wolverines]] and [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the first round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Aiyuk was born in [[Rocklin, California]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2020 |title='It Was Already Written': Rocklin Native Brandon Aiyuk Tweets Picture Of Himself In 49ers Gear At 4-Years-Old |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/brandon-aiyuk-rocklin-49ers-nfl-draft-sierra-college-arizona-state/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |work=CBS - Sacramento}}</ref> and is of [[Cameroon]]ian descent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solms |first=Leonard |date=October 3, 2023 |title=Brandon Aiyuk shows why he's the heartbeat of the 49ers offense |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/38554482/cameroon-brandon-aiyuk-shows-why-heartbeat-49ers-offense |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Growing up in [[Reno, Nevada]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Jarah |date=February 11, 2024 |title=Nevada native, San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk ready for Super Bowl 58 |url=https://www.ktnv.com/news/big-game-in-vegas/nevada-native-san-francisco-49ers-wide-receiver-brandon-aiyuk-ready-for-super-bowl-58 |access-date=February 17, 2024 |work=Channel 13 Las Vegas News KTNV}}</ref> Aiyuk attended [[Robert McQueen High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krajeewski |first=Jan |date=October 4, 2017 |title=McQueen High alum Brandon Aiyuk jumps onto recruiting radar at Sierra College |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/10/04/aiyuk-shines-sierra-college-one-several-former-prep-standouts/734231001/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]]}}</ref> There, he played wide receiver and defensive back and also returned kicks for the Lancers and was named first-team All-Northern Nevada and honorable mention All-State as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krajeewski |first=Jan |date=December 7, 2015 |title=American Family Insurance ALL-USA Northern football |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/football-am-fam-insurance-allnorth-div-i-team?utm_content |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=[[USA Today|USATodayHSS.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==

===Sierra College===
====2016 season====
[[File:Brandon Aiyuk - Sierra College Football.jpg|thumb|Aiyuk in 2016|left]]
Aiyuk began his [[college football]] career at [[Sierra College]] in [[Rocklin, California|Rocklin]]. As a freshman, he caught 29 passes for 573 yards and five touchdowns for the Wolverines and was named All-NorCal Conference.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 15, 2016 |title=Aiyuk named All-conference at Sierra College |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/2016/11/15/aiyuk-named-all-conference-sierra-college/93941498/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]]}}</ref>

====2017 season====
Aiyuk was named a Junior College [[All-American]] as a sophomore after recording 60 receptions for 960 yards and 14 touchdowns while also returning 11 kickoffs for 418 yards and two touchdowns and 14 punts for 313 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Little |first=Josh |date=December 15, 2017 |title=McQueen alum Aiyuk named a JC All-American |url=https://www.kolotv.com/content/sports/McQueen-alum-Aiyuk-named-a-JC-All-American-464491863.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311133447/https://www.kolotv.com/content/sports/McQueen-alum-Aiyuk-named-a-JC-All-American-464491863.html |archive-date=March 11, 2018 |access-date=October 30, 2020 |website=KOLOTV.com}}</ref> He finished his junior college career with 2,499 all-purpose yards and 21 touchdowns. Aiyuk was named First-Team All-NorCal Conference and All-State after the season.

Aiyuk committed to transfer to [[Arizona State University]] for the final two years of his [[NCAA]] eligibility over offers from Colorado State, Kansas, Tennessee, and Alabama.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Karpman |first=Chris |date=February 8, 2018 |title=Sun Devils land Brandon Aiyuk despite interest from Alabama |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona-state/Article/Sun-Devils-land-Brandon-Aiyuk-despite-interest-from-Alabama-114845478/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref> He chose Arizona State because it was one of the few schools that recruited him to play wide receiver; others recruited him as only a return specialist or planned to move him to the defensive side of the ball.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gardner |first=Michelle |date=September 11, 2019 |title=ASU offered Brandon Aiyuk the chance to play WR so he took it |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/asu/2019/09/11/arizona-state-offered-brandon-aiyuk-chance-play-wr-so-he-took/2279365001/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[The Arizona Republic]]}}</ref>

===Arizona State===
====2018 season====
In his first year with the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Sun Devils]], Aiyuk had 33 catches for 474 yards and three touchdowns with an additional 381 total return yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |date=October 18, 2019 |title=Meet the Prospect: Fast-rising receiver Brandon Aiyuk and the art of YAC |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1302255/2019/10/18/meet-the-prospect-fast-rising-receiver-prospect-brandon-aiyuk-and-the-art-of-yac/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rudner |first=Jacob |date=August 28, 2019 |title=Arizona State season preview: WR |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona-state/Article/ASU-football-preview-wide-receivers-Brandon-Aiyuk-Frank-Darby-134873142/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

====2019 season====
[[File:Brandon Aiyuk.jpg|thumb|Aiyuk in 2019]]
Aiyuk was named first-team preseason [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] going into his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pauline |first=Tony |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Arizona State Sun Devils: Benjamin, Aiyuk, Cabral headline players to watch |url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/arizona-state-sun-devils-summer-grades/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=ProFootballNetwork.com}}</ref> He was named the Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Week after catching seven passes for 196 yards and three touchdowns in a 38–34 victory over [[2019 Washington State Cougars football team|Washington State]] on October 12, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2019 |title=Arizona State's Brandon Aiyuk earns Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Week honors after career receiving day |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/arizona-states-brandon-aiyuk-earns-193014464.html |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|via=Pac-12 Network}}</ref> Aiyuk was also named the conference Special Teams Player of the Week after posting 44 kickoff return yards and 76 punt return yards, 63 of which came on his first return for a touchdown at ASU, against [[2019 Oregon State Beavers football team|Oregon State]] on November 16. He also had a career-high 10 receptions for 173 yards and a touchdown in the game and his 293 all-purpose yards were the fifth-most in a single game in school history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuebel |first=Tom |date=November 18, 2019 |title=Brandon Aiyuk wins 3rd Pac-12 special teams award for ASU this year |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2161789/brandon-aiyuk-wins-3rd-pac-12-special-teams-award-asu-year/ |access-date=November 20, 2019 |website=[[KMVP-FM|ArizonaSports.com]]}}</ref>

Aiyuk finished the season with 65 receptions for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns, returned 14 punts for 226 yards and a touchdown and 14 kickoffs for 446 yards, and was named first-team All-Pac-12 as both a wide receiver and as a return specialist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Booth |first=Trevor |date=December 10, 2019 |title=Brandon Aiyuk to skip ASU's bowl game |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona-state/Article/ASU-football-Brandon-Aiyuk-Eno-Benjamin-Michael-Turk-Jermayne-Lole-Kobe-Williams-Pac-12-honors-Herm-Edwards--140140484/ |access-date=December 18, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

===2020 season===
[[File:Brandon Aiyuk (50730673553) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Aiyuk in 2020]]
Aiyuk was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the first round (25th overall) in the [[2020 NFL draft]], acquired in a trade with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] for San Francisco's 31st ([[Jeff Gladney]]), 117th ([[D. J. Wonnum|D.J. Wonnum]]) and 176th ([[K. J. Osborn|K.J. Osborn]]) picks.<ref>{{Cite news |last=White |first=R.J. |date=April 23, 2020 |title=2020 NFL Draft grades: 49ers get a 'B+' for trading up for Brandon Aiyuk at No. 25 overall |work=[[CBS Sports]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/news/2020-nfl-draft-grades-49ers-get-a-b-for-trading-up-for-brandon-aiyuk-at-no-25-overall/ |access-date=April 23, 2020}}</ref> On June 26, 2020, he signed a four-year, $12.5 million contract with a $6.6 million signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Posey |first=Kyle |date=June 26, 2020 |title=49ers sign first-round pick Brandon Aiyuk to a four-year deal |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2020/6/26/21304850/49ers-sign-first-round-pick-brandon-aiyuk-to-a-four-year-deal |access-date=June 26, 2020 |website=Niners Nation |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

On August 23, Aiyuk sustained a hamstring injury in [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]], resulting in him being inactive for the season-opener.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maiocco |first=Matt |date=September 13, 2020 |title=Rookie Aiyuk inactive for 49ers in opener vs. Cardinals |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/49ers-inactives-brandon-aiyuk-out-vs-cardinals-season-opener |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=RSN}}</ref> Aiyuk made his NFL debut during Week 2 against the [[New York Jets]] and recorded two receptions for 21 yards in the 31–13 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at New York Jets – September 20th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009200nyj.htm |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the next game against the [[New York Giants]], Aiyuk recorded 101 all-purpose yards and his first career rushing touchdown during the 36–9 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at New York Giants – September 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009270nyg.htm |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Aiyuk became the franchise's first wide receiver since 1970 to have a rushing touchdown be their first career score.<ref>{{Cite web |title=49ers' Aiyuk achieved rare feat with first career NFL TD |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/49ers-brandon-aiyuk-achieved-rare-feat-first-career-touchdown |access-date=October 8, 2020 |website=RSN}}</ref> During Week 4 against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football]]'', he had a 38-yard rushing touchdown in the 20–25 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at San Francisco 49ers – October 4th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010040sfo.htm |access-date=October 8, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] }}</ref> Aiyuk became the first wide receiver since the |access-date=October 8, 2020 |work=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref>

During Week 7, Aiyuk recorded his first career game with 100+ receiving yards, catching six passes for 115 yards, in a 33–6 road victory over the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at New England Patriots – October 25th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010250nwe.htm |access-date=October 30, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-trent-williams-brandon-aiyuuk-deebo-samuel-on-reserve-covid-19-list |website=49ers.com |date=November 4, 2020 |access-date=December 6, 2020}}</ref> and was === 2021 season ===
Aiyuk played in all 17 regular-season games with 16 starts for the 49ers, the exception being a Week 1 win against the [[2021 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] where he only contributed a punt return for seven yards. He finished the season with 56 receptions for 826 yards and five touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aiyuk 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AiyuBr00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

=== 2022 season ===
In Week 17 against the [[2022 Las Vegas Raiders season|Las Vegas Raiders]], Aiyuk had nine receptions for 101 yards and a touchdown, as well as a single carry for 16 yards, during the 37–34 overtime road victory.<ref>{{cite web | title=Stats and Facts from the 49ers New Year's Day Victory vs. Raiders | website=49ers.com| date=2023-01-02 | url=https://www.49ers.com/news/stats-and-facts-from-the-49ers-new-year-s-day-victory-vs-raiders | access-date=2026-03-22}}</ref> For the season, Aiyuk played in 17 games and starts, recording 78 receptions for 1,015 yards and a career-high eight touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aiyuk 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AiyuBr00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

=== 2023 season ===
On April 28, 2023, the 49ers picked up the fifth-year option of Aiyuk's rookie contract.<ref>{{cite news |last=Madson |first=Kyle |date=April 28, 2023 |title=Report: 49ers to pick up 5th-year option on WR Brandon Aiyuk |url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/2023/04/28/brandon-aiyuk-contract-5th-year-option-49ers/ |accessdate=November 16, 2023 |work=Niners Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> During the season opener against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Aiyuk had eight receptions for 129 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–7 road victory, earning NFC Offensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |author=Gordon, Grant |date=September 13, 2023 |title=Dolphins QB Tua Tagovailoa, 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2023-week-1-tua-tagovailoa-brandon-aiyuk |access-date=March 22, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], he injured his shoulder on his first catch of the game. Despite continuing play, Aiyuk was designated as inactive for their Week 3 match against the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dubow |first=Josh |date=September 21, 2023 |title=49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk will miss game against Giants with shoulder injury |url=https://apnews.com/article/nfl-49ers-brandon-aiyuk-f8078323bcaa6310ac8a756be93dbbc5 |access-date=September 25, 2023 |work=AP News}}</ref> During a Week 4 victory over the [[Arizona Cardinals]], he had six receptions for 148 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers - October 1st, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310010sfo.htm |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In a Week 11 victory over the Buccaneers, he had five receptions for 156 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at San Francisco 49ers - November 19th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311190sfo.htm |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Aiyuk started in all 16 games he played in. He had seven total games going over 100 receiving yards. He finished with 75 receptions for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aiyuk 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AiyuBr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 18, 2024|website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> and earned his first career [[2023 All-Pro Team|All-Pro]] selection as a second-team wide receiver.

During the NFC Championship Game against the Lions, Aiyuk had a receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship - Detroit Lions at San Francisco 49ers - January 28th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401280sfo.htm |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the third quarter of the game, he recorded a 51-yard reception off a pass that was deflected off of [[Kindle Vildor]]'s helmet that helped get the 49ers into scoring position.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Tyler |date=January 29, 2024 |title=49ers' Brandon Aiyuk makes sensational catch off Lions defender's helmet, sets up key TD in NFC title-game win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/49ers-brandon-aiyuk-makes-sensational-catch-off-lions-defenders-helmet-sets-up-key-td-in-nfc-title-game-win/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |work=CBS Sports}}</ref> In [[Super Bowl LVIII]], Aiyuk had three receptions for 49 yards in the 25–22 overtime loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVIII - San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 11th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202402110kan.htm |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

=== 2024 season ===
On August 30, 2024, Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=49ers Sign WR Brandon Aiyuk to Four-Year Extension|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-wr-brandon-aiyuk-to-four-year-extension|website=49ers.com|date=August 30, 2024|access-date=August 30, 2024}}</ref> During Week 5 against the Cardinals, he had eight receptions for 147 yards in the narrow 24–23 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers - October 6th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410060sfo.htm |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Chiefs, Aiyuk tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]]. He was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Shook |first=Nick |title=49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk out for rest of 2024 season after suffering torn ACL, MCL vs. Chiefs |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/49ers-wr-brandon-aiyuk-out-for-rest-of-2024-season-torn-acl-mcl-chiefs |access-date=October 21, 2024 |work=NFL.com |date=October 21, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Place Aiyuk on IR, Promote Anderson to 53-Man Roster and More Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-aiyuk-on-ir-promote-anderson-to-53-man-roster-and-more-moves|website=49ers.com|date=October 23, 2024|access-date=October 23, 2024}}</ref>

Aiyuk finished the 2024 season with 25 receptions for 374 yards in seven games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Aiyuk 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AiyuBr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2025 season ===
On July 18, 2025, Aiyuk was placed on the [[physically unable to perform|PUP]] list as he worked his way back from the knee injuries that he had suffered the previous October.<ref>{{cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=July 18, 2025 |title=Ricky Pearsall, Brandon Aiyuk land on 49ers’ PUP list |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/ricky-pearsall-brandon-aiyuk-land-on-49ers-pup-list |access-date=March 22, 2026 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

On November 21, 2025, it was reported that the 49ers voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation. Aiyuk told the [[NFL Players Association]] (NFLPA) he was not interested in filing a grievance.<ref> {{Cite news |last=Russini |first=Dianna |last2=Silver |first2=Michael |date=2025-11-25 |title=49ers preparing for stunning split with star receiver Brandon Aiyuk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6826885/2025/11/21/brandon-aiyuk-49ers-news-contract-guaranteed-money-release/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On December 13, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on their reserve/left squad list.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wagoner |first=Nick |date=December 13, 2025 |title=49ers place Brandon Aiyuk on reserve/left team list |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47296496/49ers-place-brandon-aiyuk-reserve-left-team-list |access-date=March 22, 2026 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Aiyuk married Rochelle Searight in April 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.com/san-francisco-49ers-player-brandon-aiyuk-marries-rochelle-searight-11714550|work=People.com|title=San Francisco 49ers Player Brandon Aiyuk Marries Longtime Partner Rochelle Searight: 'The Culmination of Our Love'|first=Rachel|last=Raposas|date=April 14, 2025|accessdate=July 29, 2025}}</ref> They started dating in 2018 while attending Arizona State University, and their son was born in September 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.com/who-is-rochelle-searight-brandon-aiyuk-8575079|work=People.com|title=Who Is Brandon Aiyuk's Girlfriend? All About Rochelle Searight|first=Haley|last=Van Horn|date=February 12, 2024|accessdate=July 29, 2025}}</ref>

On December 20, 2025, Aiyuk posted a video of himself speeding past [[Levi's Stadium]], reportedly going over 100 mph.<ref> {{Cite web |last=Ostly |first=Ayrton |date=December 20, 2025 |title=Brandon Aiyuk video speeding stadium |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2025/12/20/brandon-aiyuk-video-speeding-49ers-stadium/87866119007/ |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=[[USA Today]]}} </ref> After this incident, Aiyuk apologized for his actions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Valdes |first=Alex |date=2025-12-29 |title=49ers’ Brandon Aiyuk apologizes after showing himself speeding in video |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6918239/2025/12/24/49ers-brandon-aiyuk-apology-driving-over-100-mph/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In June 2026, an arrest warrant was issued for the speeding incident.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arrest warrant issued for 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk for exhibition of speed |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brandon-aiyuk-arrest-warrant-issued-49ers-wr-exhibition-speed |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Brandon Dorlus''' (born March 22, 2001) is an  American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon Ducks]].

==Early life==
Dorlus originally attended [[Calvary Christian High School (Florida)|Calvary Christian High School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] before transferring to [[Deerfield Beach High School]] in [[Deerfield Beach, Florida]]. As a senior, he had 74 tackles, 11 sacks and an [[interception]] that he returned for a [[touchdown]]. He originally committed to [[Virginia Tech]] to play college football before changing to the [[University of Oregon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Furones |first=David |date=August 3, 2018 |title=Deerfield Beach DL Brandon Dorlus commits to Virginia Tech |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2018/08/02/deerfield-beach-dl-brandon-dorlus-commits-to-virginia-tech/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=Sun Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |date=December 19, 2018 |title=Deerfield Beach defensive lineman Brandon Dorlus signs with Oregon Ducks |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2018/12/19/deerfield-beach-defensive-lineman-brandon-dorlus-signs-with-oregon-ducks/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=Sun Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Dorlus played in nine games as a true freshman at Oregon in 2019, recording five tackles and one sack. '''Brandon Coleman''' (born October 12, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He grew up in [[Berlin]], Germany, moving back to the U.S. for high school prior to playing [[college football]] for the [[Trinity Valley Cardinals football|Trinity Valley Cardinals]] and [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]]. Coleman was selected by the Commanders in the third round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Coleman was born on October 12, 2000, in [[Newport News, Virginia]], to an American military serviceman and a German woman.<ref name="TheBeast">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2024 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2024/04/11162958/TheBeast2024_MasterFile-8.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240411212702/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2024/04/11162958/TheBeast2024_MasterFile-8.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2024 |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 14, 2024 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=118–119}}</ref><ref name="auto3">{{Cite news |last=Davison |first=Drew |date=September 19, 2019 |title=TCU's newest commit expects to compete for starting spot as soon as he gets on campus |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article235222987.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-05-25 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]}}</ref><ref name="German">{{Cite news |last=Davison |first=Drew |date=October 15, 2021 |title=He's fluent in German and paving the way for TCU's rushing attack. Meet Brandon Coleman |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article254984417.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-05-25 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]}}</ref> He spent his childhood in [[Berlin, Germany]], before returning to the United States in 2016 and enrolling at [[Denton High School]] in [[Denton, Texas]].<ref name="German"/> He played basketball as a [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] in Germany and first played [[American football]] in high school as a [[defensive lineman]] before playing on the [[offensive line]] as a [[Senior (education)|senior]].<ref name="German"/><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |last=Yates |first=Carter |date=August 14, 2023 |title=TCU's in a season of change, but Coker and Coleman's basketball rivalry is a constant |url=https://www.texasfootball.com/article/2023/08/14/coker-coleman-feature?ref=article_preview_title |access-date=2024-05-25 |website=[[Dave Campbell's Texas Football]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Coleman began his [[college football]] career with the Cardinals of [[Trinity Valley Community College]], appearing in seven games as a freshman in 2019.<ref name="German"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Coleman |url=https://www.tvccsports.com/sports/fball/2019-20/bios/coleman_brandon_eg7f |access-date=2024-05-25 |publisher=[[Trinity Valley Cardinals]]}}</ref> He was ranked a three-star [[junior college]] recruit and the eighth [[offensive tackle]] nationally by [[247Sports]], committing to play for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]] in 2020.<ref name="auto3"/>

Coleman played in the first four games of the 2020 season at TCU before his year ended due to injury.<ref name="German"/> He became a starter in 2021, finishing the season with 11 games played, eight as a starter.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |title=Brandon Coleman |url=https://gofrogs.com/sports/football/roster/brandon-coleman/15202 |access-date=2024-05-25 |publisher=[[TCU Horned Frogs]]}}</ref> He started all 15 games in 2022 and helped the team have one of the best offenses nationally while reaching the national championship, being named honorable mention [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12 Conference]].<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto2"/> Entering the 2023 season, Coleman's athletic ability was cited on ''[[The Athletic]]''{{'s}} annual "Freaks" list.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Lewis |first=Barry |date=August 18, 2023 |title=TCU Football: Three Players Selected To 2023 Freak List |url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/football/tcu-football-three-players-selected-2023-freak-list |access-date=2024-05-25 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He was selected team [[Captain (sports)|captain]] and started 11 games, being named second-team All-Big 12 and an honorable mention for conference lineman of the year while allowing only one [[Quarterback sack|sack]].<ref name="auto2"/> He played in the [[2024 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Gibbons |first=Brett |date=January 23, 2024 |title=Seven TCU Horned Frogs To Play In College Football All-Star Games |url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/football/tcu-horned-frogs-college-football-all-star-games-senior-bowl-east-west-shrine-2024 |access-date=2024-05-25 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref>

'''Brandon Codrington''' (born November 17, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] and [[return specialist]] for the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[North Carolina Central Eagles football|North Carolina Central Eagles]] and was signed by the [[New York Jets]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] after the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Codrington was born on November 17, 2000, in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Codrington Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CodrBr00.htm |access-date=2024-10-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He attended [[Broughton High School (North Carolina)|Broughton High School]] in North Carolina and was used on the football team as a [[return specialist]], totaling 320 kickoff return yards as a [[Senior (education)|senior]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Codrington's Broughton High School Football Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/nc/raleigh/broughton-capitals/athletes/brandon-condrington/football/stats/?careerid=bb25dfcpuah99 |access-date=2024-10-17 |publisher=[[MaxPreps]]}}</ref>
==College career==
Codrington, who was lightly recruited, [[Walk-on (sports)|walked-on]] at [[North Carolina Central University]] in 2019, as he had several family members who had attended the school.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Jalon |date=August 17, 2022 |title=Brandon Codrington, a NCCU walk-on who became an All-American |url=https://qcitymetro.com/2022/08/17/brandon-codrington-a-nccu-walk-on-who-became-an-all-american/ |access-date=2024-10-17 |publisher=QCityMetro}}</ref> In his first year with the football team, he was mainly used as a return specialist and averaged 18.8 yards per kickoff return and 7.8 yards per punt return.<ref name="auto" /> He was the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]] (MEAC) Specialist of the Week after returning a kickoff 75 yards for the game-winning [[touchdown]] against [[Delaware State Hornets football|Delaware State]] and ended the season ranked third in the conference in punt return average, being named third-team All-MEAC.<ref name="auto" /><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.blackenterprise.com/new-york-jets-sign-brandon-codrington/|publisher=[[Black Enterprise]]|title=New York Jets Sign HBCU Graduate, Brandon Codrington|date=May 10, 2024|author=Thorton, Cedric}}</ref> He also recorded eight [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] as a [[defensive back]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://nccueaglepride.com/sports/football/roster/brandon-codrington/8038|publisher=[[North Carolina Central Eagles]]|title=Brandon Codrington}}</ref>

Following the 2020 season being canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Codrington started the 2021 season with a game-sealing 77 yard punt return touchdown in the opener against [[Alcorn State Braves football|Alcorn State]].<ref name="auto" /> He was the third-leading punt returner at the [[NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision|NCAA Division I FCS]] level in the 2021 season, with an average of 15.0 yards that also placed first in the MEAC.<ref name="auto1"/> Codrington also was second in the MEAC with an average of 22.5 yards per kick return and made 43 tackles and four [[Pass deflected|pass breakups]] on defense.<ref name="auto1"/> He was named to [[Phil Steele]]'s All-MEAC team at four different positions, being a first-team All-MEAC punt returner, third-team All-MEAC kick returner, third-team All-MEAC all-purpose player, and fourth-team All-MEAC defensive back.<ref name="auto1"/> Codrington also earned selection to the BOXTOROW HBCU [[College Football All-America Team|All-America]] team at punt returner and was a one-time MEAC Specialist of the Week during the 2021 season.<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://meacsports.com/news/2021/12/14/nccus-codrington-named-to-boxtorow-hbcu-all-america-football-team.aspx|publisher=[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]]|title=NCCU’s Codrington Named to BOXTOROW HBCU All-America Football Team|date=December 14, 2021}}</ref>

Codrington was named third-team All-MEAC at return specialist in 2022, after recording averages of 19.3 yards per kick return and 6.8 yards per punt return.<ref name="auto2"/> In his senior year, 2023, he averaged 19.6 yards per punt return and 17.9 yards per kick return, scoring two punt return touchdowns.<ref name="auto1"/> He finished his collegiate career having started 41 games, totaling 93 tackles and 10 pass breakups on defense and 2,148 return yards and four return touchdowns on 130 total returns.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto2"/>

'''Brandon Cisse''' ([[Help:IPA/English|/siːseɪ/]] [[Help:Pronunciation respelling key|SEE-say]]; born July 3, 2005) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State Wolfpack]] and [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]] and was selected by the Packers in the second round of the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Cisse attended [[Lakewood High School (Sumter, South Carolina)|Lakewood High School]] in [[Sumter, South Carolina]], where he played both cornerback and [[wide receiver]]. As a senior, he had 37 tackles and one [[interception]] on defense and 42 receptions for 764 yards and eight [[touchdowns]] on offense. He committed to [[NC State University]] to play college football.<ref>{{cite web | last=Lucas | first=Isaiah | title=Lakewood DB Cisse officially joins North Carolina State | website=The Sumter Item | date=2022-12-21 | url=https://www.theitem.com/stories/lakewood-db-cisse-officially-joins-north-carolina-state,392617 | access-date=2026-04-28}}</ref>

==College career==
Cisse played at NC State in 2023 and 2024.<ref>[https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article297909798.html NC State secondary takes a hit after expected returner enters transfer portal]</ref> As a freshman he played in all 13 games and recorded 10 tackles and as a sophomore started all nine games he played in and had 28 tackles and one interception.<ref>[https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-football/article298147888.html Gamecocks add transfer corner from NC State who hails from Palmetto State]</ref><ref>[https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-football/article301496909.html Brandon Cisse signed with NC State’s collective. A month later, he transferred. What happened?]</ref> 

After the 2024 season, Cisse entered the [[transfer portal]] and transferred to the [[University of South Carolina]].<ref>[https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-football/article311503803.html NC State coach reflects on Brandon Cisse’s surprise transfer to South Carolina]</ref><ref>[https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/usc/2025/01/14/south-carolina-football-brandon-cisse-nc-state-cornerback-transfer-portal/77690635007/ South Carolina football, Shane Beamer land NC State transfer cornerback Brandon Cisse]</ref> He opened his first year at South Carolina in 2025 as a starter.<ref>[https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/carolina/gamecocks-brandon-cisse-cornerback-transfer-football-nc-state-sumter/article_f1dc468c-2ad3-4a4a-9e59-821c8e39ce4c.html New Gamecock transfer happy to be back home and ready to add to defensive tradition]</ref><ref>[https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-football/article311774703.html Brandon Cisse earns new nickname from Gamecocks thanks to speed, versatility]</ref> In 12 appearances for the team, Cisse recorded one interception, five pass deflections, one forced fumble, and 27 combined tackles. On December 11, 2025, Cisse declared for the [[2026 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=South Carolina. CB Brandon Cisse entering NFL draft|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/47276730/south-carolina-cb-brandon-cisse-entering-nfl-draft|access-date=December 30, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>
